categories.title: Decking

blocks.text: Decking. Decking is the wearing surface of the deck: the boards people walk on, and the only part of the structure exposed to sun, rain and foot traffic every single day.

Decking is more than just a feature of your outdoor living space; it's a statement of style, a testament to quality, and an extension of your home into the natural world. Choose from our amazing selection of tropical hardwoods and composite decking options, and build a well-crafted deck that adds value, aesthetic appeal, and extra space for relaxing or entertaining guests.

Upgrade your outdoor space with our exceptional decking options. From tropical hardwoods, domestic softwoods, composite, and thermally treated, we have the perfect solution for your project. Our decking materials are designed to withstand the elements while enhancing your home's aesthetics. Create a stylish and durable outdoor oasis that will be enjoyed for years. Discover our decking category and transform your space today!

Our range of tropical hardwood decking goes beyond mere aesthetics. Every board tells a unique story of resilience and longevity. With species such as Ipe Lumber, Garapa Lumber, Cumaru Lumber, Jatoba Lumber, and Tigerwood, we provide you with the charm of authentic tropical hardwood right at your doorstep.

We stock 189 products in this category, covering 26 milled sizes (1 x 10, 1 x 12, 1 x 2, 1 x 4, 1 x 6, 1 x 8, 2 x 10 and 2 x 12), 15 species (Thermo Ayous, Bamboo, Cumaru, Douglas Fir, Garapa and Ipe) and 10 brands (Armadillo, AZEK, Cali Bamboo, DeckoTech, DeckWise and MoistureShield). Everything ships from our own yards in Miami, Los Angeles and New Jersey, cut to length on request.

What sits in this category right now: Trex Composite Decking Transcend Collection (1x12), Ipe 5/4x6, Thermo Ayous Wood 1x6, Trex Composite Decking Transcend Collection (1x8), Trex Composite Decking Select Collection (2x6) and Ipe lumber 1X3. Stock moves, so ask the sales desk to confirm before you specify.
How to choose

items: Hardness. Janka hardness predicts how the surface survives furniture legs, dog claws and dropped tools. Anything above 1,600 lbf holds up to normal residential use; above 3,000 lbf is commercial territory.
Exposure. Full southern sun and salt air are the hardest conditions there are. Dense tropical hardwoods and capped composites handle them; softwoods need treatment and a maintenance schedule.

Movement. Wood moves with humidity, composite moves with temperature. That is why gapping rules differ: a hardwood gap is set by moisture content at install, a composite gap by the thermometer that morning.

blocks.text: The species side by side
Ipe is the hardest of the group at 3,680 lbf, which is what you want where the surface takes a beating. The softer species are easier to work and easier on the budget.
The brands we carry here

items: Armadillo: composite, a low-sheen, textured surface. Warranty: 25-year limited warranty.
AZEK: capped cellular PVC, contains no wood flour at all, so there is nothing in the board for mold to feed on. Warranty: 50-year limited warranty.
Cali Bamboo: fused bamboo, fused bamboo fiber with a Janka rating above most tropical hardwoods. Warranty: manufacturer warranty.
DeckoTech: co-extruded composite, a co-extruded shell over a dense wood-polymer core. Warranty: 25-year limited warranty.
DeckWise: hardwood installation hardware and finishes, the reference brand for hidden fasteners and oils in tropical hardwood decking. Warranty: manufacturer warranty.
MoistureShield: solid core composite, the only composite rated for direct ground and underwater contact. Warranty: 50-year structural warranty.
NewTechWood: capped composite, UltraShield capping on all four sides. Warranty: 25-year limited warranty.
TimberTech: capped composite and capped polymer, a four-sided cap seals the board against moisture. Warranty: 30-year limited fade and stain warranty.
Trex: wood-alternative composite, made from 95% reclaimed wood and plastic film. Warranty: 25-year limited residential fade and stain warranty.
Zuri: PVC with a photographic wear layer, a printed hardwood grain under a clear acrylic wear layer. Warranty: 25-year limited warranty.

blocks.text: Installation

Boards run perpendicular to joists spaced at 16 inches on center, or 12 inches for a diagonal layout. Every deck needs airflow underneath: a sealed, unventilated substructure is the single most common cause of premature failure, well ahead of the choice of board.

Stock moves, so ask the sales desk to confirm before you specify.
How to choose

items: Maintenance. Decide before you buy whether you will oil the deck once a year. If the answer is no, either accept a silver patina on hardwood, or choose a capped composite that never needs it.

Hardness. Janka hardness predicts how the surface survives furniture legs, dog claws and dropped tools. Anything above 1,600 lbf holds up to normal residential use; above 3,000 lbf is commercial territory.
Exposure. Full southern sun and salt air are the hardest conditions there are. Dense tropical hardwoods and capped composites handle them; softwoods need treatment and a maintenance schedule.

blocks.text: Installation

Boards run perpendicular to joists spaced at 16 inches on center, or 12 inches for a diagonal layout. Every deck needs airflow underneath: a sealed, unventilated substructure is the single most common cause of premature failure, well ahead of the choice of board.
Frequently asked questions
What warranty comes with Armadillo?
A 25-year limited warranty. Registration is handled by the manufacturer and we supply the proof of purchase.
How far apart should deck joists be?
Sixteen inches on center for a standard perpendicular layout, twelve inches for a diagonal pattern or for boards thinner than 1 inch. Stair treads and cantilevers need their own blocking.
What gap should I leave between deck boards?

About 3/16 of an inch for kiln dried tropical hardwood, which absorbs moisture and swells slightly after install. Composite and PVC follow the manufacturer chart, because the gap depends on the air temperature the day the boards go down.
What sizes do you stock?
Currently 1 x 6. We also mill to order, so ask if the size you need is not listed.
Do you deliver outside Florida, California and New Jersey?
Yes. The three yards cover the country by freight, and the order ships from whichever one is closest to the jobsite.

Sixteen inches on center for a standard perpendicular layout, twelve inches for a diagonal pattern or for boards thinner than 1 inch. Stair treads and cantilevers need their own blocking.

items: Maintenance. Decide before you buy whether you will oil the deck once a year. If the answer is no, either accept a silver patina on hardwood, or choose a capped composite that never needs it.

blocks.text: Flooring. Flooring is the interior surface: the one specified for how it looks, and judged on how it wears.

Welcome to Brazilian Lumber , where quality meets durability in the world of Hardwood Flooring. Our unique and diverse selection of wood flooring options are not only visually stunning but also environmentally responsible and long-lasting. Each one of our products offers a blend of beauty and strength that suits a broad spectrum of tastes and applications.

Upgrade your indoor spaces with our exceptional woods for flooring. From tropical hardwoods and thermally treated wood , we have the perfect solution for your project. Our different hardwoods are designed to be solid and durable while enhancing your home's aesthetics. Discover our flooring category and transform your indoor space today!

Our range of tropical hardwoods goes beyond mere aesthetics. Every board tells a unique story of resilience and longevity. With species such as Ipe Lumber, Garapa Lumber, Cumaru Lumber, Jatoba Lumber, and Tigerwood, we provide you with the charm of authentic tropical hardwood right at your doorstep.
We stock 1 product in this category. Everything ships from our own yards in Miami, Los Angeles and New Jersey, cut to length on request.

Choosing the right one

items: Solid or engineered. Solid boards can be sanded many times and suit a stable, dry interior. Engineered boards handle humidity swings and underfloor heating far better, and go over concrete.
Finish. Site finished floors give a seamless surface and let you match a color exactly. Prefinished floors go down faster and carry a wear warranty.

Acclimate the flooring inside the finished, conditioned space for at least 72 hours before installation, and check the subfloor moisture. Almost every flooring complaint traces back to one of those two steps being skipped.

items: Drying. A slab must be kiln dried to interior moisture content before it is worked. An air dried slab looks identical and will split after it is finished.

What to look at before you order

items: Stainless only. On tropical hardwood, use stainless steel. The tannins in dense hardwood corrode coated and galvanized fasteners, and the corrosion stains the board around every screw.

products.title: Piquia
specs: Kiln dried to 12-16% for exterior use

blocks.text: Piquia is a Piquia product. The species is light yellowish to grayish brown, rates 1,700 lbf Janka, and delivers 20+ years untreated.
Piquia is also known as White Iron Wood as the name implies is a light colored hardwood that is resistant to climate and wear. It is a yellowish or light grayish brown wood with interlocked grain.
Like other hardwoods, it is used for exterior constructions. Indoor applications such as countertops and tables are also common.
Piquia Origin: Central and South America (Brazil, Peru, Colombia, Costa Rica, Guyana, Venezuela)

Appearance: It is characterized by a yellowish to light grayish brown color. The texture is medium to coarse, and the grain is generally interlocked. It is very durable and resistant to decay fungi and dry-wood termites which makes it an ideal structure for exterior construction.
Why builders specify Piquia

items: Janka hardness of 1,700 lbf and 20+ years untreated outdoors with no chemical treatment.
Color: light yellowish to grayish brown.
Stocked in Miami, Los Angeles and New Jersey, with cut-to-length service and nationwide freight.

blocks.text: Installation notes

Pre-drill every fastener hole. At this density the board will split before a screw bites, so a counterbore and a stainless screw are not optional. Space boards 3/16 inch apart, keep the substructure ventilated, and seal cut ends immediately to stop end checking.
Care and maintenance

Piquia needs no sealer to survive. The only reason to oil it is color: one coat of a penetrating UV oil each spring keeps the light yellowish to grayish brown tone; skip it and the surface silvers evenly instead.
Frequently asked questions
How long will Piquia last outdoors?
20+ years untreated in a ventilated installation, with no chemical treatment. The limiting factor is almost never the board, it is the substructure underneath it.
Does Piquia need to be sealed?
Only the cut ends, and only to prevent checking. Surface oil is a cosmetic choice, not a structural one.
Can I get this cut to length?
Yes. We mill to order in house and can ship cut stock, which cuts jobsite waste and freight cost on long runs.

blocks.text: WiseWrap Deck Joist Flashing Tape - 3'' x 75' is part of the WiseWrap line of joist protection tape. It carries a manufacturer warranty and a butyl tape that seals the joist top against standing water.

WiseWrap Deck Joist Flashing Tape can be applied to decking joists, around deck support posts, and over ledger boards. DeckWise Joist Tape creates a waterproof seal that helps prevent decay and wood rot. DeckWise Joist Tape is a waterproof wood flashing that uses rubberized asphalt mastic adhesive.

When WiseWrap Deck Joist Flashing Tape is applied to the top of decking joists or over ledger boards, and around support posts, it creates a waterproof seal that helps stop decay and wood rot. Rot is caused by moisture that stays in contact with treated and untreated lumber deck framing and the above decking material.

Wood decay can also occur when deck screws penetrate the deck boards, piercing the joist sub-framing below. The application of WiseWrap JoistTape seals around decking screws to prevent the intrusion of moisture and water.

WiseWrap JoistTape rubberized asphalt adhesive is a self-sealer around deck screws that blocks a primary pathway for water infiltration into deck joists. When it blocks this moisture and prevents wood rot, the barrier tape will maximize the life of a brand new deck or restoration.
What you get with WiseWrap

items: WiseWrap construction: joist protection tape, a butyl tape that seals the joist top against standing water.
Backed by a manufacturer warranty.
No sanding, sealing or staining. Washing with soap and water is the full maintenance program.
Stocked in Miami, Los Angeles and New Jersey, with cut-to-length service and nationwide freight.

blocks.text: Installation notes

Install over joists at 16 inches on center, tightening to 12 inches for diagonal or stair applications. WiseWrap expands and contracts with temperature, so the gap at install has to be read off the manufacturer chart rather than set by eye.
Care and maintenance
Wash with warm water and a mild soap. Do not use a pressure washer above 1,500 psi, and keep the nozzle at least twelve inches from the surface.

blocks.text: Installation notes
Install over a ventilated, level substructure. Keep the material dry and stickered on site, and let it acclimate to local humidity before it is fastened down.
Care and maintenance
Wash with warm water and a mild soap. Do not use a pressure washer above 1,500 psi, and keep the nozzle at least twelve inches from the surface.
What to look at before you order

items: Hardness. Janka matters more indoors than outdoors, because dents show under interior light. Above 1,300 lbf handles a family home; below that, expect character.
Solid or engineered. Solid boards can be sanded many times and suit a stable, dry interior. Engineered boards handle humidity swings and underfloor heating far better, and go over concrete.
Finish. Site finished floors give a seamless surface and let you match a color exactly. Prefinished floors go down faster and carry a wear warranty.

blocks.text: Installation

Acclimate the flooring inside the finished, conditioned space for at least 72 hours before installation, and check the subfloor moisture. Almost every flooring complaint traces back to one of those two steps being skipped.
Frequently asked questions
Can I get this cut to length?
Yes. We mill to order in house and can ship cut stock, which cuts jobsite waste and freight cost on long runs.
Solid or engineered hardwood?
Engineered, if the floor sits over concrete, over underfloor heating, or in a humid climate. Solid, if you want a floor that can be sanded back several times over its life.
Can hardwood flooring go over concrete?
Engineered can, with the right moisture barrier. Solid hardwood generally cannot be fastened directly to a slab.

blocks.text: Ipe 1x4 gives you a 3/4" x 3-1/2" decking board in Ipe: deep olive-brown with fine, tight grain, 3,680 lbf Janka, and 50+ years untreated of service with no chemical treatment.

Ipe (pronounced ee-pay) is one of the densest hardwoods available for outdoor construction. Ipe 1x4 is very dense (in fact it sinks in water), it has the same fire rating as concrete and steel, and it is mildew and decay-resistant. Its denseness and natural oils make it virtually impenetrable to insects (so insect deterioration is not an issue). Ipe 1x4 does not scratch or splinter easily, it does not become hot in the sun, and has a high friction coefficient, making it perfect for outdoor and seaside construction.

blocks.text: This 1-1/2" x 5-1/2" dimensional lumber and stair tread stock is cut from Massaranduba. The wood is deep red that ages to a rich russet, rates 3,190 lbf on the Janka hardness scale, and is one of the densest South American hardwoods in commercial supply.

Massaranduba (pronounced Ma-sah- ran-due-bah) is one of the most beautiful hardwoods available for outdoor projects such as decking. Known as Brazilian Redwood it has a vivid reddish-brown color. Massaranduba 2x6 Standard is the hardwood of choice for people looking for a uniform look as the wood has very little movement. Like other hardwoods, Massaranduba 2x6 Standard is highly decay, insect, mold, and rot resistant. It is used in many outdoor projects such as stairs, decking, treads, and most curious of all billiard cues. Compared to ipe hardwood, it is a less expensive option.

Other Names: Brazilian Redwood Bulletwood, Red balata, Balata, Balata franc, Balata gomme, Balata rouge Maçaranduba, Acana, Aus, Ausabo, , Beefwood, Bolletri, Bolletrie, Chicozapota, Macaranduba, Maparajuba, Massarandu, Nispero, Pamashto, Paraju, Quinilla colorada,
Massaranduba Origin: Central and South America (Brazil, Colombia, Costa Rica, Guyana, Honduras, Jamaica, Mexico, Panama, Venezuela) and the Caribbean
Workability: Moderately easy to work with considering it is a hardwood. It machines and finishes to a very smooth surface. The timber takes a fine polish and has the appearance of walnut.

blocks.text: Installation notes

Plan for pre-drilling and for carbide tooling: this wood will dull standard steel blades quickly. Fasten with stainless steel only, hold a 3/16 inch gap between boards, and apply end grain sealer to every cut within the same working day.

Massaranduba needs no sealer to survive. The only reason to oil it is color: one coat of a penetrating UV oil each spring keeps the deep red that ages to a rich russet tone; skip it and the surface silvers evenly instead.

30+ years untreated in a ventilated installation, with no chemical treatment. The limiting factor is almost never the board, it is the substructure underneath it.

Only the cut ends, and only to prevent checking. Surface oil is a cosmetic choice, not a structural one.

blocks.text: Ipe Oil Hardwood Deck Finish 1 Gallon is milled from Ipe, a deep olive-brown with fine, tight grain. It rates 3,680 lbf on the Janka scale and is Class A fire rating, the same rating as concrete and steel.

IPE OIL HARDWOOD DECK FINISH is an oil-based natural wood finish and protectant. Enhance the beauty of your hardwood deck and protect it from damaging sun UV, harsh , toxic mold and mildew at the same time. IPE OIL HARDWOOD DECK FINISH is specifically formulated to protect as well as preserve the natural beauty of exterior hardwood decks. This finish is not just for use on deck boards; it penetrates into the densest hardwood fences and wood railings as well.

IPE OIL HARDWOOD DECK FINISH works with all Brazilian hardwoods and American hardwood products. Deckwise does not recommend use with soft woods. The exception to that is Cedar decking. DeckWise Ipe Oil is compatible with softwood Cedar, however it may require more than one coat. Ipe Oil is not for use with yellow pine.

DeckWise Ipe Oil is a low-odor low VOC formula comes in a natural transparent tone to enhance the appearance of any hardwood species, and the Ipe Oil Hardwood Deck Finish formula contains Transoxide pigments which provide added grain enhancement. Ipe Oil is easy-to-use with three simple steps: 1. Clean and Brighten the deck surface and let dry 2. Apply Ipe Oil Hardwood deck finish 3. Wipe any excess Ipe Oil

It is recommended to sand new wood decking with 80-120 grit sandpaper prior to allying Ipe Oil™ Hardwood Finish to open the wood's pores and allow natural oils to come to the surface. Always clean older gray or dirty wood decking before applying Ipe Oil™ Hardwood Finish. Use a product like DeckWise® Part 1 Wood Cleaner and DeckWise Part 2 Wood Brightener to clean hardwood decks. Then, allow wood decking to completely dry for at least 24 to 48 hours. Previously stained or treated wood should be sufficiently weathered to allow for complete penetration of Ipe Oil™ Hardwood Finish. New wood should be aged at least 6-8 weeks and cleaned before applying product.

blocks.text: Cedar Wood is milled from Western Red Cedar, a reddish brown with pale sapwood. It rates 350 lbf on the Janka scale and is naturally rot resistant, light, and easy to work.

Cedar is a softwood that has the advantage of being very stable. It is not very permeable to liquids and has natural phenol that preserves it from moisture, decay, and insect damage. Another great trait of Cedar Wood is that it is not prone to expansion, even with temperature changes, twisting, cupping, or cracking.

Drying : The drying method depends on the size of the wood. Any wood that is 1" in width (such as that used for siding) will be kiln-dried. Any lumber over 2" wide will be air-dried. Pecky Cypress can be bought air-dried or kiln-dried. It requires 6 months of air drying before being kiln-dried. It is essential not to over-dry cypress in the ovens because the outside will dry easily, and the interior will be moisture which causes faster cracking.

Sustainable : Pine overgrows and is thus a very sustainable option. The Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora ( CITES ) does not list Cedar in its appendices. The International Union for Conservation of Nature's Red List of Threatened Species ( IUCN ) list Cedar as a species of least concern.

blocks.text: This 1-1/2" x 9-1/4" structural joist stock is cut from Ipe. The wood is deep olive-brown with fine, tight grain, rates 3,680 lbf on the Janka hardness scale, and is Class A fire rating, the same rating as concrete and steel.

Ipe (pronounced ee-pay) is one of the densest hardwoods available for outdoor construction. Ipe 2x10 is very dense (in fact it sinks in water), it has the same fire rating as concrete and steel, and it is mildew and decay-resistant. Its denseness and natural oils make it virtually impenetrable to insects (so insect deterioration is not an issue). Ipe 2x10 does not scratch or splinter easily, it does not become hot in the sun, and has a high friction coefficient, making it perfect for outdoor and seaside construction.

Other Names: Brazilian Walnut, Lapacho, Iron Wood, Amapa, Cortez, Guayacan polvillo, Flor Amarillo, Greenheart, Madera negra, Tahuari, Lapacho negro, Pau D ́arco, Canaguate, Polvillo, Hakia, Tahuari Negro, Groenhart, Acapro Puy, Yellow poui
Ipe Origin: Central and South America (Brazil, Peru, Paraguay, Argentina, Colombia, Costa Rica, Guyana, Honduras, Jamaica, Mexico, Panama, Venezuela)
Appearance: The color of ipe 2x10 is similar to walnut with dark tones that have olive brown to reddish undertones. If left untreated it will gradually turn to a beautiful natural silver patina.

Dense tropical hardwood has to be pre-drilled and counterbored before fastening; a screw driven straight into it will snap or split the board. Use stainless steel fasteners, leave a 3/16 inch gap between boards for airflow, and seal every fresh cut end with an end grain sealer the same day it is cut.

Ipe needs no sealer to survive. The only reason to oil it is color: one coat of a penetrating UV oil each spring keeps the deep olive-brown tone; skip it and the surface silvers evenly instead.

blocks.text: Ipe 4X8 is milled from Ipe, a deep olive-brown with fine, tight grain. It rates 3,680 lbf on the Janka scale and is Class A fire rating, the same rating as concrete and steel.

Ipe Lumber 4X8 (pronounced ee-pay) is one of the densest hardwoods available for outdoor construction. Ipe Lumber 4X8 is very dense (in fact, it sinks in water), has the same fire rating as concrete and steel, and is mildew and decay-resistant.

Its denseness and natural oils make it virtually impenetrable to insects (so insect deterioration is not an issue). Ipe does not scratch or splinter easily, does not become hot in the sun, and has a high friction coefficient, making it perfect for outdoor and seaside construction.

Other Names: Brazilian Walnut, Lapacho, Iron Wood, Amapa, Cortez, Guayacan polvillo, Flor Amarillo, Greenheart, Madera negra, Tahuari, Lapacho negro, Pau D ́arco, Canaguate, Polvillo, Hakia, Tahuari Negro, Groenhart, Acapro Puy, Yellow poui.
Ipe Origin: Central and South America (Brazil, Peru, Paraguay, Argentina, Colombia, Costa Rica, Guyana, Honduras, Jamaica, Mexico, Panama, Venezuela).

each linear foot covers 0.62 square feet with a 3/16 inch gap, so 100 square feet of deck takes about 161 linear feet. blocks.text: Installation notes

Dense tropical hardwood has to be pre-drilled and counterbored before fastening; a screw driven straight into it will snap or split the board. Use stainless steel fasteners, leave a 3/16 inch gap between boards for airflow, and seal every fresh cut end with an end grain sealer the same day it is cut.
Care and maintenance

Left alone, Ipe fades to a soft silver patina without losing an ounce of structural strength. If you want to hold the deep olive-brown tone, clean the deck and re-apply a penetrating hardwood oil once a year, twice in full southern sun.

How long will Ipe last outdoors?
50+ years untreated in a ventilated installation, with no chemical treatment. The limiting factor is almost never the board, it is the substructure underneath it.
Does Ipe need to be sealed?
Only the cut ends, and only to prevent checking. Surface oil is a cosmetic choice, not a structural one.
What is the actual size of a 4 x 8?
None. Nominal sizes describe the rough sawn dimension before milling, so the finished board always measures less.

blocks.text: DeckWise Hardwood Wrench is part of the DeckWise line of hardwood installation hardware and finishes. It carries a manufacturer warranty and the reference brand for hidden fasteners and oils in tropical hardwood decking.

We hear it always: "I wish I had THAT last week!" It never gets old to see the amazement and delight builders have when they first see the DeckWise Hardwood Wrench in action. They grab it and raise it upward in the air as if it were a Knight's sword. They sense its hefty toughness and straight away want to use it on a project. It's thrilling to observe!

Why the excitement when builders grasp our hardwood board straightening tool? In reality, bending warped hardwood boards into place is done with a chisel. This is the primary method in the building industry. It's a practice that gets handed down from builder to builder and generation to generation. It's not wrong per se, just more of an old-school method.
When hardwood installers consider how back-breaking it is to battle unwieldy hardwood boards, they appreciate the ease of use our Hardwood Wrench™ offers them.

Besides, when installers see our wrench also includes a locking cam which permits them to let go of the wrench handle while installing fasteners, they immediately know they won't need a knee propped up to hold the tool from slipping. They understand the Hardwood Wrench™ stays in place and will not pop off the board, as other wrenches often do.

items: Stainless only. On tropical hardwood, use stainless steel. The tannins in dense hardwood corrode coated and galvanized fasteners, and the corrosion stains the board around every screw.

blocks.text: Installation notes
Install over a ventilated, level substructure. Keep the material dry and stickered on site, and let it acclimate to local humidity before it is fastened down.
Care and maintenance
Wash with warm water and a mild soap. Do not use a pressure washer above 1,500 psi, and keep the nozzle at least twelve inches from the surface.
What to look at before you order

items: Hardness. Janka hardness predicts how the surface survives furniture legs, dog claws and dropped tools. Anything above 1,600 lbf holds up to normal residential use; above 3,000 lbf is commercial territory.
Exposure. Full southern sun and salt air are the hardest conditions there are. Dense tropical hardwoods and capped composites handle them; softwoods need treatment and a maintenance schedule.

Movement. Wood moves with humidity, composite moves with temperature. That is why gapping rules differ: a hardwood gap is set by moisture content at install, a composite gap by the thermometer that morning.
Maintenance. Decide before you buy whether you will oil the deck once a year. If the answer is no, either accept a silver patina on hardwood, or choose a capped composite that never needs it.

blocks.text: Installation

Boards run perpendicular to joists spaced at 16 inches on center, or 12 inches for a diagonal layout. Every deck needs airflow underneath: a sealed, unventilated substructure is the single most common cause of premature failure, well ahead of the choice of board.
Frequently asked questions
Can I get this cut to length?
Yes. We mill to order in house and can ship cut stock, which cuts jobsite waste and freight cost on long runs.
How far apart should deck joists be?
Sixteen inches on center for a standard perpendicular layout, twelve inches for a diagonal pattern or for boards thinner than 1 inch. Stair treads and cantilevers need their own blocking.
What gap should I leave between deck boards?

About 3/16 of an inch for kiln dried tropical hardwood, which absorbs moisture and swells slightly after install. Composite and PVC follow the manufacturer chart, because the gap depends on the air temperature the day the boards go down.

blocks.text: This 1-1/2" x 3-1/2" dimensional lumber is cut from Cumaru. The wood is warm golden to reddish brown with interlocked grain, rates 3,540 lbf on the Janka hardness scale, and is often specified as a lower-cost alternative to Ipe with nearly identical hardness.

Cumaru (pronounced Ku-mah-rue), also known as Brazilian Teak, is one of the densest hardwoods available for outdoor construction, second only to ipe . It is very dense, which is why it is ideal for exterior use, as it is mildew and decay-resistant. It is often used for decking, flooring, railroad ties, and other purposes. Just like Ipe, Cumaru has an A1 fire rating, does not scratch or splinter easily, does not become hot in the sun, and has a high friction coefficient. All these characteristics make it perfect for outdoor and seaside construction.

Other Names: Almendrillo, Amburana, Brazilian Teak, Cumaru Rosa, Imburana de Cheiro, Tonka, Tonka Bean, Tonquin Bean cumaru decking for building, kumaru, Gaiac de Cayenne, Amendrillo, ebo, Shihuahuaco Amarillo, Charapilla, Sarrapia.
Cumaru Origin: Central and South America (Brazil, Colombia, Peru, Bolivia, Costa Rica, Guyana, Honduras, Jamaica, Mexico, Panama, Venezuela).

Appearance: Cumaru hardwood is a deep reddish brown with a tight, even grain. Over time the red Cumaru color will slightly fade to a light brown. The species has an irregular, slightly interlocked grain and is coarse and wavy in texture.

blocks.text: Installation notes

Dense tropical hardwood has to be pre-drilled and counterbored before fastening; a screw driven straight into it will snap or split the board. Use stainless steel fasteners, leave a 3/16 inch gap between boards for airflow, and seal every fresh cut end with an end grain sealer the same day it is cut.
Care and maintenance
Ipe needs no sealer to survive. The only reason to oil it is color: one coat of a penetrating UV oil each spring keeps the deep olive-brown tone; skip it and the surface silvers evenly instead.
Frequently asked questions
How long will Ipe last outdoors?
50+ years untreated in a ventilated installation, with no chemical treatment. The limiting factor is almost never the board, it is the substructure underneath it.
Does Ipe need to be sealed?
Only the cut ends, and only to prevent checking. Surface oil is a cosmetic choice, not a structural one.
What is the actual size of a 1 x 2?
None. Nominal sizes describe the rough sawn dimension before milling, so the finished board always measures less.
Can I get this cut to length?
Yes. We mill to order in house and can ship cut stock, which cuts jobsite waste and freight cost on long runs.

Install over a ventilated, level substructure. Keep the material dry and stickered on site, and let it acclimate to local humidity before it is fastened down.
Care and maintenance
Wash with warm water and a mild soap. Do not use a pressure washer above 1,500 psi, and keep the nozzle at least twelve inches from the surface.
What to look at before you order

items: Hardness. Janka hardness predicts how the surface survives furniture legs, dog claws and dropped tools. Anything above 1,600 lbf holds up to normal residential use; above 3,000 lbf is commercial territory.
Exposure. Full southern sun and salt air are the hardest conditions there are. Dense tropical hardwoods and capped composites handle them; softwoods need treatment and a maintenance schedule.

Movement. Wood moves with humidity, composite moves with temperature. That is why gapping rules differ: a hardwood gap is set by moisture content at install, a composite gap by the thermometer that morning.
Maintenance. Decide before you buy whether you will oil the deck once a year. If the answer is no, either accept a silver patina on hardwood, or choose a capped composite that never needs it.

blocks.text: Installation

Boards run perpendicular to joists spaced at 16 inches on center, or 12 inches for a diagonal layout. Every deck needs airflow underneath: a sealed, unventilated substructure is the single most common cause of premature failure, well ahead of the choice of board.
Frequently asked questions
What is the actual size of a 1 x 6?
3/4" x 5-1/2". Nominal sizes describe the rough sawn dimension before milling, so the finished board always measures less.
Can I get this cut to length?
Yes. We mill to order in house and can ship cut stock, which cuts jobsite waste and freight cost on long runs.

Install over a ventilated, level substructure. Keep the material dry and stickered on site, and let it acclimate to local humidity before it is fastened down.
Care and maintenance
Wash with warm water and a mild soap. Do not use a pressure washer above 1,500 psi, and keep the nozzle at least twelve inches from the surface.
What to look at before you order

items: Profile. Shiplap and tongue and groove shed water by geometry; open joint profiles rely on the membrane behind them. Choose the profile before the species, because it decides the whole detail.
Ventilation. A cladding system needs a drained and ventilated cavity behind it. Boards fixed flat to sheathing will trap moisture and fail early, whatever the material.
Fixing. Face fixing is faster and cheaper; concealed fixing is what makes a facade look designed. Decide early, because it changes the profile.
Orientation. Vertical boards drain faster, horizontal boards read wider. Both work, but the flashing detail is different.

blocks.text: Installation

Fix over battens to create a ventilated cavity of at least 3/4 of an inch, with insect mesh top and bottom. Seal every cut end the same day, and keep fasteners stainless: a corroding fastener stains the facade long before it fails.

Does wood cladding need a ventilated cavity?
Yes. A drained and back-ventilated cavity of at least 3/4 of an inch is what lets the board dry from both faces. Without it the board cups and the coating fails.
Can I use decking boards as cladding?
Sometimes, but not automatically. Cladding profiles are thinner and lighter, and they are milled to shed water in a vertical plane. Ask before you substitute.

Exposure. Full southern sun and salt air are the hardest conditions there are. Dense tropical hardwoods and capped composites handle them; softwoods need treatment and a maintenance schedule.

Movement. Wood moves with humidity, composite moves with temperature. That is why gapping rules differ: a hardwood gap is set by moisture content at install, a composite gap by the thermometer that morning.
Maintenance. Decide before you buy whether you will oil the deck once a year. If the answer is no, either accept a silver patina on hardwood, or choose a capped composite that never needs it.

blocks.text: This 3/4" x 7-1/4" decking and cladding board is cut from Cumaru. The wood is warm golden to reddish brown with interlocked grain, rates 3,540 lbf on the Janka hardness scale, and is often specified as a lower-cost alternative to Ipe with nearly identical hardness.

Cumaru Hardwood (pronounced Ku-mah-rue), also known as Brazilian Teak, is one of the densest hardwoods available for outdoor construction, second only to ipe . It is very dense, which is why it is ideal for exterior use, as it is mildew and decay-resistant. It is often used for decking, flooring, railroad ties, and other purposes. Just like ipe, cumaru has an A1 fire rating, does not scratch or splinter easily, does not become hot in the sun, and has a high friction coefficient, making it perfect for outdoor and seaside construction.

Other Names: Almendrillo, Amburana, Brazilian Teak, Cumaru Rosa, Imburana de Cheiro, Tonka, Tonka Bean, Tonquin Bean cumaru decking for building, kumaru, Gaiac de Cayenne, Amendrillo, ebo, Shihuahuaco Amarillo, Charapilla, Sarrapia
Cumaru Origin: Central and South America (Brazil, Colombia, Peru, Bolivia, Costa Rica, Guyana, Honduras, Jamaica, Mexico, Panama, Venezuela)

Appearance: Cumaru hardwood is a deep reddish brown color with a tight, even grain. Over time, the red cumaru color will fade slightly to a light brown. The species has an irregular, slightly interlocked grain and coarse and wavy texture.

blocks.text: Ipe 1x10 is milled from Ipe, a deep olive-brown with fine, tight grain. It rates 3,680 lbf on the Janka scale and is Class A fire rating, the same rating as concrete and steel.

Ipe (pronounced ee-pay) is one of the densest hardwoods available for outdoor construction. Ipe 1x10 is very dense (in fact it sinks in water), it has the same fire rating as concrete and steel, and it is mildew and decay-resistant. Its denseness and natural oils make it virtually impenetrable to insects (so insect deterioration is not an issue). Ipe 1x10 does not scratch or splinter easily, it does not become hot in the sun, and has a high friction coefficient, making it perfect for outdoor and seaside construction.

posts.title: Five Reasons Ipe is the Best Decking Material
posts.h1: Five Reasons Ipe is the Best Decking Material

blocks.text: Even though wood is not the only material used for decking, it is the most popular choice. There is a wide choice of lumber that can be used for deck building, depending on the weather conditions of where you live, how large a deck you want to build, and what your budget for the project is. However, if you are looking for the best wood for deck building there is only one choice: IPE . Ipe or Brazilian walnut as it is sometimes called is the hardest tropical wood. It is used to make decks, siding, docks, and any other outdoor structure. Here are the top reasons why it is the best choice for deck building:
1. Lasts for Over 50 Years

Ipe, or Ipê, ( Pronunciation: Eee-pay) has been used in commercial boardwalks and decks that were installed more than 50 years ago - a testament to its longevity. Because of its density (it sinks in water) ipe can withstand all types of threats such as extreme weather, sunshine and thanks to its high tannic acid content, it will not rot, mold, mildew, or be affected by insects. Ipe comes from the Amazon Rain Forest where it is constantly exposed to heavy rainfall and insects, so it has adapted over the years to become resistant to all those threats.

The longevity of ipe is one of the reasons so many architects and designers choose ipe. As a long-lasting material, it will not need to be replaced. Also, ipe is naturally dense and resistant, which means that unlike softwoods or domestic wood, it does not need to be chemically treated in order to be preserved. Ipe can be bought with chain of custody certification or The Forest Stewardship Council ( FSC ) certification to guarantee that the trees were responsibly sourced and harvested . If you check out the CITES Appendices (the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora) , you will see that ipe is not on the list, nor is it listed by the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species.
3. Increases your home's value

An ipe deck will add extra space to a home and is an element of architectural interest that will increase the curb appeal of a home. It will help extend the living area outside, creating an outdoor area for relaxation or entertainment. Ipe decks are found in all mayor luxury resorts from the Maldives to the Turks and Caicos, any high-end beach resort will use ipe hardwood for its decks and boardwalks. Any world traveler will instantly recognize an ipe deck, which will give your home an immediate tone of wealth. High end guests who see ipe decks associate it with luxury and opulence.
4. Safe Against Weather Exposure

Safety is important when it comes to decking materials because they are more exposed to the elements than indoor items. Ipe wood the same fire rating as concrete or steel, which makes it a very safe in case of a grilling or smoking accident. Also, Ipe wood does not crack or splinters over the years, which means it is safe for bare feet to walk on. Another great feature, especially for feet, is that unlike PVC or Composite Decking, ipe wood does not absorb the sun's heat and so it will not scald bare feet.
5. Comes in all different lengths and sizes

If you buy Composite Decking or PVC you will only be able to work with certain board lengths. With ipe wood, you have a choice of board length, width, and thickness. Many carpenters and deck installers complain that they are limited when they have to work with composite decking because it does not generally cut well or can lose its guarantee if cut. Different facia boards have to be purchased. By contrast, ipe comes in all sizes imaginable, and can be milled to any specifications.
Quite simply, Brazilian ipe look is the best type of wood for decking. Considering both the building qualities of the wood and the prestige it gives to any space, it is a choice product.

posts.title: The 3 Most Recommended Decking Materials That You Should Use

blocks.text: Grand-Hyatt-Baha-Mar (photo)
Choosing a decking material is perhaps the most important decision you will make when building a new deck. There are many types of materials that can meet your needs.
Each decking material option has its own unique aesthetic, maintenance requirements, and other significant aspects to consider when making a choice.
Just a few years ago, wood was the only option out there. Today there are dozens of different materials, such as composite wood , plastic decking, PVC decking, domestic and imported hardwood .

So before you make any decisions, it is important to familiarize yourself with the different decking materials available, the different types of decking materials installation techniques, the price point of each, as well as the future maintenance and care required of each.
Here is a list of the top three (3) decking materials, along with their benefits, aesthetic features, and maintenance requirements, according to our team of experts here at Brazilian Lumber .

items: Hardwoods
Composite Decking
PVC Decking

blocks.text: Decking Materials: Hardwoods

Although wood is not the only material used for decking, it is the most popular choice. Its quality and style set it apart from other decking materials. Both domestic and tropical woods can be used for decking.
However, tropical hardwoods are ideal given that they are long-lasting thanks to their dense composition, resistant to insect damage and rot, and weather resistance.
Additionally, hardwood has the advantage of having a fire rating equal to steel and concrete. This means it is fire-resistant, adding an extra layer of protection to the exterior of your house.
Also, hardwood decking materials offersnot only remarkable durability, but also aesthetic warmth for any type of environment.

The most commonly used hardwoods for exterior constructions are: Garapa , Cumaru , Jatoba , Tigerwood , and Ipe . The last mentioned is the most demanded premium wood nowadays. Its high-quality, natural oil, and extraordinary features make it one of a kind.

Nevertheless, any of the other lumber types mentioned above are also nice types of wood. These deeply grained woods are extremely hard, very durable, naturally resistant to mold, weather, and insect damage.

In fact, these decking materials are so dense that it is virtually impossible to screw them into a panel without first drilling a hole. For this reason, it is recommended that decking boards be pre-drilled.

As explained above, Ipe deserves a special mention. This amazing lumber, sometimes called Brazilian Walnut, comes from South America and is the hardest tropical wood. That is how it earns its nickname iron wood.

Decks, docks, pergolas, siding, cladding, boardwalks, as well as interior flooring are made of it. But what makes IPE truly remarkable and the perfect decking material is its durability, quality, and weather resistance.
Although Ipe stands out as the best wood, all of the above have exceptional properties, such as:

items: Natural, renewable, recyclable, and biodegradable building material
Carbon positive element
Adaptable, versatile, and durable material
Sound absorbing decking material
Scratch and splinter resistant
Cool in the sun
Mold, mildew, and termite resistant
Fire repellant / retardant
High friction coefficient (slip resistant)

blocks.text: Decking Materials: Composite
Composite decking material is one of the fastest growing materials available today.
It is made primarily from recycled wood fiber and plastics. That's why most people consider it a very environmentally friendly option.
This is a material that does not warp or splinter. In addition, it is not affected by rot or insects, making it a truly durable option, which does not require a lot of maintenance.

Composite decking does not require sanding or finishing. For proper maintenance, a thorough cleaning with water and soap is enough. By following this advice, you will preserve the high quality of the material for about 25 years. The actual guarantee period will depend on each manufacturer.

Although there is a fear that composite decking may not be as nice and organic-looking as natural wood, thanks to modern technology, that is no longer an issue. Another nice option of using composite decking materials is that there is a far greater variety of colors to choose from.
Also, most boards are similar to each other, something that with a natural product such as wood cannot be guaranteed.
This amazing material gives you superior durability, ultra-low maintenance, resistance to external factors, and it is a cost-efficient material.

At Brazilian Lumber we are authorized distributors of brands that offer high standards of quality, good service, and good design. The following is a list of some of the most popular composite decking material brands we offer:

items: Trex
TimberTech
Newtech Wood
Norx
Azek
For Us Plastic Wood

blocks.text: All of these brands offer a variety of color and aesthetic options, warranties, different types of protective capping, and a decking material that does not weather, splinter, or warp.
Decking Materials: PVC Decking
An alternative to both hardwood and composite decking materials is PVC.
Both PVC and composite decking are equally fade-resistant based on the quality and brand. PVC decking is more synthetic in appearance, while composite decking better resembles natural wood.
PVC (polyvinyl chloride) cover, also known as plastic decking material, is composed of 100% plastic; there are no wood fibers.
It is known as the cousin of composite, as they share many properties. For example, both are extremely weather resistant, easy to clean, and will not splinter, warp or rot.
They are available in different colors and have a wooden structure that really takes on the appearance of natural wood.

Not everything is the same, there are also differences. PVC decking is much lighter than composite decking, which makes it easier to move and lay. This material comes in many quality grades, but almost all of them are quite strong.

In fact, high-quality PVC decking has almost none of the weaknesses of wood. This means you don't have to worry about sanding or staining plastics, making this decking material almost maintenance-free.
Aesthetically, PVC decking offers more options than ordinary wood. You can find brown, gray, white, tan, or even patterns that resemble wood grain.
At Brazilian Lumber we are also authorized distributors of brands that offer PVC alternatives, such as:

items: Endeck
Zuri
Azek

blocks.text: All of them share high quality components and the best technological procedures in their products. In addition, a wide variety of colors and designs that will enhance your spaces with these durable and low-maintenance decking material alternatives.
To conclude, building a deck can be a hard experience if you have no idea of which are the best decking material options for it. To avoid that, better to have the best ally by your side.
CALL US, and we will make your dream project a reality in an easy, simple, and satisfying way.

blocks.text: There are two things The Caribbean is known for: its paradises and its intense heat. This last fact is the reason why some luxury hotels on these tropical islands are looking for ways to control high temperatures to provide comfortable surfaces to their guests. With Ipe they have found the solution.
Ipe wood is your best bet, not only because of its superior strength, high durability, and natural beauty, but also because it doesn't get hot underfoot. That makes it the best choice.

There is no doubt that there's nothing worse than stepping out onto your patio in mid-July only to find a scorching surface. With Ipe that is not an issue. Here at Brazilian Lumber , we have it in all dimensions and board lengths to meet your needs.

Therefore, it is important to choose a decking material that will stay cool in the summer months, especially if you live in a warmer climate or if your deck is exposed to full sunlight. The following explains how high temperatures affect wooden elements.

Under the sun, the surface of your deck will heat up more due to the amount of solar or thermal energy absorbed versus the amount reflected. The darker the color of the surface, the more heat is absorbed and the warmer it gets.
Having a decking that is uncomfortable for your feet can be quite annoying. Nobody wants to walk on hot decking while using the pool. So do not take this recommendation for granted.
Obviously, with Ipe wood there is no need to worry about that. In fact, many issues are solved with this remarkable hardwood. We are glad to share with you a list with its most important features.

items: Salt water-resistant
Free of chemical pollution
Heat absorbing power
Luxurious material
Long-lasting wood

blocks.text: 1. Ipe Is Salt Water-Resistant
The Cove Eleuthera Bahamas Resort

One of the things that most affects wood is salt water, so finding a high quality wood resistance to it is wonderful. Ipe is naturally resistant to salt water and moisture, so pretty much nothing can damage it.

No other species of wood can withstand the constant exposure to the sea like Ipe does without deteriorating. This is because it is a type of lumber that grows in the rainforest, where it already deals with harsh weather conditions and insect attacks.
2. Ipe Is Free Of Chemical Pollution

The Caribbean Islands must protect their most valuable resources. Their beautiful and natural paradises attract tourists from all over the world. So, in order to preserve them, it is important to build with ecological materials.

Ipe wood is completely natural and does not require any chemical treatment or corrosive process of sanding. This means that Ipe does not emit harmful chemicals into the air or ocean, and does not become plastic waste after its useful life.

In addition, this hardwood does not intoxicate animals that are part of the natural habitat. The only animals that will not like this wood are termites and fungus, as Ipe is impermeable to those insects.
3. Ipe Does Not Get Hot Underfoot
The Modern Honolulu in Honolulu

One of the reasons why Ipe wood is so popular in the Caribbean is that it does not heat up in the sun. The Caribbean is synonymous with hot and sunny weather. If you are not careful, you can end up burning your feet when picking the wrong material to build your new deck.
Ipe wood keeps its surface cool due to its characteristic of absorbing less heat than other materials. Other decking choices cannot claim this feature, as they contain plastic or metal.

The Caribbean Islands are the preferred choice for vacation. Their natural environment is not the only thing that attracts tourists, but the stunning resorts that enhance their luxury and beauty with wooden elements.

In addition to the beautiful views and secluded locations, guests are looking for five-star places when visiting the Caribbean. Due to its prestige and its exclusivity, Ipe hardwood offers the perfect building material for a luxury resort.
Ipe wood is a premium product not only because of its high quality, but also because of its beautiful color. It has a rich chocolate brown when it is first installed or it can turn silver overtime.

When it comes about guests, safety and comfort are also important. This is a big deal for all resorts, but mostly for luxurious hotels that have demanding guests. Only ipe can offer the required level of safety, such as accidents when walking barefoot. Its surface is always intact.

Another fact that makes Ipe so irresistible is its hardness, key for heavily traveled vacation destinations. There are many high traffic places where Ipe is the protagonist, such as the Atlantic City Boardwalk and also at Disney World. Still doubts about its toughness?
5. Ipe Is A Long Term Investment
Ipe is a long-lasting material that requires almost no maintenance. These two factors make it a good investment that you will enjoy for more than 50 years.
This does not mean that you have to leave your deck unattended. We recommend regular cleaning as well as occasional oiling if you are looking to preserve its color.
Now, for a proper maintenance, we share with you three simple recommendations:

items: Sweep it daily to remove dirt, pollen, and leaves
Wash it and let it dry well for at least 24 hours
Then oil it with proper products like the ones we sell here at Brazilian Lumber

blocks.text: Ipe is guaranteed to last due to its resistance to mold, mildew, and insect damage. Also, it has an A-1 fire rating, making it as strong as concrete.
As it does not splinter, it is not a risky material to install in places where many bare feet pass through. In addition, its coefficient of friction makes it extremely non-slip even when it gets wet.

These features make Ipe be the preferred choice of many Caribbean hotels such as Sandals , The cove Eleuthera - Bahamas Resort , Warwick-Paradise , The Modern Honolulu in Honolulu , SLS Baha Mar 3 , and Sandals Royal Caribbean .
Because having such durable, high-quality, saltwater-resistant hardwood is practically everything a hotel near the ocean needs.

To conclude, if you are looking for a durable, high quality wood, that does not get hot underfoot, and is naturally resistant to mold, weathering, and insect damage, Ipe is the one. Don't waste your time with different options.

blocks.text: When choosing the right wood for decking, you should not settle for just any type of wood. There are some good alternatives that will surely meet your needs, but there is one that has a captivating color, its name is Massaranduba.
This stunning hardwood, also known as Bulletwood or Brazilian Redwood, has a nice finish and polishes to a high luster that many customers appreciate.
Where do you start? Massaranduba wood is exactly what you need to keep your deck looking new for many years. This hardwood is known for its excellent properties and features. Want to learn more?
Have you heard about the incredible strength, durability, and longevity of Ipe? Massaranduba shares many similarities with Ipe , so in some cases they are used interchangeably.

Being one of the hardest woods in existence, Massaranduba also has impressive durability and longevity. It is naturally resistant to insect attack, mold, rot, and fire. Because of its fine texture, this wood also offers great slip resistance.

When you build a deck with Massaranduba wood, you have a very versatile material, perfect for commercial projects with high traffic areas. Besides that, it is its beauty, hardness, and low maintenance that makes it a leading option for residential constructions as well.

The deep red color of this amazing hardwood, which makes it attractive, can be maintained with regular use of oil. Without this maintenance advice, it can be assumed that the wood will turn silver when exposed to the weather, as with Ipe.

Our experts here at Brazilian Lumber recommend oiling hardwood at least once every six months to preserve its natural color. This is in addition to regular and proper cleaning to keep it in top condition.

Having explained some of its advantages, Bulletwood can be a legitimate alternative to more expensive exotic types of hardwood decking such as Ipe. Still, Ipe offers the best weather resistance, stability, longevity, and no other species performs at this level.

However, Massaranduba is the wood of choice for those seeking a uniform appearance, as the wood has very little movement ( for this it is recommended to wait about 7 days for the wood to acclimatize and a good installation process ).
It is very resistant to insects, mildew, and rot. It is used in many exterior projects, such as stairs, decks, and sidewalks.
So, are you ready to learn about the wonder of this remarkable hardwood? Here are 6 facts you may not know about Massaranduba decking (but you should):

items: Hardness
Weather, insect, slip & fire-resistant
Natural beauty
Easy board replacement
A cost-effective choice
Sustainable harvest

blocks.text: 1. Massaranduba Is One Of The Hardest Woods In The World

There is no doubt that Massaranduba decking is considered to be one of the best woods in the world thanks to its hardness. This makes it an incredible option for anyone looking for a deck that is more durable and will last longer than other materials on the market.
Because Massaranduba wood is so durable, it is very versatile and is used in many types of construction, from commercial to residential. Therefore, pretty much nothing can go wrong if you choose it.
2. Massaranduba Is Weather, Insect, Slip & Fire-Resistant
This amazing hardwood comes from South America. It is found in forests where it can receive up to 400+ inches of rain per year, which makes it naturally resistant to heavy rain power.

Additionally, Massaranduba evolved in forests with insects much more skilled at penetrating the wood than their North American counterparts. Very few insects are able to infiltrate their fibers, and certainly native U.S. insects cannot, which is one of the advantages of most tropical hardwoods.

It is also highly resistant to flame spread. Massaranduba typically achieves a high B fire rating. This means that prolonged exposure to flame can cause damage, but the risk of flame spread is minimal.

Like all these advantages were not enough, Massaranduba is also slip resistant. The fine texture of the wood means you don't have to worry about slipping out of the door or falling out while walking late for work.
3. Massaranduba Wood Is All Natural
Massaranduba wood is 100% natural, which means that you can have a beautiful new deck, knowing that you will not do any harm to the planet or its people.
It is biodegradable and does not generate any by-products that can harm the environment. There are no chemicals or plastics, only 100% real wood, making it ideal for reuse.
4. With Massaranduba A Board Replacement Is Not An Issue

One thing that can be stressful is when it comes time to replace your deck boards. Fortunately, this is not a difficulty with Massaranduba. Like other tropical hardwoods, the Bulletwood is known for being a long-lasting material.

If you require replacement parts, you don't have to worry. Since most tropical woods look a little different from the start. Nobody will ever find out that you have replaced the board in the middle for a new one.
5. Massaranduba Is A Cost Effective Choice

With its remarkable properties, you might think that Massaranduba wood might leave a big hole in your wallet, but you will be surprised to see that this is far from the truth. The prices of this magnificent tropical hardwood are about the same as some composites .
Want to know what the best part is? Massaranduba decking can last anywhere from 20 to 70 years, with proper maintenance and depending on weather conditions.
This means it will take some time before you start worrying about replacing a single board of your Massaranduba deck, compared to surfaces made with other materials.
So, is Massaranduba the most profitable deck? Yes, not so much in the short term, but always in the long term.
6. The Massaranduba Is Harvested Sustainably

Brazil's hardwood industry is possibly the best protection of the forest against clear-cutting uses, such as livestock and agriculture. When Massaranduba is harvested and grown in its natural habitat, that area is protected by the organization that has replanted, according to the local or federal government.

Without responsible forest management, forest areas are more likely to be cleared for livestock grazing and plant cultivation. Every purchase of Massaranduba or other tropical wood from conscientious sellers like us increases the value of land with natural forests.

As a company, we specialize in the manufacture and import of sustainably sourced tropical hardwoods and outdoor decking materials. Due to our high technology, we develop the most resistant product while respecting the environment.
We believe that following a sustainable procedure means doing it right. Therefore, one of our main values is to respect the environment by supporting the preservation of the forest .
If you are looking for a wood decking that lasts a long time, is weatherproof, looks great, and does not break the bank, Massaranduba wood is perfect for you.
Rely on our knowledge, expertise, and experience. We promise we offer you only the best products and recommendations for your projects.

posts.title: 7 Features Why Oak Hardwood Flooring Is So Popular In Antigua And Barbuda
posts.h1: 7 Features Why Oak Hardwood Flooring Is So Popular In Antigua And Barbuda

blocks.text: Northern Red Oak makes up a lot of the Oak used for hardwood, but there is also Southern Red Oak and White Oak. The Northern Red Oak is very plentiful in the United States. This Oak Hardwood is native to North America and you can find it anywhere from Southern Appalachia to Central Canada. It's been known to grow up to 150 ft. in height and 6 ft in diameter. A White Oak tree can grow more than 80 ft and also 6 ft in diameter. Also called Spanish Oak, Southern Red Oak often grows in the early founded Spanish colonies.
If you're considering adding or redoing new hardwood floors to your house in Antigua and Barbuda, Oak provides some advantages over other types of wood.
1. Oak Hardwood: Color

Oak comes in various colors that range from brown and red to light beige. You'll often find different colors throughout the same tree. The inner heartwood is often darker than outer sapwoods, but this isn't always the case. In many cases, the sapwood and the heartwood are the same color and over time, the Oak often becomes darker. It often takes on a more amber hue when it's exposed to oxygen and UV light.
2. Oak Hardwood: Stains Easily

One of Oak's advantages to other types of hardwood is its ability of being easily stained. And, because of this, any room can be brightened by its light color and can even become dark like Walnut. Oak's ability of being stained easily allows you to select from various color options. Many popular wood types don't stain as easily and you end up having to deal with the color of wood.
3. Oak Hardwood: Character
Oak has a certain board length and character, particularly European Oak. It's character is it's streaks, knots and other features unique to the tree the natural flooring came from.
4. Oak Hardwood: Abnormalities
Since Oak has a strong, natural grain pattern, it can mask abnormalities like dents, nicks, scratches and other small floor mishaps much better than other floor options.
5. Oak Hardwood: Versatility

Oak has an extremely traditional, timeless appearance. Thus, it tends to work great with many different styles of décor from classic to modern. It's hard to find a décor pattern or combination that doesn't go great with Oak.
6. Oak Hardwood: Stability

When it comes to floors, stability is how the wood responds to levels of moisture either by expanding or shrinking. Oak is a more stable option than other domestic woods and doesn't expand or shrink quite like maple or hickory wood flooring does.
7. Oak Hardwood: Maintenance

Oak's maintenance requirements are greatly based on the way it's finished. If you seal it properly, it's able to withstand moisture a lot better than other wood species. But, it's not recommended you allow water to sit on it for very long. If your Oak floor is engineered wood, it will then be able to withstand moisture exposure much better than planks of solid wood.

Overall, it's your choice which type of wood you want to go with for your flooring project in Antigua and Barbuda. But, if you're looking for stability, character, color and more, Oak flooring is the way to go and you can find it at Brazilian Lumber.

Ipe is considered one of the leading 10 hardest types of wood on the planet based on the Janka hardness test. When you combine that with the resistance to splinters, bugs, mold and decay, you'll see you have before you the ideal wood for outdoor use like decking.
4. Ipe Hardwood: Looks Good

Another benefit of Ipe over other types of materials is it looks beautiful with its smooth and uniform texture. It has straight and wavy grains with extremely fine texture. It doesn't require sealing and the maintenance tasks are as simple as mopping and cleaning stain. It's recommended you apply oil to Ipe wood to help enhance its ability of repelling water and UV rays. Oil will also help Ipe wood to maintain its brown-reddish color.
5. Ipe Wood: Sustainable

Ipe wood is sustainable. It lasts for a long time. Without application, it has an over 75 year sustainability. It can even withstand attacks from termites for up to 15 years, which is much longer than many wood types. This is another reason why so many homeowners are turning to Ipe wood decking and flooring.

blocks.text: It's found that Sapele is a tropical species that's gaining popularity the fastest. It's sourced from West Africa, mostly Congo and Cameroon and is often used as a Mahogany alternative.

It's extremely stable nature and consistent dark brown color make it very appealing for manufacturers and craftsmen to work with. When it's quartered and rifted, it has a beautiful ribbon-like look that really stands out when it's finished.

One of Sapele's most intriguing characteristics is its interlocking grain. As these trees start growing the grains in the lumber twist and experience irregular intervals of interlocking, it results in quite the distinctive appearance.
Sapele is largely used in:

items: Windows
Doors
Flooring

blocks.text: It's also used for various specialty architectural applications, including musical instruments. In fact, guitar bodies are often built from this hardwood due to its ideal visual appeal.

If you regularly work with hardwoods, you already know how essential choosing the proper species is for capturing that ideal look you're seeking. More and more woodworking professionals and manufacturers are looking to bring something new to their applications through the use of tropical species alternatives.

Many people are familiar with Teak and Mahogany. However, over the past several years, Sapele has gained popularity and is now being considered a mainstream species of wood with businesses all across the industry.
So, why should you use tropical wood for your next hardwood project in St. Lucia? Here are five reasons:
1.Sapele: The lumber's beauty
Itss dark mahogany-like color is well known and due to its extremely stable nature, it's an attractive choice for various applications.
2. Sapele: Its general availability
Grown widely throughout Africa, this wood can be sourced fairly consistently all year long, providing you with a steady and consistent supply.
3. Sapele: Ease of use

This tropical wood has a reputation of being an extremely simple species to work with. It's simple to machine, glue, fasten and finish which makes it an ideal choice for products like architectural millwork and doors.
4. Sapele: Its durability

Many individuals decide to use this wood for its appealing grain pattern and color, but it's also known for its durability and strength, which makes it a popular species for creating musical instruments.
5. Sapele: Variety of sizes

A Sapele tree typically grows to a very large size, allowing mills to really maximize the output of its logs. This results in various thicknesses and lengths available in the market. These days, you can find this wood in all standard thicknesses that range from 4/4 to 16/4, helping it nicely match up with nearly any project.

Also, to continue singing the praises of Sapele, only to inform you that you'll have a difficult time finding this tropical wood in stock in lumber yards or that there's a waning supply of it, would only defeat the point, right? Not to worry - with this premium African hardwood, that scenario is far from reality.
With such stability, availability and beauty, it's not a surprise that Sapele has become the most popular sought-after African hardwood species.

posts.title: Best 3 Ways To Use Cumaru in Your Ceiling
posts.h1: Best 3 Ways To Use Cumaru in Your Ceiling

blocks.text: In a pandemic world, homeowners are rethinking what outdoor living means. If before outdoor living space was used to extend the usable capacity of a home, with Covid-19 there are safety and practical aspects for using the exterior as well.

The outer space can provide a more ventilated gathering area for family and friends, which may decrease the risk of transmission if all other precautions are taken. It also means you can entertain people without having them enter into your home.

Outdoor space has become essential for commercial businesses as well, since people are opting more and more for outdoor seating. With limited indoor occupancy, an outdoor area for commercial businesses can increase their seating capacity. Outdoor gatherings are now the new normal.
Why To Consider Cumaru When Designing An Outdoor Space

One of the most important aspects when designing a new space is choosing the color. That is why selecting the right type of hardwood for your outdoor (and indoor) ceiling is really crucial. There are many considerations when it comes to picking the right type of wood, and color is on the top of that list. Using light or dark colored wood can create an entirely different vibe. It even determines what you're able to do with the rest of your space.

Cumaru has become a popular hardwood option for outdoor ceilings. With its golden tan to honey brown color, it is an option that gives warmth to contemporary and modern homes and is neutral enough to allow for many design options.

For those not yet familiar with this amazing hardwood, Cumaru (dipteryx odorata, pronounced as ku-mah-rue) or Brazilian teak is a naturally durable timber similar to Ipe. It is ideal for exterior use since it is a highly resistant wood that has an A1 fire rating as well as being rot, decay, and insect resistant without the use of chemicals and toxins. For this reason, Cumaru is often used for decking, siding, cladding, flooring, and even for exterior ceilings or overhangs.
Cumaru looks just as appealing indoors as it does outdoors, and using the same wood throughout the house creates a seamless transition from exterior to interior spaces.

The continuity in materials also creates a natural flow between indoor and outdoor rooms. Choosing Cumaru for both interior and exterior ceilings will have a tremendous impact on the aesthetics of your house and the way you experience the exterior of your home.

In Florida, where the weather can shift between sunny hot and persistently rainy all in one day, Cumaru has been gaining popularity for some time. As Cumaru can withstand extreme weather conditions without warping or bending, it is ideal for the Sunshine State's fickle weather. Also, when used for ceilings, Cumaru requires very little maintenance if it's not in the direct path of sunlight, and thus not exposed to UV rays which "bleach" out the color of Cumaru unless protected by a hardwood oil or sealer.
Even before the pandemic, homes in Miami incorporated a lot of indoor-outdoor living spaces. With near perfect weather all year long, it is the ideal spot for outdoor activities and relaxation.

When selecting the right hardwood for this luxury Miami home, the architect contacted Brazilian Lumber and chose its premium Cumaru. The use of Cumaru tied in the exterior cladding to the interior ceilings of the private gym the owners built on their second story. The Cumaru for this posh home provides a warm contrast to the copper gutters and glass windows wrapped around it.

Sliding doors on the second floor offers a view of its upscale neighborhood - for ventilation - and again, with the semi-outdoors concept in mind. The gym is surrounded by a small wraparound balcony which has the same Cumaru cladding on its ceilings.

The architect of the home also chose Brazilian Lumber's Cumaru for the ceilings on the back balcony which is attached to the master bedroom as well as all the first floor's outside ceilings and outdoor kitchen cabana.
How To Install Cumaru On An Angled Ceiling
In this same home, the 45-angled ceiling in the gym area adds dimension and appeal to the small space.
For those who would like to use Cumaru in a 45-angled ceiling, it is best to use a professional contractor. As with all hardwoods, it is good to have someone with experience doing the installation.

Hiring a professional is invaluable as he or she will know all the steps required for proper installation. The first thing that should be done is acclimate the wood to the temperature of the indoor space. Even though Cumaru does not generally warp or shift when it is installed, it will need to be acclimated for at least three days, if it will be placed in air conditioning.

The next step, and possibly the most important step, is leveling the ceiling so that the 45 angle cuts will align perfectly. For the angled ceiling in this gym, tongue and groove boards were used with hidden deck fasteners with the exception of the boards that were perpendicular to the center boards. Due to the angle, those had to be installed using stainless steel 8 x 1 1/2 screws , which were then covered with Cumaru plugs .

Different board lengths can be used to create patterns or designs for the ceiling. In this gym ceiling 1 x 6 Cumaru boards were used throughout. Three foot long boards were used for the center of the ceiling, while seven foot and fourteen foot boards were installed all around the sides.

Placing the long boards at a 90° angle to the short boards added visual interest as well as the illusion of a larger space. The gym ceiling would look boring with a flat drywall and crown molding or other decorative features would not work for such a modern house. The Cumaru ceilings were an ideal choice for this space.

If a home gym can use Cumaru in the ceiling, commercial gyms may also want to try it to provide contrast to their industrial look. Doing yoga or sit-ups with a Cumaru ceiling is more pleasing to look at than drywall. Come to think of it, wood on the ceiling certainly makes it look like you are looking down on your floor.
Other Benefits Of Cumaru

The pandemic has certainly made it almost essential for people to open up their spaces for air to come in - and out. You will like to know that Cumaru ceilings can withstand hot and humid temperatures for many outdoor projects, protecting their color and tone as long as they are not in direct sunlight.
Here is an example of a Cumaru ceiling used in a bathroom:

Other than the ceiling, of course, Cumaru can be used for many projects, including cabinetry , flooring, furniture, docks and other outdoor home projects. Here's why Cumaru also makes a big difference:
Grain/Texture: Grain is interlocked, with a medium texture and a waxy feel.
Rot Resistance: Cumaru has excellent durability and weathering properties. The wood is rated as very durable regarding decay resistance, with good resistance to termites.
Odor: Cumaru has a faint, vanilla or cinnamon-like odor when being worked.

Sustainability: This wood species is not listed in the CITES Appendices or on the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species. CITES stands for the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora), while IUCN is the acronym for International Union for Conservation of Nature.
For more info on Cumaru, refer to Wood Database .

Cumaru can also be mixed with Ipe or your choice of hardwood. Brazilian Lumber's outstanding customer service can help guide you to more than 20 types of hardwoods and composite decks you can use for both your indoor and outdoor projects.
