posts.title: Best 9 Outdoor Living Room Ideas for Homeowner Renovators
posts.h1: Best 9 Outdoor Living Room Ideas for Homeowner Renovators

blocks.text: Having stayed at home for many months, homeowners have suddenly discovered a new pastime and for some, a new passion: homeowner renovators. Unlike any other pastime or project, though, this one has some strong staying power, according to several reports .

With limited travel options and restrictions, as well as fewer outdoor activities and social engagement options, many are finding ways to spruce up every inch of their homes all the way to their outdoor spaces.

In the luxury sector, for instance, homeowners are adding areas to their homes that they can no longer visit with confidence, including gyms, saunas or public swimming pools. As a result, more people are choosing to either remodel their outdoor space or add outdoor elements such as decks and pergolas to their backyards.

Jesse Harrison of Harrison Design, an architectural and interior design firm based in Los Angeles, was even quoted as saying in a Wall Street Journal feature, "For homeowners renovators and clients with two working adults and children trying to do schoolwork," you need three or four distinct spaces." For homeowners renovators trying to make room, the front yard or backyard - is certainly getting more than a cursory look.

It helps that confidence is back in the home market. It was not the case last May when the NAHB-Wells Fargo Housing Market Index , which depicts builder confidence in the construction of single-family houses, was only 37 points. In September, it climbed up by 48 points, reaching 83 points (the barometer is 50 points).

Todd Teta of ATTOM , a leading provider of nationwide property data in the US, said: "Homeowners renovators saw their equity rise far and wide throughout the United States during the second quarter of this year in yet another sign of the housing market punching back against the Coronavirus pandemic.
More homeowner renovators rose into equity-rich territory and escaped the seriously underwater lane, putting more money into the average household."

The housing market is clearly showing signs of stabilizing and for those seeking to unleash their creativity, the homeowner renovators find that it's well worth the effort to renovate their space. Renovating their homes keeps them busy - and at home, where they feel safer.
Idea For Homeowner Renovators: Comfort Zone
For Trexpert Kate Campbell, outdoor spaces are comfort zones: "When it comes to home design and outdoor spaces, comfort zones are exactly where we need to be."

Campbell recalls the time when decks were utilitarian, even boring, but advances in outdoor living have changed all that perception. "Your deck should feel like an extension of your indoor living space and what better way to do that than creating a zone that feels completely geared toward your personal style and comfort."
Outdoor living rooms with roofs can provide that comfort vibe. You can unwind on dry, clean and comfortable outdoor furniture that doesn't get rained out or snowed in.

An expert should be able to map out the construction of your outdoor living room, but before he or she does that, you must have a building permit and should have already chosen the types of wood and roof that suit your personal style. Ceiling applications can be done in a variety of materials including hardwood and composite decking for homeowner renovators.

Whether the joists of your porch ceiling are exposed or if you already have a covering, a layer of plywood must be installed first. Then, the boards are nailed to the plywood and then installed using the tongue and groove method.

Learning to ask the right questions is essential? Hardwood comes in a variety of lengths and dimensions, and can be milled to fit specifications. On the other hand, composite decking boards come in standard lengths. Most composite decking companies sell 12 foot boards or 16 foot boards.

The length of the space should be considered when picking the right type of material. The most commonly used board sizes are 1x6 or 5/4 x6 boards since the broader boards give the ceiling a more ample appearance.

Another aspect of planning your outdoor living or dining room should be the flooring. The right type of material can give the area a comfort vibe. Some options include concrete pavers, stones, tiles, bricks, composite decking, wood tiles or deck tiles, or hardwood decking boards. Wood options for flooring are great for covered areas because of their easy maintenance since they are out of direct sunlight.

Choosing the right type of hardwood for your outdoor space is important and your contractor or designer should be able to help you. Hardwood deck tiles or boards made of Ipe wood or Cumaru wood are becoming increasingly popular. These hardwoods are heat- and scratch-resistant, mildew and insect resistant, and very elegant, making them ideal for any exterior project.
Here are some of the best outdoor living ideas to inspire you as you renovate your spaces:
Idea For Homeowner Renovators: Playing With Ceiling Shapes Provides An Open-Style Approach

A-LINE OR CURVED DESIGN. Ceilings need not be flat and boring. A curved or A-line design gives a space an architectural element of interest while also adding spaciousness to a room. In exterior overhangs, this element of interest can be done by cladding the ceiling with hardwood. Playing with the length and layout of the wood boards can create such an effect. An added bonus of a wood clad ceiling is that it adds weather resistance as well as improving the appearance of the house as homeowner renovators. Ceiling design can maximize the potential of your outdoor space.
Idea For Homeowner Renovators: Vintage Look Works With Modern Furniture

A GED YET APPEALING. If left unoiled, hardwoods such as Ipe, Cumaru, and Garapa will turn a silver patina, which could work if you're trying to capture a vintage or coastal shabby chic look. It is important to find the right decking material that can resist the weather and suit your aesthetic preference. To see if a sliver colored deck is right for you, go to your nearest park with hardwood benches or your local beach and walk on those aged or silvery boardwalks to find out if going vintage is appealing as aged wine. An added bonus for homeowner renovators? A weathered hardwood deck needs no yearly maintenance such as sanding or oiling, saving you time and money.
Idea For Homeowner Renovators: White Outdoor Room Works Against A Backdrop Of The Ocean

CLEAN, WHITE AND CONTEMPORARY. Keeping the color palette in the neutrals such as white and beige is ideal for contemporary outdoor spaces, especially with an ocean view as a backdrop. Several materials can be used to create such a look, including hardwood floors. Hardwood floors made of Ipe or Cumaru are great because in their original color they provide a warm earth tone and left unoiled, they turn a gray color, which combines well with white furniture. White furniture can also make a semi-outdoor room look clean, classy and effortless. Nothing is as pure as white against the backdrop of an ocean with your yacht docked alongside it.
Idea For Homeowner Renovators: Have The Best Of Both Worlds - Indoors And Outdoors

INDOORS AND OUTDOORS. To create harmonious fluidity between indoor and outdoor spaces, you can incorporate elements of Mid-Century Modern design. Use the same hardwood cladding for both the interior ceilings and exterior overhangs to create a seamless transition between indoor and outdoor space. This effect can also be created by using the same hardwood flooring for the decking. This is especially true when the two spaces are separated by large sliding glass windows which provide lots of natural light.
Idea For Homeowner Renovators: Mix And Match Light And Dark, Even The Wood Stains

MIX AND MATCH. When deciding on a color scheme or look for your exterior space, don't be afraid to mix and match colors. You can go LIGHT for a more neutral feel, or DARK for a more cozy feel. Or both. Mix wood stains from your railings to your deck all the way to the color schemes of your outdoor furniture. Not sure what shade variations to choose? Consult a designer or start by incorporating less permanent elements into your design as homeowner renovators. A colorful rug, light colored throw pillows, industrial string lights or antique-looking lanterns are all ways you can upgrade from a minimalistic style.
Idea For Homeowner Renovators: Ipe Oil Can Make Your Deck Glisten

SILK AND SHINY. Going for a shiny look is also one approach you can take as a homeowner renovator. Here, Sergio Braga of My Rustic Design showcases a pool with a glistening ipe deck. It's Instagram-ready. By the way, using Ipe Oil protects and conditions the wood while maintaining a completely natural appearance.
Idea For Homeowner Renovators: Trellis Or Pergola For An Urban Or Industrial Vibe On Your Roof

TRELLIS OR PERGOLA? Many landscape architects may use the term trellis as catch-all for pergola structures, which consist of at least four columns that support a latticework made up of beams, stringers or rafters. They're usually freestanding or attached to a house. Tell your architect what you envision for your outdoor space. A pergola may have an urban or industrial vibe built alongside a commercial structure.
Idea For Homeowner Renovators: What Hardwood To Choose From
There are many selections of exotic hardwoods, North American woods and composite decking.

Exotic hardwoods such Ipe, Cumaru and Garapa are the best for your outdoor or semi-outdoor living space because they last longer and require less maintenance than North American woods. They are ideal for exterior uses as they are mildew and decay resistant. Ipe is even scratch-resistant, which makes it ideal for outdoors where it is exposed. Based on their hardness and resistance to damage, exotic hardwoods are more desirable than the most common North American hardwoods such as oak. They are perfect for homeowner renovators.

For those looking for other types of decking options, Trex offers many durable composite decking products that are easy to install. They can be installed over timber, steel or aluminum substructures with joist centers at maximum of 400mm apart.

posts.title: 3 Tips For Perfect Hardwood Maintenance
posts.h1: 3 Tips For Perfect Hardwood Maintenance

blocks.text: A hardwood deck is an investment that adds value to your house and provides space to spend quality time with friends and family. Ipe , Cumaru , Jatoba, and Garapa hardwood decks are some of the most beautiful in the world, especially because of their coloring. Although hardwood requires no maintenance for structural integrity, it is important to learn the proper way to maintain its beautiful color. So these are the tips that Brazilian Lumber recommends for deck maintenance:

items: Hardwood maintenance and color
Step by step hardwood maintenance guide
Key hardwood maintenance recommendation

blocks.text: 1. Hardwood Maintenance & Color

To keep the color and material in good condition, you should regularly finish the deck with a good oil-based finish, developed specifically for hardwood. Finishes that are not specifically formulated for these types of woods will not penetrate the deck in a sufficient quantity to provide adequate protection. When you re-oil your deck, you should pressure wash it first. It is important to remember that different hardwoods can withstand different pressures. For instance, an Ipe deck can handle a higher PSI than a Garapa deck. Most hardwoods cannot withstand pressures exceeding 1200 psi. Once the deck has been pressure washed, it should be allowed to dry for at least 24 hours before applying the oil.

Keep in mind that the structural integrity of the boards will not change depending on the color. This is why these hardwoods are so ideal for exterior construction. So if you like the silvered deck look, which you see at a lot of Caribbean resorts or on public boardwalks made of hardwood, it is not necessary to apply oil frequently.
2. Step By Step Hardwood Maintenance Guide
Pre-finish your hardwood lumber: Like sunscreen, pre-finishing helps block UV rays and slows the adaptation process. It is recommended that you complete it before installing the new hardwood decking.

items:
A well-installed deck

In order to ensure a long life span for your wood, it is important that the deck is installed correctly . If it is well installed, you won't need to incur rushed maintenance. There are many factors to consider in this process:
When hardwood enters a new environment, it takes a period of time to adapt to the new temperature and humidity to prevent the wood from shrinking or expanding.
The time required for hardwood to adapt depends on the type of wood and the environment it is in, but usually, 7 to 14 days is sufficient.

Clean the area thoroughly

Leaves, dirt, pollen, and other debris will quickly stain the surface of your deck, but the more you keep it clean, the longer it will last. Hardwoods are naturally resistant to mold and mildew, but they are not immune, especially on the surface. The removal of moisture and organic dirt on a regular basis is the key to protect it from fungus.

blocks.text: If It is no longer enough to just clean the surface, a deeper cleaning is required. To do this, use a hardwood cleaning solution that combines one gallon of warm water with one quart of powdered oxygenated bleach. The solution will be strong enough to remove mold and mildew. Before applying the product, clean the surface with a special brush, rinse it and let it dry completely. The use of a broom or a brush may help remove excess water from your deck. Brazilian Lumber also sells specific deck cleaners and brighteners .
3. Scrub and wipe
While applying the cleaning solution, use a brush to create suds and loosen deeper dirt particles. Don't forget to rinse it constantly.
4. Let the deck dry
Once the deck has been cleaned and pressure washed, allow at least 24 hours to pass before oiling the deck.
5. Refinish regularly to maintain the color

If you oil your hardwood regularly, you won't need to refinish it. And, if you prefer your wood deck to turn gray over time, you don't need to follow this esthetic recommendation either. But, if you want your hardwood to maintain its original color, you will need to use the proper products because not all cleaners, oils, and sealers are made for hardwood decking. First, we list the options for you, and then explain their differences and proper use:

items: Oil
Sealer
Brightener

Sealer: Protects hardwoods from damage due to rot and unsightly mold or mildew, while keeping the wood grain intact. For this reason, many people prefer a deck sealer that penetrates the wood rather than a deck paint that only sits on top of it.

blocks.text: 6. Sand and prevent color fading

If the color has faded, and you want to recover it, you could sand it. Do this with 220 medium-grit sandpaper and then wipe the surface with a damp cloth or sponge. This will improve the texture and make the wood assimilate the oil better. Regarding the material, it is recommended to use garnet to remove scratches and prepare the surface for finishing. Finally, remember to do more frequent maintenance such as oiling the deck so that the color does not fade.
3. Key Hardwood Maintenance Recommendation

Tough stains may need to be removed, but if you are not careful, you can also remove quite a bit of wood from the deck. So, the key to avoiding that is to use some pressure washing methods , paying attention to these recommendations:

items: Choose a day when your deck is completely dry and humidity is low.
Use the lowest possible PSI. Start at 500 PSI
Use fan-shaped nozzles that extend 40-60 degrees.
Continue to use the fiber and spray it back and forth about 1 foot away from the wood.
Start from the house and work your way outward.

blocks.text: With these recommendations in mind, the restoration of your decking will be great, and the end result will be as good as new.

posts.title: The 8 Best Weather Resistant Woods
posts.h1: The 8 Best Weather Resistant Woods

blocks.text: What do Ipe , cumaru , jatoba , garapa and teak have in common? They are some of the most resistant, durable and highly sought after hardwoods on the market.

They are incredibly resistant to rot, insect damage and weathering since the internal composition is undesirable to insects and fungi. Because of this, they are perfect for outdoor projects and will last outdoors for well over thirty five years.
Some softwoods such as California Red Wood , cedar and cypress are also used for exterior construction, and luckily you can find all the types of wood previously mentioned here at Brazilian Lumber.
The Best Weather Resistant Woods For Outdoors Projects

Real lumber is an excellent choice for adding warmth to garden structures and for decks. In addition, woods have a wide range of aesthetic expressions , from wild, uneven wood posts to sophisticated, smoothly sanded decks. The type of hardwood chosen for a project also adds style because of the variety of colors and textures they have.

From an ecological point of view, wood is a good choice if it is harvested sustainably. As an all natural product, hardwood is not treated with any chemicals or contaminants. When its life cycle is over (which isn't for well over 70 years) it will eventually be able to decay and not fill up a landfill. That is why rainforest conservation is a key aspect of our company's core values.

With this in mind, sustainability is a very important aspect for our brand and company. As it helps preserve the tropical forest, because the natural life cycle of each tree is respected, as are all other aspects of the local biodiversity. That is why the tropical rainforest preservation project has full support.

The majority of all softwood on the market has to be chemically treated to prevent rot. However, some woods have superior rot resistance naturally, without the need for chemicals. Here's a list of the best, most weather resistant woods to help you build the project of your dreams in a chemical-free way.

items: Ipe
Cumaru
Jatoba
Garapa
Teak
Cypress
California red wood
Cedar

blocks.text: Ipe's Resistance To Insect And Heat Damage

Its density and natural oils make it practically impervious to insects (so deterioration is not a problem). Ipe lumber is the perfect example of weather resistant woods because it does not scratch or splinter easily, does not heat up in the sun and has a high coefficient of friction, making it perfect for outdoor and coastal construction.

Ipe lumber has been on trend for years and deserves a special mention as there are many ways to use it. This incredible, strong, durable, and beautiful hardwood is THE perfect choice for outdoor projects like backyard decks, walkways, etc. In addition, to being used on countless home patios, it has also been used for landmarks such as the Atlantic Boardwalk and Treasure Island Resort in Las Vegas.
Image Of Atlantic Boardwalk
So, to point out some of the best features of Ipe, here are the most noteworthy:

items: Weather resistance
Resistant to insect damage
Durability
Versatile
Strength
A1 fire rating
Does not heat up in the sun
Color can vary from reddish brown, to a yellowish olive brown or blackish brown.
Janka rating (a rating largely used by the timber flooring industry to compare the hardness of a floor): 3,510 lb

blocks.text: Cumaru's Resistance To Mildew And Rotting

Cumaru lumber, also known as Brazilian teak, is one of the densest hardwoods available for outdoor use after Ipe lumber. Not only because of this characteristic, but also because it is resistant to mildew and rot. It is often used for patios, decking, railroad ties, and other purposes. Like Ipe, Cumaru is another example of weather resistant woods because it has an A1 fire rating, does not scratch or splinter easily, does not heat up in the sun, and has a high coefficient of friction, making it perfect for outdoor and coastal construction.
So, choosing Cumaru, means choosing:

items: Resistance to mildew and rot
Density
A1 fire rating
Does not heat up in the sun
High coefficient of friction
Janka hardness: 3,330 lb
Its color is mainly dark brown

blocks.text: Jatoba's Resistance To Weathering, Rot and Insect Infestation

Commonly known as Brazilian cherry due to its similarity in color to the native cherry, Jatoba lumber is another one of the incredibly strong weather resistant woods. It is also known to be resistant to termites and most insects.
This tropical wood is often used in exterior construction due to its durability.
So remember, Jatoba equals:

items: Durability
Toughness
Resistance to termites and most insects
Janka hardness: 2,690 lb
Its color ranges from a light orangish brown to a darker reddish brown

blocks.text: Garapa's Durability And Workability

This tropical hardwood is one of the finest woods for decking. You can count on Garapa lumber for nearly any sort of outdoors woodworking venture because of its sturdiness and resistance to extreme weather conditions. Also, this hardwood is water, decay, and mold resistant. It is widely used for patios and decking.
Let us remind you that by choosing Garapa you will have:

items: Durability against harsh weather conditions.
Workability
Resistance to water, decay and mold
Janka hardness: 1,650 lb
May be golden to yellowish-brown in color

blocks.text: Teak Weather Resistance

This wood is considered to be the sea-resistant wood per excellence, not only because of its durability, but also for being a perfect example of weather resistant woods. It contains natural vegetable oils that make it extremely resistant to water as well as to termites and insects.

It is probably the most strong and famous hardwood and is most likely to be used in shipbuilding as it can be protected from dry rot. It is also an excellent choice for small outdoor projects such as furniture, patios, flooring and other projects where the beauty of the wood should be as loud as the craftsmanship. blocks.text: Building a new deck can create a whole new, beautiful space for your family and friends. Plus, the deck will quickly add value to your property. This amazing hardwood, sometimes called Brazilian Walnut, comes from South America and is the hardest tropical wood. Terraces, cladding, pillars, and any other road structures are made of it. What makes IPE truly remarkable lumber and the perfect decking material is its durability, quality, and weather resistance.
Although wood is not the only material for decking, it is the best option, especially if we refer to Ipe, which has the following main characteristics:

items: Toughness
Durability
Weather resistance
Won't be damaged by insects
Versatile
A1 fire rating
Does not heat up in the sun
Scratch-resistant

blocks.text: All these characteristics make Ipe the star wood of Brazilian Lumber.

When choosing the perfect decking material there are other aspects to take into account, such as the climatic conditions of your home, the size of the platform you want to build and what is your budget for the project. For all these factors, Ipe wood remains the solution, and these are the main reasons why:
1. Ipe´s durability and hardness

Ipe wood is considered the most effective choice of wood decking on earth due to its hardness, which is generally compared to iron. That's why it's often used on boardwalks and other high-traffic decks. Ipe is incredibly strong because of the tropical environment where the tree grows, called Tabebuia , as well as the natural oils it is made of, which guarantee the durability of at least fifty years.

Moreover, thanks to its density, Ipe hardwood can withstand all kinds of threats such as extreme weather, sun, and, because of its high phenol content, it will not rot, mildew, or be damaged by insects.

Ipe lumber is biodegradable, renewable, and recyclable. Since it is a durable material, it does not need to be replaced for decades. In addition, Ipe is naturally dense and resilient, which means that, unlike soft or domestic woods, it does not have to be chemically treated to be resistant to the environment, which in turn means it doesn't have pollutants, toxins, or chemicals that are a hazard to the environment.

Also, tropical hardwoods such as Ipe hardwood are among the few renewable resources in nature that can be replenished twice or more in the course of our lives. But, it is not enough that the resource itself is sustainable, the process must also guarantee it, as we do here at Brazilian Lumber, where Ipe lumber comes from responsible and sustainable forestry .

blocks.text: 7. The fire resistance of Ipe

posts.title: 8 Reasons Why Lumber Is The Best Building Material
posts.h1: 8 Reasons Why Lumber Is The Best Building Material

blocks.text: The benefits of lumber as a building material continue to outperform other products on the market in terms of environmental sustainability and performance.

When it comes to commercial and industrial buildings that must stand the test of time, lumber has proven it has the necessary strength required, as well as unique advantages over steel and concrete. Plus, this amazing material offers not only remarkable durability but an aesthetic warmth to any type of environment.

Lumber is a very useful material that has many benefits that make it the best option for your construction projects. With all the knowledge and experience we have at Brazilian Lumber, here are what we consider the main advantages:

items: Natural, renewable, recyclable, and biodegradable building material
Carbon positive element
The use of lumber as a building material implies the need for low energy production
Lumber is an adaptable, versatile, and durable material
The sound absorption of lumber
Electrical and heat resistance
Studies show that using lumber is healthier for people
The beauty of lumber

blocks.text: Lumber: Natural, Renewable, Recyclable, and Biodegradable Construction Material

It's one of the few natural and renewable building materials. The cyclical process of harvesting and rejuvenating lumber for production ensures that it will continue to be available. As a purely natural product, it's not treated with chemicals or pollutants and is non-toxic, so it is safe to handle and touch; it also ages naturally and does not decompose into environmentally harmful material.

From an ecological point of view, lumber is a great option if it is harvested sustainably, which is a very important aspect for our brand and our company as it contributes to the preservation of the tropical forest. Therefore, the rainforest protection project has full support.
Lumber Is A CO2-Positive Building Material

The environmental impact of lumber is considerably lower compared to other building materials, such as stainless steel, aluminum or concrete. The role of trees, which are the suppliers of this material, contributes to the reduction of CO2 emissions, causing a positive effect that counteracts climate change .

As explained above, lumber can be grown and regenerated through natural processes such as replanting and forest management. As forests grow (through solar energy), they also naturally and efficiently remove carbon dioxide from the environment. This is an exclusive benefit that lumber has over other building materials.
Carbon is an elemental building block of all living things on earth. As a forest grows, the trees absorb atmospheric carbon dioxide and store it in their leaves, branches and trunks.
Lumber: Low-Energy Building Material
Producing lumber uses much less energy from fossil fuels per unit volume than steel, concrete or aluminum while minimizing pollution.

In addition, it improves energy efficiency due to its natural cellular structure . As a result, homes, and buildings require less energy for heating and cooling. Plus, it can help regulate humidity levels to a small degree.
Lumber Is An Adaptable, Versatile, and Durable Building Material

With proper care, lumber can last for hundreds of years, resisting the elements and adapting to any climate. Heavy structures can even withstand fire naturally by creating an outer layer of charcoal while remaining structurally stable.
In addition, this material is highly adaptable for both indoor and outdoor projects, and its texture and variety of colors help it blend in with most decorating styles.
Sound Absorption Of Lumber
Lumber absorbs sound instead of reflecting or amplifying it, and can help to significantly reduce the noise level for greater comfort.
Lumber: Electrical and Heat Resistance

It has a natural resistance to electrical conduction. Its strength and dimensions are also not significantly affected by heat, which provides stability to the construction and greater safety for certain fire situations. In fact, there are some types like IPE lumber which has a class A fire resistance, which is one of the many aspects by which it is compared to the strength of concrete or steel.
Studies Show That Using Lumber Is Healthier For People

A great deal of research has shown that lumber in the home environment, at work or at school has positive effects on your health. In addition, studies have found that exposure brings health benefits similar to those of being in nature. We list some positive aspects of using it in your construction projects:

items: Improved mood and self-expression
Improves air quality by moderating humidity, facilitating breathing
Warm and comfortable feeling
Reduction of blood pressure, heart rate, and stress
When surrounded with the material older adults interact more closely
Students in classrooms surrounded by the material have lower heart rates and fewer stress responses than students in classrooms with plastic and metal
Two out of three workers prefer offices with chairs, desks, and blinds made of the material, to the same office with plastic elements

blocks.text: The Beauty Of Lumber

Lumber can add warmth, texture, and character to any room. Studies have shown that people positively associate the building material and find it visually appealing. With the wide variety available, this stunning material offers an incredible range of aesthetic options . In addition to the different mechanical, acoustic, thermal, and environmental properties it possesses.

posts.title: Best 4 Step Guide For Cleaning & Treating IPE Lumber
posts.h1: Best 4 Step Guide For Cleaning & Treating IPE Lumber

blocks.text: Although it may seem like a tedious task at first, learning to clean and treat Ipe lumber is fun, easy and profitable. Plus, when the job is done, you'll feel as proud as any dedicated homeowner does.

All decks, regardless of whether they are made of hardwood, treated wood, or composite decking, can hardly avoid, at least in part, possible external effects, such as sun, rain, leaves, dirt, mold or insects.
But when it comes to Ipe wood, such crucial factors as traffic, termites and fungal infestation have no effect on the Brazilian walnut, which is also what Ipe is called.

As for sun exposure, aging seems to be an obvious benefit, which will turn your Ipe lumber into a beautiful gray patina, naturally. In addition, its durability is unbeatable. Ipe lumber is unaffected by the elements, due to its incredible density and practically zero moisture absorption.

This amazing hardwood has many extraordinary properties that makes it the perfect lumber for decks, cladding, pillars and for all other structures needed in construction. Here at Brazilian Lumber , we love Ipe, so we want to share with you what makes it a truly remarkable wood :

items: Durability
Quality
Weather, mold, rot, fire, decay and insect damage resistance
3,510 lb Janka hardness score
Ideal for indoor and outdoor projects
Can last up to 75 years with regular cleaning and annual maintenance

blocks.text: Ipe lumber has a rich brown color with red and amber undertones. The boards tend to have many color variations, which means patterns can be attractive and may appear less obvious when you need to replace them.
It has a very dense, interlocking grain, which can be straight or wavy. The result is both attractive and slip-resistant.

Since this is high quality lumber, maintenance is an important requirement that, as long as it is good, can extend the life of your wood and keep your deck in great condition for over 70 years. Luckily it's not difficult, it's not expensive, but it's necessary.

Remember that although Ipe wood is incredibly easy to maintain, it doesn't mean that it is maintenance free . Follow the tips below, and we promise that you will give your Ipe lumber the perfect maintenance treatment.
Best Tips For Cleaning and Treating Ipe Lumber:

Ipe lumber is popular with homeowners everywhere, especially because it is easy to conserve. You don't need to clean your Ipe deck once a day, just sweeping it once a week is enough to prevent dirt from building up. First, we will give you 4 tips for easy and good cleaning, and afterwards we will detail each step:

items: Sweep your Ipe deck once a week with an outdoor broom
Scrub and wipe your Ipe lumber
Let the lumber of your deck dry
Give your lumber a proper maintenance

Sweep your Ipe lumber: Excessive debris can cause stains or water accumulation, leaving scratches and unsightly marks. Therefore, once a month, you should check for proper drainage and ventilation. For this step, pay attention to these recommendations:
Start by removing garden furniture from the surface

Next, examine the cracks for leaves of pine cones gathering between the boards. If dirt builds up, use a scraper or spatula to clean it off. Instead of sweeping again, use a vacuum cleaner to remove dirt.
After vacuuming, take your garden hose and rinse the deck.

blocks.text: If you need to remove pollen or algae from your Ipe lumber, use a mild cleaning solution to make your decks spotless. You can also prepare a household cleaning solution, which will remove these elements without damaging your patio. Mix one quart of bleach in one gallon of warm water, and you will get the right solution.
2 . Scrub and wipe your Ipe lumber: Use a brush to apply your preferred cleaning solution to the boards. Then rinse the entire decking again to make sure there is no residue left on the wood.
3 . Let the Ipe lumber of your deck dry: Once the cover has been cleaned and pressure washed, allow at least 24 hours before oiling.

4. Give your Ipe lumber proper maintenance: Although cleaning helps the Ipe decking retain its natural properties, you should also perform annual maintenance to ensure the durability of the lumber. The following is a list of the materials you need to properly treat your Ipe wood:

items: An oil-based sealer for natural hardwood, like walnut oil
A 220 medium-grit sandpaper
A vacuum
Protection gloves
A natural bristle brush

blocks.text: After proper cleaning and thorough drying, which is actually how good maintenance begins, it is time to sand and apply the oil base. Why? Because this will help prevent the color from fading, keeping its original tone.

For proper sanding you can use 220 grit sandpaper, then wipe the surface with a damp cloth or sponge, this will improve the texture and allow the lumber to better absorb the oil. As for the material, it is recommended to use garnet to remove scratches and prepare the surface for finishing.
Now it's time to oil it up. Just remember that if you oil your Ipe lumber regularly , it won't need to be refinished .
If you choose to keep your Ipe in silver, all you have to do is seal the deck during installation. And don't worry, the bleaching process doesn't affect the structure of the lumber.
In addition, vacuuming and rinsing the dust is a must. For better penetration, consider using a pre-sealer to open up the wood. You can find all the products you need here with us.
Apply the sealer with a lint-free cloth or natural bristle brush. Then, use a dry cloth to remove excess oil. Finally, allow the product to dry for 24 hours.
Final Recommendations For Cleaning and Treating Ipe Lumber:

items: Before cleaning the Ipe deck, make sure that the weather does not hold any unpleasant surprises. Choose a sunny day, when the air is dry and the chances of rain are minimal.

Pressure-washing your Ipe is a tricky subject. Some experts say it's harmful, while others advise that it's okay. If you choose to pressure wash the deck, make sure the setting is no higher than 1200psi.
If you oil your Ipe deck to maintain its color and protect it from UV fading, we recommend that you do so once a year.

blocks.text: There you have it! By now, you should know everything there is to know on how to clean Ipe lumber and help it maintain its natural shine. Do not forget to follow a simple cleaning routine and do an annual checkup.

posts.title: 5 Best Reasons Why Teak Is Supremely Water Resistant
posts.h1: 5 Best Reasons Why Teak Is Supremely Water Resistant

blocks.text: Teak is an exceptionally durable wood, known primarily for its resistance to water and wet climates , which is why it is used in shipbuilding. It has been used in the construction of high-end ships and yachts since the Middle Ages. When it was first introduced in the United States in the 1950s, it quickly became a popular choice for outdoor furniture.

It contains natural vegetable oils that make it very resistant to water, which is why it is considered the sea-resistant wood par excellence. It is also resistant to termites and insects. In addition, it is a stable wood that does not crack severely in the weather like other woods.

It's also a great choice for small outdoor projects like furniture, patios, flooring, and other structures where the beauty of the wood should be as strong as the craftsmanship. In fact, any yacht or boat you see with a wooden deck is most likely made of teak.

So why choose this material? It has a beautiful natural honey golden hue, but more importantly, it is renowned for its high resistance to rot, pests (insects, termites and worms) and fungi in both terrestrial and marine environments.
Teak is one of our favorite woods here at Brazilian Lumber , and these are the reasons that make it stand out from other woods:

items: Weather & water resistant
It has three main natural components that give it special properties
Durability
Low maintenance
Versatility

blocks.text: 1. Teak Is Weather & Water Resistant

One of the most outstanding features of teak outdoor furniture is its ability to withstand any weather. It is one of the few woods in the world that contains a natural oil that repels water and prevents it from warping, cracking or becoming brittle and helps it withstand the harsh effects of torrential rains, heavy winter snowstorms and scorching sun.

It is not susceptible to significant swelling or shrinking with changes in humidity. Teak's oils make it weather resistant , for example its high silica content gives it slip resistance and durability. This makes it a good choice in wet environments or in areas where slipping can be very dangerous.
2. The Three Main Components Of Teak That Make It Water Resistant:

It contains three main components that make it unique: tectoquinone, rubber, and silica. The first is a type of natural pesticide that makes wood less attractive to parasites like termites, fungi, and ants.

The second substance acts like latex. On the one hand, it prevents the penetration of excess moisture and, on the other hand, it prevents the wood from drying out, keeping it lubricated and resistant to abrasion, which makes it very useful in the construction of wooden boats, pool decks and outdoor furniture.
Silica gives it strength and resilience, which helps it last longer than many other woods. Despite these properties, it also has lightness and flexibility, making it a favorite of many designers.
3. Durability Of Teak That Increases Its Water Resistance:

Durability and stability are other great properties of teak . As mentioned above, this tropical hardwood contains a large amount of silica that protects the wood from the elements and insects, ensuring that it will last for years to come.
4. Low Maintenance Of The Teak Due To Its Water Resistance:

Teak garden furniture needs neither paint nor varnish. Because of the wood's high oil content, this material takes on a beautiful, evenly colored patina that does not look uneven or dark. If you just want to bring out its luster, apply a natural teak sealer, if necessary.
5. The Versatility Of Teak Thanks To Its Water Resistance :
Because of its many good characteristics, teak has multiple uses. Here are some ideas:

items: Decking: Teak is known for its great durability and water resistance . This material is able to withstand bad weather and constant moisture, which made it a very durable and waterproof lumber. It has all the properties required for a long-lasting terrace.

Boat building: A boat must be in contact with salt water for a long time. In this case, teak is the perfect choice. This wood has a relatively low shrinkage rate, so it changes very little even after prolonged exposure to water and sunlight. Thanks to its excellent properties, it is a good choice for boat builders.

Furniture: Teak is relatively easy to work with and very versatile. Tables, benches, shelves, chairs and loungers can be made from teak. Depending on the style of furniture and individual preferences, it can also be left natural, lacquered, stained, waxed, or varnished.

posts.title: 5 Amazing Features Of Cumaru Lumber
posts.h1: 5 Amazing Features Of Cumaru Lumber

blocks.text: Cumaru lumber or Brazilian Teak , as it is also called, is a beautiful wood that is found in the tropical environment and grows in the dense forests of Brazil. The wood is rated very high in terms of durability, workability, and quality

In addition, it is considered one of the best hardwoods for outdoor projects such as patios, exterior walls, fences, and more. Also, it can last for decades due to its resistance to insect infestation, mold, water, fire, or rot damage.
Below, the Brazilian Lumber team shares a list of the top 5 characteristics of Cumaru lumber:

items: Hardness
Rot resistant
Durability
Environmentally Friendly
Preserves its natural beauty

blocks.text: 1. Hardness Of Cumaru Lumber:

This hardwood has a Janka hardness of 3,330 lbf . The Janka hardness test is called the "high heel test". This consists of subjecting a 0.444-inch steel ball to enough pressure to be half-buried in a piece of wood. It is incredibly difficult, requiring over 3,000 pounds of pressure per square inch!
2. Rot Resistance Of Cumaru Lumber:
The wood is classified as very durable due to properties that make it resistant to rot, insect damage, and weathering.

In addition, this tropical hardwood is less prone to cracking and splitting due to moisture and inclement weather, making it ideal for exterior decks. Also, Cumaru lumber is too dense and tough for pests that could get into it, minimizing routine maintenance .
3. Cumaru Lumber Is A Dense And Durable Building Material:

When it comes to protecting the exterior of your home, Cumaru lumber is one of the best solutions. This hardwood will stand the test of time and harsh weather conditions thanks to its extraordinary properties.
4. Cumaru Lumber Is Ecological :
No pesticides or plastics are used in the production of this wood, so it is 100% environmentally friendly.
5. The Natural Beauty Of Cumaru Lumber:

Its beautiful appearance is given by its color, a medium to dark brown, sometimes with a reddish or purple tinge. Some pieces may have streaks of yellowish or greenish brown and over time naturally take on a nice silvery color.

Whether for a residential or commercial outdoor project, Cumaru lumber is an excellent choice for decking. Cumaru's incredible density, strength, durability, and toughness are four main characteristics where this amazing lumber has earned very good comparisons to Ipe lumber.
Just like Ipe, Cumaru has an A1 fire rating, it does not scratch or splinter easily, it does not heat up in the sun, and has a high coefficient of friction, making it perfect for outdoor use.
To sum up, Cumaru lumber is extremely strong, hard, and works well for a variety of uses such as flooring, cabinets, furniture, heavy construction, decks, cladding etc.
Its quality and remarkable features make it comparable to Ipe. For example, both are notable types of high density hardwood decking and siding, long life, and strong resistance to external factors.

posts.title: The 4 Best Decking Fasteners And Their Use
posts.h1: The 4 Best Decking Fasteners And Their Use

blocks.text: One of the most functional outdoor features is a beautiful deck. It becomes a gathering space for friends and family to create wonderful memories together outside. Once the type of decking fasteners is chosen, the method of installation should be decided upon. Just as there are many options of decking materials, so too are there many options of installation methods. The decking material chosen will determine whether one can use nails, hidden fasteners , deck plugs, decking clips, or stainless steel screws .

Now, it is important to specify two things: First, when working with tropical hardwoods, pre-drilling is mandatory, due to the hardness and density of the wood. Second, to fasten the wooden board, screws are always a must.
But this is just a preview of information regarding the installation part, for now we will focus only on the materials and their individual characteristics.

In addition to the size, shape, and color of the new outdoor area, another important decision to make is whether to fasten the deck to its structure with visible stainless steel screws or coated with plugs, or with hidden fasteners.
Here at Brazilian Lumber , we share what we consider to be the 4 best decking fasteners, as well as their features and the variety of alternatives they offer:

items: Stainless Steel Screws
Hidden Deck Fasteners
Coated Steel Screws
Fasteners for composite decking

blocks.text: 1.Decking Fasteners: Stainless Steel Screws 5 Main Features

Fastening the decking to the substructure with screws has long been the preferred method. Not only is it a fairly simple and straightforward process for wood and composite decking, but screws also provide a strong and secure connection for fastening wooden boards, as well as being a cost-effective option.
They are preferred to nails because they do not rot or discolor wood, and the screw thread mechanics provide much greater holding power than nails. This is in addition to their durability.
The screw heads come in a variety of colors so that they can easily be matched to the hardwood or composite decking being used.

Stainless steel screws are one option, or coated steel screws can also be used. Therefore, holes for these screws should be pre-drilled when installing high quality hardwood products such as: Ipe, Cumaru, Tigerwood, Jatoba, and others.
Here at Brazilian Lumber, we have many options of stainless steel screws, such as:

items: The DeckWise Bugle-Head Deck Screws : Available in 305 Grade stainless steel for decking, use for optimum performance with hardwoods, thermally modified softwoods, PT softwoods, and composite decking materials. Pre-drilling is not required except for exotic hardwoods.

The DeckWise Self-Tapping Metal Joist Deck Screw is designed explicitly for metal joist applications. It can be used to attach most types of decking materials such as hardwoods, heat-treated lumber, softwoods, composite, and PVC.

blocks.text: To sum up, these are the reasons why some people prefer stainless steel screws for decking:

items: Easy installation at a low cost
Strong and secure bond
Functional and strong construction with deeply recessed star drive head to prevent slipping
Reverse threading to avoid mold and surface defects
High holding power

blocks.text: If aesthetically you would prefer not to have visible screws, here are two solutions for you:

items: Our line of 3 Signature Colormatch painted heads : Hardwood Brown, Cedar, and Outdoor Grey to match your decking material, plus a general purpose unpainted stainless steel head.
The Master Plug Kit offers four species of hardwood plugs (plain or our grooved Extreme Plugs). Their function is to be placed over the screw so that it is hidden, making the board seamless.

blocks.text: They are made from real hardwood and tapered for easy installation; builders can perfectly blend into the rich tones of Cumaru, Garapa, or Ipe.
2.Decking Fasteners: The 5 Most Important Aspects Of Hidden Fasteners
Some hidden deck fasteners, such as the Ipe Clip and Deck Clip, are also very popular because your deck can be built without visible screws on the top of the boards.
The screws are visible looking down between the cracks in the boards, but hidden fasteners are much less visible than boards screwed on the front.
Also, there is the idea that with the use of hidden decking fasteners, a truly barefoot-friendly space is created, with a clean and smooth surface.
To use them, each wooden board is fixed to a clip, achieving a faster, easier, and more flexible method of assembly.
In summary, these are the properties that make hidden decking fasteners stand out from other materials:

items: A seamless finish with no visible fasteners elements
Pre-assembled clip enables quick and easy installation
Easy removal of the boards if necessary (even in the middle of your deck)
Great holding power thanks to the serrated edges on the clip
Consistent board spacing along the deck

blocks.text: Here at Brazilian Lumber, we have some marvelous hidden fasteners options:

UV resistantç

blocks.text: 3.Decking Fasteners: Coated Steel Screws
They can be installed without pre-drilling holes, have superior holding power over nails, and cost less than stainless steel screws.
Many prefer to drill a pilot hole when installing very hard Brazilian Cumaru and Ipe decking that makes screwing easier, but the strength of these screws is still a useful feature.
4.Decking Fasteners For Composite Structures

Regular deck screws are made to go through pressure treated wood only . Composite materials are much denser, so it can be difficult to drive a normal screw through them, and pre-drilling may be necessary before the screws can be inserted.
Alternative deck materials such as PVC and wood-plastic composites are much more stable than wood and therefore don't need a large head to hold them together.
The smaller screw heads make the deck look much cleaner and elegant. But, this really depends on the brand and the products it offers.

posts.title: The 5 Best Types Of Lumber For Outdoor Projects
posts.h1: The 5 Best Types Of Lumber For Outdoor Projects

blocks.text: If you are looking for the best lumber options for outdoor projects, this is the right article for you. Ipe, Teak, Cumaru, Jatoba, and Garapa are the types of wood that come to mind when looking for a durable material that is resistant to weathering, rot, decay, and insect damage.
As if these incredible features weren't enough reason to choose them for outdoor projects, there's the natural beauty of lumber, as well as the warmth and comfort they bring to your home.

But not all types of lumber are suitable for outdoor projects, Ipe, Teak, Cumaru, Jatoba, and Garapa are tropical hardwoods that have special properties that make them the best alternatives for exteriors.
For example, they have natural barriers that prevent moisture, insects, and organisms from entering the wood, without the need for chemical treatment.
From an ecological point of view, wood is a perfect choice as long as it is harvested sustainably. As a natural product, it is not treated with any chemicals or harmful substances.

For our brand and company, sustainability is a very important aspect as it helps preserve the tropical forest, because the natural life cycle of each tree is respected. That is why the tropical rainforest preservation project has full support.
Now, back to the main point, here is a list of what the Brazilian Lumber team considers to be the 5 best types of lumber for outdoor projects:

items: Ipe
Teak
Cumaru
Jatoba
Garapa

blocks.text: Before giving all the information about these super-powerful tropical hardwoods, it is important to specify that they share many of the same properties, as these types of woods are the most resistant to external factors.
However, there is one aspect that sets them apart, and that is their Janka rating (a rating largely used by the wood flooring industry to compare the hardness of a floor):

items: Ipe: 3,510 lb
Cumaru: 3,330 lb
Jatoba; 2,690 lb
Garapa: 1,650 lb
Teak: 1,070 lb

blocks.text: 1 . The Superpower Of Ipe Lumber
Ipe lumber is a special and unique type of tropical hardwood found in South and Central America. It is much stronger and more weather resistant than many other decking wood options.
In addition, it has a natural dark red and brown color that many people like. Plus, it has the ability to naturally acquire a platinum color over the years.
It also resists movement, warping, cracking, rotting, and denting. Thanks to its oil content, it is also highly resistant to insects and fungi, making Ipe the ideal wood for outdoor applications.

It is often sold for decking due to its extreme weather resistance and density. Also, this lumber does not scratch or splinter easily, does not heat up in the sun, and has a high coefficient of friction.
These are the most important characteristics of Ipe:

items: Robust and durable: Ipe is one of the densest woods in the world due to its cell structure and the natural oils it is made of.
Low maintenance: Ipe wood decking is an easy-care surface. For added protection, it can be cleaned regularly, sanded to prevent fading, and oiled.
Non-slip surface
Not a heat absorbant surface

blocks.text: 2. Teak Is The King Of Waterproof Lumber

Burmese Teak is the most durable lumber for outdoor projects. It is extremely resistant to rot, which is why it is associated with boat building, is relatively dense and straight, will not warp or split over time, and has an attractive appearance.
This lumber contains natural oils that repel some insects. In addition, it does not shrink or swell as much with changes in humidity as many other woods.
For maintenance, you have two alternatives: use teak oil to maintain its natural color, or let the sun's ultraviolet rays turn it gray.
Here is the list of the outstanding properties of teak:

items: Weather and water-resistant: The same resins and oils that protect against weathering also act as repellents against insects such as termites and marine borers.

blocks.text: The natural oils inside this wood help it to repel water and prevent it from warping, cracking or becoming brittle.

items: Easy to care for: Teak needs neither paint nor varnish. Due to its high oil content, teak acquires a beautiful patina of uniform color that does not look stained or black.
It lasts a lifetime: Some proof of the longevity of this lumber are the benches in England, which were made from dismantled teak ships.

blocks.text: 3. The Density And Resistance Of Cumaru Lumber

Cumaru lumber, also known as Brazilian Teak , is one of the densest hardwoods for exterior use after Ipe wood. It is resistant to mold and rot, so it is often used for patios, decks, railroad ties, and other purposes.
Like Ipe, Cumaru has an A1 fire rating, does not scratch or splinter easily, does not heat up in the sun, and has a high coefficient of friction.
It's a perfect example of how to give your home a beautiful look when it comes to installing a deck or a wall cladding.
The main characteristics of Cumaru lumber are:

items: Dense and durable: Due to its resistance properties, it can withstand harsh weather conditions and does not require much maintenance.
High fire rating: Same as the Ipe, you can use Cumaru for cladding on the exterior walls of your home to create a great visual appearance and avoid the risk of fire damage.
Environmentally friendly: No pesticides or plastics are used in the production of this lumber, which makes it 100% non-polluting.

blocks.text: 4. Insect Resistance Of Jatoba Lumber
Jatoba lumber is an incredibly strong wood known for its resistance to termites and most insects. It is commonly known as the Brazilian cherry because of its color similarity to the native cherry.
This tropical hardwood is very popular for flooring due to its extreme hardness and resistance, especially in high traffic areas.
It is clear that Jatoba lumber has many outstanding properties, but these two stand out the most:

items: Amazing properties: Very strong, tough, and resilient with high impact resistance.
Durability: Very resistant to termites and extremely resistant to preservatives.

blocks.text: 5. Garapa Lumber And Its Resistance To The Elements
Thanks to its robustness and resistance to extreme weather conditions, water, rot, and mold, Garapa lumber is one of the best woods for decking.
The natural properties of this lumber make it the perfect material to build a deck for a pool or hot tub without having to worry about frequent exposure to water.
The waterproof grain of Garapa lumber keeps moisture out, naturally preventing rot and creating a pool-ready surface.
Although there are many important aspects of Garapa lumber, these are the main ones:

items: No risk of splintering: With proper maintenance, Garapa will be less prone to rotting and splintering.
Low maintenance: By checking your deck regularly and keeping the surface free of debris, you won't have to worry about constant maintenance.

blocks.text: In conclusion, remember that when looking for a durable material that is resistant to weathering, rot, decay and insect damage, the above options are the best.

posts.title: 5 Reasons Ipe Is The Best Decking Material
posts.h1: 5 Reasons Ipe Is The Best Decking Material

blocks.text: Even though wood is not the only material used for decking, it is the most popular choice. There is a wide choice of lumber that can be used for deck building, depending on the weather conditions of where you live, how large a deck you want to build, and what your budget for the project is. You can always consider Ipe.

If you are looking for the best wood for deck building there is only one choice: IPE. Ipe or Brazilian walnut as it is sometimes called is the hardest tropical wood. It is used to make decks, siding, docks, and any other outdoor structure. And you can always find it at Brazilian Lumber.
Here are the top reasons why it is the best choice for deck building:
1. Ipe Lasts Over 50 Years
Ipe has been used in commercial boardwalks and decks that were installed more than 50 years ago - a testament to its longevity.

Because of its density (it sinks in water) ipe can withstand all types of threats such as extreme weather, sunshine and thanks to its high tannic acid content, it will not rot, mold, mildew, or be affected by insects.
I pe comes from the Amazon Rain Forest where it is constantly exposed to heavy rainfall and insects, so it has adapted over the years to become resistant to all those threats.
2. Ipe Is Eco-Friendly

The longevity of this wood is one of the reasons so many architects and designers choose ipe. As a long-lasting material, it will not need to be replaced. Also, it is naturally dense and resistant, which means that unlike softwoods or domestic wood, it does not need to be chemically treated to be preserved.
This material can be bought with chain of custody certification or The Forest Stewardship Council ( FSC ) certification to guarantee that the trees were responsibly sourced and harvested .

If you check out the CITES Appendices (the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora ), you will see that ipe is not on the list, nor is it listed by the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species.
3. Ipe Increases Home Value

An ipe deck will add extra space to a home and is an element of architectural interest that will increase the curb appeal of a home. It will help extend the living area outside, creating an outdoor area for relaxation or entertainment.

These decks are found in all mayor luxury resorts from the Maldives to the Turks and Caicos, any high-end beach resort will use ipe hardwood for its decks and boardwalks. Any world traveler will instantly recognize this deck, which will give your home an immediate tone of wealth. High end guests who see these materials associate it with luxury and opulence.
4. Safe Against Weather Exposure

Safety is important when it comes to decking materials because they are more exposed to the elements than indoor items. This wood the same fire rating as concrete or steel, which makes it a very safe in case of a grilling or smoking accident.

Also, this material does not crack or splinters over the years, which means it is safe for bare feet to walk on. Another great feature, especially for feet, is that unlike PVC or Composite Decking, this wood does not absorb the sun's heat and so it will not scald bare feet.
5. Ipe Comes In All Different Lengths And Sizes
If you buy Composite Decking or PVC you will only be able to work with certain board lengths. With this wood, you have a choice of board length, width, and thickness.

Many carpenters and deck installers complain that they are limited when they have to work with composite decking because it does not generally cut well or can lose its guarantee if cut. Different facia boards have to be purchased. By contrast, this wood comes in all sizes imaginable, and can be milled to any specifications.
Quite simply, Brazilian ipe look is the best type of wood for decking. Considering the wood's building qualities and the prestige it gives to any space, it is a choice product.

posts.title: 7 Best Features Of Garapa Lumber
posts.h1: 7 Best Features Of Garapa Lumber

blocks.text: Garapa lumber is one of the best woods for decking . The workability of this tropical hardwood goes beyond words. Due to its robustness and resistance to extreme weather conditions, it can be used for any type of outdoor construction.

In addition, this hardwood is resistant to water, rot, and mildew. It is widely used in decking, siding, and floors with heavy foot traffic. Plus, its beautiful golden tones enrich the project with a warm atmosphere and a natural look.

However, it is true that there are some good tropical hardwoods alternatives when it comes to building a deck, such as Ipe , Cumaru or Jatoba . They are all beautiful, dense and durable options, so it can be difficult to decide which one is best for the project.

In the last few years, Garapa lumber has rapidly gained popularity with homeowners. Why? Here at Brazilian Lumber we share with you what we believe are the 7 reasons that make this tropical hardwood, also known as Brazilian Ash, stand out from the crowd:

items: Fiber bending strength
Density
Low maintenance
Lower price than Ipe
Resistance to rot, decay, and insects
Variety in color
Fire safety rating

blocks.text: 1. The Fiber Bending Strength Of Garapa Lumber
Instagram photo from @mgcdeks
The Garapa deck has a flexural strength of 12,900 psi. This means that this wood spans greater distances with very little deflection. With less deflection, deck boards gain more stability.
In addition, Garapa lumber has a Janka hardness of 1650 lbf (7,350 N) , which is also another aspect that proves its high quality.
The quality of this wood is sometimes compared to more popular ones such as cedar, redwood or pine.

The deck is designed to last, and the need for the best quality is emphasized by the fact that items placed outdoors are not only exposed to the harshest conditions, but also to the roughest handling.
2. The Density Of Garapa Lumber

Garapa lumber has a high density, which makes it inherently resistant to pests and rot. Therefore, it is an excellent choice if you are looking to build a permanent, beautiful, and long-lasting outdoor deck or structure.
You may not think a floor is dangerous, but from splinters to slips and falls, accidents can happen on a surface with imperfections.
Water, dirt and insects can weaken wooden boards over time and cause them to rot. The last thing you want to do is find out by sticking your foot through the rotting board.

Using Garapa lumber for your outdoor projects can help reduce these hazards. Garapa, like other high quality hardwoods, is less prone to splintering than properly cared-for softwoods. And because it's rot-resistant, it tends to be more durable.
3. Garapa Lumber Is A Low Maintenance Material

Another benefit of using Garapa lumber is that you don't have to spend a lot of time looking after it. Hardwoods are usually very easy to care for. Most of the time, all they need is a little soap and water to keep them in top condition.

Here's an important tip: Garapa decking should be swept up as needed to remove dirt and grime for optimal appearance. As for maintenance, this wood can be left alone to weather naturally, or it can be oiled.

Just keep in mind that the density of the Garapa makes it difficult for the wood to properly absorb some oil-based products. For best results, always test products on a small area of ​​your deck before finishing the entire surface.
4. Garapa Lumber Is Resistant To Rot, Decay, And Insects

When choosing a material for an outdoor project, you need to get something that will withstand the elements. For example, if you are building near a pool or hot tub, you should also consider frequent exposure to water.

The waterproof grain of Garapa lumber keeps moisture out, naturally prevents rot and decay, and creates a pool-friendly surface . The density of this wood also keeps hungry insects like termites out, which prolongs the life of your deck.
5. Garapa Lumber And Its Variety In Color
If you want to improve the exterior of your home, Garapa lumber will help you with that. Thanks to its red-brown hues, the golden color of Garapa has gained popularity in modern architecture.

Blonde, yellow, and honey, are other words commonly used to describe the shades of Garapa. But whatever the name, there's no doubt that the rich, bright color of this tropical hardwood is breathtaking.
If left in the open air, Garapa naturally acquires a soft silvery-platinum tone, very similar to the appearance of weathered Ipe wood.

Nothing could be more pleasant than spending the afternoons on a deck with perfectly sawn and machined surfaces, such as Garapa lumber. The combination of color, texture and grain make it a noble wood that stands out from the rest.
6. Garapa Lumber Has A Lower Price Than Ipe
While any hardwood would make a great deck, homeowners love the fact that Garapa is one of the cheapest hardwoods out there.

Although Ipe is the king of density and durability, Garapa is not far behind. For one thing, it's still a lot harder than softwoods like cedar and pine. And like Ipe, Garapa offers rot and insect resistance, and a high quality appearance at a fraction of the cost.
7. Garapa Lumber Has The Same Fire-Safety Rating As Ipe

While some people think of wood as a flammable material, Garapa actually has a reputation for being fire-resistant. With a Class A fire rating, equal to Ipe, Garapa is in the same category as steel, brick, and concrete.

This does not mean that Garapa is 100% fire-resistant, but it does mean that fire spreads much more slowly across the surface of this material. This should give you some security when grilling on your deck.
There you have it. With Garapa lumber you get: high quality, a beautiful and long-lasting material, and safety all in one.

posts.title: 3 Best Facts About The Use Of Cumaru Wood In Jamaica
posts.h1: 3 Best Facts About The Use Of Cumaru Wood In Jamaica

blocks.text: For many commercial and high-end residential decking projects, hardwood species have been the optimal selection. However, have you heard about Cumaru Wood? It's quite common for you to hear from homeowners and customers who have hardwood decks to sing their praises about the hardwood deck's significant strength, exceptional durability and unique aesthetics. One type of wood commonly used for hardwood decks is Cumaru Wood and it's one of the more popular lumber deck materials recommended and favored by professional woodworkers.
What Is Cumaru Wood?

Cumaru is also known as Golden Teak or Brazilian Teak. This Brazilian lumber is naturally durable and has a density close to Ipe. It's moderate cost and consistent golden brown color make it an appealing alternative to the other more costly hardwoods such as Ipe or Teak. Cumaru is resistant to decay and rot, which makes it an outstanding option for exterior applications like decking. It not only is as beautiful as an indoor hardwood, but it also lasts a long time. In fact, it outlasts many of the other favored wood decking species like:

items: Cedar
Pine
Fir
Douglas
Redwood

blocks.text: How Cumaru Wood Is Used in Jamaica

Cumaru is almost three times harder than Oak and is the second hardest type of Brazilian hardwood. It'a a more economical option for exterior decking than Ipe hardwood, while still keeping its premium quality.

Because of Cumaru wood's high durability and economical price, it's well-suited for high traffic decks and major commercial developments. It's also a smart option for residential decking projects since it comes with a 50+ year life expectancy and is resistant to:

items: Mildew
Mold
Decay
Insects

blocks.text: You can use Cumaru timer for things like:

items: Cabinetry
Decking
Flooring
Docks
Heavy construction
Furniture
Bearings
Railroad ties
Hands
Other turned objects

blocks.text: You can use it whenever you require good weathering and rot resistance.
Things To Know About Cumaru Wood
A few things to know about Cumaru wood include:

items: Durability

blocks.text: Cumaru wood is extremely durable. The heartwood has been shown to be extremely durable in resistance in both white rot fungi and brown rot fungi.

items: Working Properties

blocks.text: It's hard to bore and saw. When there's no presence of severely interlocked grain, the wood will plane to smooth surfaces. Because of its oily nature and high density, the wood doesn't glue that well. It does screw and nail well and it will require pre-boring.

items: Seasoning

blocks.text: Cumaru is rated as simple to air-season and has a slight tendency to check. Drying is uniformly rapid and there's moderate warping.

Safety always comes first - this should go without saying. So, you'll always want to check and follow all local building codes. On the job, be sure to wear the proper safety equipment when you're working with hardwood, particularly safety goggles. Remember the significant weight of this wood when you lift Cumaru boards

Cumaru deck boards can be stored before installation either in a garage or away from direct sunlight. For Cumaru wood to acclimatize with its neighboring environment, you'll want to allow it to sit for a couple weeks before installation.

Periodically cleaning with a garden hose should be sufficient. Adding simple soap if needed is fine. If you're not familiar with the process, follow a professional decking cleaner's instructions. Just like you would care for Teak decking, with Cumaru decking, you should not use a pressure washer. High-pressure cleaners can create uneven surfaces and grooves by damaging the tearing and sanding Cumaru wood fibers.

posts.title: The Top 7 Decking Tools Every Professional Needs
posts.h1: The Top 7 Decking Tools Every Professional Needs

blocks.text: Having a proper installation process is key for great results when putting together a deck. And that's why we are thrilled to be an authorized DeckWise dealer, which allows us to offer the best decking tools on the market, with high quality, durability, and a wide variety.
Check out some of our products at Brazilian Lumber and learn more about their use:
1. Decking Tools: Hidden Fasteners

The purpose of hidden deck fasteners is to give the deck a seamless, uniform look with and clean lines . Unlike face screws, hidden fasteners are installed from the sides of the boars so they are less visible.

Another advantage of using the hidden fastener system is that they are less exposed to water and thus last longer. DeckWise® makes a great ipe hidden fastener called Ipe Clip ® which is made out of a malleable plastic polymer resin coating over a rigid stainless insert.

The advantage of using these special hidden fasteners is that they will not react to the wood or stain it should there be a lot of rain or wood expansion. Hidden fasteners come in three basic colors that are intended to camouflage them - brown, grey, black - in order to best match the exotic hardwood that is being installed.
2. Decking Tools: Stainless Steel Deck Screws

Ipe hardwood is often chosen because it is weather resistant, especially near the ocean. In order to maximize the length of the installed ipe it is important to use stainless steel screws. DeckWise® stainless steel screws for ipe hardwood come in 305 grade stainless steel and 316 grade stainless steel.

Depending on whether the ipe is installed near the ocean water or in the ocean water, the grade needs to be adjusted, with 305 grade stainless steel being installed near the water and 316 being able to be installed right on the water.

The length of the screws ranges from 1" to 3 1 / 8 " and the screw heads com in six different colors (Shadowline Black, Hardwood Brown, Stainless Steel, Cedar, Rosy Brown or Outdoor Grey). Stainless steel screws have to enter at least 1" into the deck frame. Usually 2" screws are used for 1x6 ipe deck boards and 2 1 / 2 " screws are used for 5/4x6 ipe deck boards.
3. Decking Tools: Hardwood Plugs

Each hardwood is unique, so thankfully deck plugs come in each type of exotic hardwoods. Most commonly used are ipe plugs and cumaru plugs. These hardwood plugs are placed into the small hole that exists when a screw is drilled into a deck board. A small amount of glue is placed in the hole, which is then plugged with the hardwood plug (it looks a little like a cork for a wine bottle, but much smaller). Then the plug is sanded to the level of the deck board so that the place of entry is virtually invisible.
4. Decking Tools: Waterproofing Tapes

This tape is placed over any wood flashing to create a waterproof barrier. WiseWrap ® JoistTape™ by DeckWise® ® is made of polyethylene and uses a rubberized asphalt mastic adhesive. It is very thin, approximately 37mm, which means it will not affect the deck measurements.

This added layer of protection help guarantee the frame of the deck and prevents wood rot and decay caused by trapped water or heavy rain season. Each roll measures 3" wide by 75' feet long and specs out at 35-40 mil thick. Easily apply to decking joists, around deck support posts and over ledger boards.

For wooden posts that go directly into the ground, WiseWrap ® LedgerTape™ by DeckWise® ® is recommended. Made out of the same flexible polyethylene material, this self-adhesive can be easily wrapped around in-ground wood creating a nice barrier against moisture from the soil and fungi.
5. Decking Tools: Deck Board Straightening Tools

One of the most important things for the aesthetics of a deck is that the boards are lain straight and are spaced out evenly. DeckWise® ® makes a Hardwood Wrench™ which is designed to bend any warped hardwood board. It has eight times the bending power of other tools, with a push force of about 1100 lbs. It is attached to the joist and then it has a handle that is rotated to straighten the deck board, which is then cam locked into place while the fastener is installed.
6. Decking Tools: Deck Spacers

posts.title: The 4 Reasons That Make Composite Decking A Great Choice
posts.h1: The 4 Reasons That Make Composite Decking A Great Choice

blocks.text: More durability, low maintenance, better workability and greater resistance to the elements are some benefits of choosing composite decking for your projects.
Although there is a fear that composite decking may not be as nice and organic-looking as natural wood , thanks to modern technology, that is no longer an issue.
Composite decking is the fastest growing alternative to wood decking on the market. Its major advantage is that it has a core and cover that makes it resistant to moisture, weathering, and fading.

Wood-plastic composite decks, invented around the 1980s, consist of wood fibers coated with plastic. Both the plastic and wood used are often made from recycled materials, making composite decking an environmentally friendly option.
In addition, this material is free from the pesticides and other harmful chemicals commonly used in the creation and maintenance of wood decking.

That's why the Brazilian Lumber team is pleased to share with you all the incredible options we offer as authorized distributors of Trex , Timbertch , Newtech Wood , Norx , Zuri , Azek , Endeck , and For Us Plastic Wood .
First, it is important to highlight the 4 reasons that make composite decking a great choice:

items: Superior durability
Ultra-low maintenance
Resistance to external factors
Cost-efficient

blocks.text: 1. The Superior Durability Of Composite Decking

It can last in optimum condition for many years. It withstands fading, scratches & mold, and does not rot, warp, crack, or splinter. Composite decking withstands harsh weather such as snow storms, hurricanes, and long hot summer days. Spilled food, falling grill utensils, and damp pots are no hazards to this material.
2. The Ultra-Low Maintenance Of Composite Decking

High-performance composites retain their beauty for decades with minimal maintenance. In fact, you'll never have to worry about sanding, staining, or painting. Just cleaning it with soap and water twice a year will be enough.

Since spills, splashes, and other mishaps are inevitable, it is extremely important to choose a cleaning compound that will ensure that the color will not fade. Therefore, your surface will continue to look as good as the day it was installed for years to come.
3. Composite Decking And Its Resistance To Weather, Insects, And Mold

For many homeowners, one of the main advantages of composite decking is the safety provided by the protective covers. Coated composite decking is much less susceptible to erosion, fading, and general degeneration than traditional wood for outdoors. Many of the composite brands that are available at Brazilian Lumber come with four-sided capping.
The capping provides excellent protection against moisture, keeps mold and mildew out of the frame, and leaves the surface intact.
4. Cost-efficient Composite Decking

Just like with most products, composite decking is available for every type of budget. When it comes to installation costs, most people will be surprised to learn that composite decks are actually cheaper to build in the long run. While they can be a little more expensive to buy, this material actually costs less when maintenance and durability are considered.
Reducing the amount of maintenance in your life is an added benefit of composite decking, as well as adding value to your home.

As mentioned above, here at Brazilian Lumber we offer many composite decking types and brands, including three-sided caps, four-sided caps, PVC as well as other alternatives.
