posts.title: Best 4 Tips To Keep Your Hardwood Deck Spotless
posts.h1: Best 4 Tips To Keep Your Hardwood Deck Spotless

blocks.text: You are doing things right if you have a hardwood deck in your backyard. Hardwoods are the perfect choice for outdoor projects; we tell you why in this article. Throughout history, wood has been the most widely used material in construction. Today, it is still the preferred choice for building a project due to its remarkable properties, especially when it comes to hardwoods .

At Brazilian Lumber , we are direct importers of the best tropical hardwoods in the world. Ipe , Cumaru , Garapa , Jatoba , and Tigerwood are the star products of our business, as they offer the highest quality and durability compared to other materials.

These five incredible tropical hardwoods have natural oils that make them impervious to almost anything. They are resistant to water, rot, insect damage, and mildew. Plus, they won't scratch or splinter and have a high coefficient of friction. Some are even resistant to fire and salt water and won't heat up in the sun.

All these great features are proof of the superior quality that characterizes them. But there is more. You may think these premium hardwoods require significant maintenance and care, but it is quite the opposite. These species are very low maintenance, so you won't need to invest a lot of time and money to keep your deck in optimal condition.

Nevertheless, giving it a little attention once in a while is a good thing. We are happy to share a basic, simple, and practical 4-step cleaning routine to help you keep your hardwood deck spotless. It is easy to follow, and you will only need to do it twice a year if you want to.
Before beginning the routine, picking up a sunny day is essential because your hardwood deck will need to dry properly.
Best 4-step Cleaning Routine For Your Hardwood Deck
1. Sweep Your Hardwood Deck
Even if you follow only some steps of the cleaning routine that we are about to share with you, we recommend sweeping your deck once a week to remove debris and prevent dirt from building up.

Use an outdoor broom and get rid of any debris that may block proper drainage and ventilation. Start by removing garden furniture from the surface. Next, examine the cracks for leaves or pine cones gathering between the boards. If dirt builds up, use a scraper or spatula to clean it. Instead of sweeping again, use a vacuum cleaner to remove dirt. After vacuuming, take your garden hose and rinse the deck.

If old foliage is in between the deck boards, make sure to remove it. Debris in these areas can cause problems on any surface. You may need to use water, a brush, and mild dish soap for those stains that are hard to remove.
We suggest preparing your own cleaning solution, as some soaps may be too strong for hardwood. Get the right mixture by mixing one gallon of warm water with one quart of powdered oxygen bleach.
2. Scrub And Wipe Your Hardwood Deck

For those stains that won't come out, scrub the boards gently using a brush with the homemade cleaning solution we recommended above. Then rinse the entire decking again to ensure no residue is left on the wood. Do not use a wire brush to clean stains because it will damage the deck boards and leave rough edges and splinters. Use a plastic bristle brush instead.
3. Wash Your Hardwood Deck And Let It Dry Properly

For more thorough cleaning, you can pressure wash your deck . Just keep in mind that most hardwoods cannot withstand pressures above 1200 psi. It is always good to pressure test an invisible corner of the wood.
Once the cover has been cleaned, and pressure washed, allow it to dry properly for at least 24 hours.
4. Oil Your Hardwood Deck To Keep Its Natural Color

After proper cleaning and complete drying, it is time to apply a hardwood oil base to prevent its natural color from fading. For sanding, you can use 220-grit sandpaper and then wipe the surface with a damp cloth or sponge. This will improve the texture and allow the hardwood to absorb the oil better. posts.title: How To Replace Hardwood Decking Boards: A Complete 9-Step Guide
posts.h1: How To Replace Hardwood Decking Boards: A Complete 9-Step Guide

blocks.text: If you are thinking of improving your deck -either because it's old or damaged or because you want to make renovations at home - here we bring you a DIY tutorial to replace hardwood decking boards by yourself without having to be an expert .
If you feel identified, this practical and easy guide is ideal for you. Keep reading!
IMPORTANT - always check the underlying deck structure to ensure it is safe. You want to check the hardware as well as the wood structure.
Time To Make Some Changes

Has your deck seen better days? The good news is that there is no need to build a whole new deck if all you have to do is replace a few deck boards . This complete tutorial will guide you step by step on how to replace hardwood decking boards at home.

Whether you have one bad deck board to replace or many, the process is the same. We'll show you how to save hundreds of dollars in lumber by splicing in boards instead of replacing the entire decking.
Knowing how to repair a hardwood floor plank can save you time and money and ultimately save your floor !
Say Hello To A Beautiful New Floor For Little Money

If you decide to replace your hardwood deck boards by yourself, congratulations! Doing that without being an expert can be a little intimidating, especially when the boards are installed using hidden deck fasteners .
Hidden deck fasteners are precise that, hidden. They are secured on timber planks' edges inside slot grooves and fastened through the plank into the sleeper below.
This uniqueness often tends to intimidate people from replacing damaged deck boards. The issue is how to remove a damaged plank when deck screws are hidden inside the fixing.
Replacing tongue-and-groove hardwood floorboards is easy with the right tools and a little know-how. Much of the work can be done in a day to make your floor look like new.
What You Might Need
This simple how-to tutorial will show you how to replace hardwood decking boards. So before getting started, pay attention to the materials you'll need for the process .
Beginner - but with some carpentry experience (knowing how to use the tools is key!)

items: Saw (circular or miter)
Drill
23-gauge pin nailer
Pry bar
Hardwood Deck Boards

blocks.text: Extra tools (not strictly necessary):

items: Hammer
Extension cord
Hearing protection
Jigsaw
Locking pliers
Safety Glasses
Sawhorses
Tape measure

blocks.text: STAGE 1: Preparation before installation
Step 1 - Stain and Finish the New Board to Match
We recommend doing this step first , but it's on you! Test some stain colors on new floorboards and apply some urethane. Once you find a good match, repeat that process on all boards for repair.
Pro-tip: Even when you use the same stain and finish, each board may look slightly different. Stain and finish several pieces and go with the best match.
Step 2 - Tape the Boundary Area
Inspect the damaged flooring plank and decide how much length to remove. Once you do that, place masking tape to define the boundary, using the replacement board as a guide.
Step 3 - Drill Relief Holes
Drill three 1/2 in. holes with a Forstner bit close to each end of the board you're removing. Don't try to get the holes ideally on the butt joint - about 1/8 in. away is fine.
STAGE 2: Cut and Replacing
Cut the damaged deck plank that needs to be replaced down the center. If tight, making two cuts can help you remove the center portion of the plank more easily.
Use a circular hand saw to cut down the center of the deck plank to be removed.
Pro-tip: While making these cuts, you may run into flooring staples or nails, so use a blade with carbide teeth designed for demolition.
To avoid cutting through the subfloor, set the saw blade at most 1/16 in. deeper than the thickness of the flooring.
Step 5 - Remove the Damaged Board

Remove the cut pieces with a small pry bar and unscrew the hidden deck fastener . Next, pull out the tongue-and-groove edges of the damaged board to remove side sections of plank (the side that the screw is running through may need to be pried out).

items: Remove the centerpiece that was cut in the previous step.
Remove side sections of the plank (the side that the screw is running through may need to be pried out).
If the screw breaks, pound flush into the sleeper with a hammer.

blocks.text: Step 6 - Cut the Replacement Board to Length
Cut the replacement piece to length with a miter saw. Make the cuts with a slight angle, so the piece will drop into place easier, creating a cleaner, tighter butt joint.
Spread glue on the tongues of the replacement piece and the adjacent board. Any wood glue will work.
STAGE 3: Installation of The New Deck
Step 8 - Install the New Board
Install a new deck screw at a 45° angle into the side groove where you removed the Ipe Clip® fastener.
Installing a board with a groove on just one side of the deck board is optimal in this step.
Tip : Position the new boards, so the growth rings cup down. For a spotless cut, identify the top side of the board, flip it over, and make the cut.
To get a tight joint between old and new boards, angle the jigsaw slightly when cutting out the bad board so the angle on the remaining deck board is longer at the top.
Step 9 - Secure the Repair
After gluing in the replacement board, add 23-gauge pins for peace of mind. Angle the gun slightly and drive in a nail every four inches.
Installing a board with a groove on just one side of the deck board is optimal in this step.
If installing a deck plank with side grooves on both sides of the deck board, make sure not to drive the fact-driven screw through the side groove. (That could crack the edge of the board.)
Cut out the bad pieces, so the splices are offset by at least one joint width, and new boards are at least two joist spaces wide. Staggered splices look better and make a stronger deck.
Removing the bad sections and making the splices work can be a bit of a puzzle, so get off on the right foot by marking the replacement boards before starting.
If you want a close match between old and new deck boards, you'll have to match the wood species. This is tricky because weathered deck boards look alike.
Remove a board, cut it with a circular saw, and smell the wood to identify the species.

Pressure-treated pine has a sweet smell, cedar has an aromatic fragrance, and redwood has a more intense aroma. Ask your lumberyard to cut a scrap from each species and match the smell to your own board.
Since you'll be cutting random-length replacement boards, buy the longest boards you can transport; they'll yield less waste.
Buy galvanized or stainless steel nails or screws long enough to penetrate the joints by at least 1-1/2. The length of the fasteners depends on the thickness of your decking.

posts.title: 7 Ways To Illuminate Your Outdoor Composite Decking
posts.h1: 7 Ways To Illuminate Your Outdoor Composite Decking

blocks.text: If you are looking for ways to embellish your patio so you can enjoy it to the highest at every time of the year, Brazilian Lumber brings you 7 amazing ideas to illuminate your outdoor composite decking .
You don't need much money, just a bit of creativity and the wish to enjoy stunning and bright nights outdoors with your loved ones.
Enjoy Your Patio With Our Tips To Add Light

Winter can be an easy excuse to take refuge inside your home and leave the patio of your dreams that you worked so hard to achieve. Nevertheless, cold weather can also be enjoyed outside with a good blanket, a cup of coffee or hot chocolate, a fire pit, and a beautiful illuminated outdoor composite deck .
Clever use of deck lighting means you'll enjoy your space throughout the year , regardless of the season.

Your decking area is as important as your indoor spaces . That being said, adding lighting to it is crucial, like the ones you would have inside your home. If you have a decking area, treat this space like another room and use it for entertaining, dining, and relaxing.
Why Composite Decking is A Great Choice

More durability, low maintenance, better workability , and greater resistance to the elements are some benefits of choosing composite decking for your projects, especially outdoor ones. Although there is a fear that composite decking may not be as nice and organic-looking as natural wood, thanks to modern technology, that is no longer an issue.

Composite decking is the fastest-growing alternative to wood decking on the market. Its major advantage is that it comes in a variety of colors, has an affordable price point, and can easily be installed.

Wood-plastic composite decks, invented around the 1980s, consist of wood fibers coated with plastic. Both the plastic and wood used are often made from recycled materials, making composite decking an environmentally friendly option .
In addition, this material is free from the pesticides and other harmful chemicals commonly used to create and maintain domestic (pine) wood decking.

That's why Brazilian Lumber is pleased to share with you all the incredible options we offer as authorized distributors of Trex , Timbertch , Newtech Wood , Norx , Zuri , Azek , Endeck , and For Us Plastic Wood .
Deck Lighting Ideas
If you already have a decked area, there's much you can do to refresh its lighting. For inspiration, we've compiled the best ways to bring a glow to your decked space . Take a look!

items: Spark up a fire pit for a warming glow.

blocks.text: Fire pits are one of many fantastic deck lighting ideas to illuminate your outdoor composite decking that makes an attractive feature for the garden. It'll give you extra warmth , allowing you to spend more time outside, and cast a lovely flickering glow .
Some options can also be used for cooking , so if you want to double up, ensure you find the best BBQ for your space.
Perhaps not the brightest light source, but it's the warmest and is undeniably beautiful ! A tall light will make a fabulous feature to any outdoor zone, creating a living room feel.
You can complement the fire pit with additional lightings, like the ones we will show you below.

items: Hang Festoon lights.

blocks.text: One of the most straightforward deck lighting ideas to illuminate your outdoor composite decking is to hang some festoon lights. Drape them from two anchor points , such as from the boughs of a tree. If you do not have a tree to hang them from, you can always add a pole to your fence in order to reach the height needed to hang lights.
Suppose your decked area is at the bottom of the garden and needs further illumination. In that case, you can introduce it with portable lanterns, candles, and solar-powered decorative lights.
This is a beautiful way to disguise or brighten deck rail ideas. Always an extra!

items: Carry a beautiful lantern everywhere you need it.

blocks.text: You'll be surprised by how much glow a handled hanging lantern will release . Genuine gas versions are rare, but you can readily pick up solar-powered ones or battery powered versions.
Remember that you can hang the lanterns, too! They'll look great in a mix of colors and positioned from an overhead pergola at varying heights.

items: Add lights to the underside of a patio umbrella.

blocks.text: If you're running short of places where you're going to hang lights - there's no nearby tree, fence, or another highpoint - this is your lifeboat.

Every outdoor space can have an umbrella or garden brolly; you can use yours to bring in those extra garden lighting ideas. Wrap exterior lights around its shaft and entwine them through the ribs and stretchers of its canopy.
Solar-powered or battery-operated, these are inexpensive and a great way to introduce lighting wherever you need them.
5. Install permanent downlights.
If your garden has an exterior brick wall - either the back of the house or as a boundary wall you can benefit by using it to mount permanent downlighters.
A professional electrician can install them and provide you with a switch inside your home to operate them.
A great idea is to mount them above a sofa or whatever seat you have against the wall, lighting the area for reading and relaxing as the night draws in. Also, look how pretty it looks!

items: Lighting along the deck edge.

blocks.text: Adding strip lighting or inserting permanent lights to your outdoor composite decking can create a focal point in certain spaces . Deck lighting is the perfect way to finish a decked area and allows for showcasing garden paths and frame zones in your outdoor space.

They can be inset into the tops of boards, or set into fascia boards to give an impactful finish. And strip lighting can be placed under an overhanging edge; these lights work best when illuminating steps and edges.

items: Hang solar-powered bulbs from trees.

blocks.text: You don't need to spend a fortune to illuminate your garden beautifully. There are plenty of affordable solar-powered or battery-operated lights available. These hanging solar-powered light bulbs are a fantastic example of an inexpensive deck lighting idea.

Whether in a string of multiple lights or single bulbs, hang them from the boughs of trees, along fence panels, or the struts of a garden pergola. How pretty would these look, hanging off a tree on a winter night?
If you liked the tip about lighting the plants, another good idea is to add push lights into flower pots!
What Is The Best Way To Light A Deck?
You can do plenty of things to light up an outdoor composite deck.

What's most important is you think about what you'll use the decking for and where . Sanel Konyar, the Interior Designer and Founder of Interior Kollection , recommends: "Aim your light carefully. If you wish to create feature lighting, you don't want the lights directed at eye level. You want to create a welcoming, soft ambiance, not make your guests feel as though they are under a spotlight beam."

"Low-level lighting is also great to create ambiance and can be used to guide guests along paths and steps. There are a vast array of solar lights that are perfect for this, and can be moved around to suit your needs and layout with ease, " Sanel resumes.
How Bright Should Deck Lights Be?
The beauty of decking lighting is that you can achieve a look that suits your decking needs .

When deciding how bright your lights should be or what color temperature to choose, check out local recommendations for your environment . For example, if you live near the beach where turtles nest, you should be sure to use red lights with a low visible light spectrum and special fixtures to shield as much light from the beach as possible.

Remember that the more bulbs you have, the brighter the illumination, so think about where you want the light to be positioned - festoon lights will spread light in smaller pockets of glow. In contrast, a spotlight or downlight will direct its glow more precisely.

For subtle, intimate lighting, you can use candles (faux are a great alternative to real flames), lanterns, or even a small fire or chimney. Sources of heat, such as fire pits, heaters, and tabletop fires, allow you to enjoy your garden comfortably when the temperature outside is not ideal. Plus, the flames provide beautiful and warm lighting for those dark evenings.
Play with your imagination and create the outdoor composite decking of your dreams .
Light Up the Night

Create a completely outdoor composite deck with the proper lighting. You can find the best decking lights for decks, porches, and railings in TimberTech and MoistureShield . They offer the perfect selection of complimentary outdoor composite deck lighting options to add ambiance, elegance, and safety to your outdoor environment.
Choose your favorite style and complete your deck design with the glowing ambiance of great lighting!
To sum up, lights for outdoor composite decking provide beautiful and plenty of alternatives suitable for all kinds of budgets .
And last but not least, remember that Brazilian Lumber is a dealer or distributor for many of the best brands . Hence, customers have plenty of options when shopping from us.

posts.title: Best 5 Uses Of Douglas Fir Wood
posts.h1: Best 5 Uses Of Douglas Fir Wood

blocks.text: Douglas Fir is one of the most versatile woods available. It is strong and durable , making it ideal for construction and furniture making . Douglas Fir Wood is also relatively lightweight and easy to work with , which makes it a popular choice for many woodworking projects.

In addition to its many practical applications, Douglas Fir Wood is also prized for its aesthetic value . The warm honey-colored wood is often used in interior design, and the unique grain pattern can add a touch of visual interest to any space.

Even though Douglas Fir Wood is a softwood, it has impressive strength . Some claim that this wood has the highest strength-to-weight ratio of any wood on the earth. That made it well known for its strength, beauty, and versatility .
What is Douglas Fir Wood?
Douglas Fir Wood comes from Douglas Fir trees , the Pseudotsuga menziesii , a native tree of North America.

The tree was first documented by David Douglas , a Scottish naturalist who discovered them on Vancouver Island and for whom the tree bears its name. He sent the seeds back to his homeland, where they took root and are one of the fast-growing timbers in the UK. You also find it in Australia, New Zealand, and South Africa .
Douglas Fir Characteristics
Douglas Fir Wood has characteristics that make it o ne of the most used varieties of wood for builders and artisans .
This softwood is also resistant to fungal and insect infestation and exhibits good natural durability when exposed to the elements.
Douglas Fir is a softwood with a hardness rating lower than many other kinds of wood, like hardwoods. Compared to others, it is more robust and more durable .

The color of Douglas Fir Wood ranges depending on where the wood is located inside the tree . This wood is white to light brown, and the heartwood has a reddish hue. Its color will change and become more muted and gray once exposed to sunlight.
Douglas Fir has a coarse grain and an open and porous texture. Preparing the wood before you finish is essential to achieve a good finish.
Sustainability of Douglas Fir Wood:

Douglas Fir trees are a sustainable resource for supplying lumber . They are fast-growing trees at 13-24 inches per year. These trees grow tall and survive for many years, meaning they can remove and store carbon from the air.
- Building and Construction;
- Parquet flooring, stairs, flooring;
- Interior Façade and wall paneling;
- Production of cellulose products, fibrous paneling, and plywood.

There is an ample supply of these trees, which comprise around 20% of America's softwood reserves . To ensure that you get your trees from a company with ethical practices, like Brazilian Lumber , make sure you look for certifications that check their practices.
Best 5 Uses Of Douglas Fir Wood
Douglas Fir Wood is versatile in many home design types , from contemporary to rustic. Some of the best uses of this softwood are:
1. Flooring

There are many reasons why Douglas Fir Wood is such a popular choice for flooring. First, it's an incredibly durable wood , making it withstand a lot of wear and tear. It's also resistant to insect damage and rot , making it ideal for use in areas with a moisture risk.

Douglas Fir is also easy to acquire , so it's often more affordable than other types of hardwood flooring, while its wide boards and light color give a room a spacious feel and the right touch of light in it.
2. Doors and Windows Frames

Douglas Fir is used for doors and windows because it is strong and durable . It can resist changes in temperature and humidity , which means it won't warp or swell like other materials. Additionally, it is easy to work with and accepts a variety of finishes .
These features make it an ideal choice for interior applications . Doors and windows are two essential elements in a home, so choosing a material that will provide both beauty and function is vital.
3. Trim and Joinery
This is an excellent option if you're looking for a versatile wood for trim and joinery work. It's strong and durable, yet it can be sawed and nailed easily .
Douglas Fir Wood also holds paint and stain well, so it's a good choice for finishing projects . With a bit of care, this wood can help you create beautiful works that will last for years .
4. Furniture Making

Typically, hardwoods are the best choice for furniture making, primarily because of their sturdiness. However, softwoods like this also give an excellent output in furniture making because they are more malleable and thus easier to work with.
This might be because it is almost as robust as the hardwoods or because of its vertical grain length . The wood's smooth, sleek, attractive finish is also a plus.
5. Boat Making
The notable strength of Douglas-fir prevents it from warping or buckling . This is one of the features required in boat building materials.
Also, Douglas-fir was one of the woods used in making wooden ships, specifically the minesweepers used by the US Navy.
Wrapping up: Use More Douglas-Fir Wood!

In conclusion, Douglas Fir is one of North America's most plentiful types of wood . It is not as hard as Ipe or Cumaru, but it has a higher weight-to-strength ratio than any other and is an excellent construction material . It also has an even wood grain, making it versatile and flexible for different projects.
So, if you're looking for high-quality, durable wood for your next home improvement project, now you know about the Douglas Fir benefits .
At Brazilian Lumber, we can help you select the perfect wood. Contact us today!

posts.title: The 5 Most Beautiful Exteriors Made Of Silver Ipe
posts.h1: The 5 Most Beautiful Exteriors Made Of Silver Ipe

blocks.text: Undoubtedly, Ipe is one of the best woods in town for any decking project . This one-of-a-kind hardwood has some outstanding characteristics and even more unique natural properties , reaching a beautiful silver color when exposed to the sun without oils or varnish.
This Silver Ipe is as hard as it is beautiful, making it the number one choice for your project.
Introduction To Silver Ipe
You've probably heard of Ipe wood, but in case you haven't, we will give you more insight about it in this blog.
Ipe is a type of hardwood that is native to Central and South America. It's a highly dense wood, making it strong and durable.

Ipe is a beautiful wood that reaches its incredible natural silver color when exposed to the sun without oils. So if you're looking for a durable, attractive, and low-maintenance decking material to complement any home, backyard, or deck, Ipe Silver is the best choice. And you can always find it at Brazilian Lumber .
How Can I Get A Silver Ipe?

Luckily, you don't have to do much. Of course, people looking for low-maintenance decking often want to know just how little work they can get away with. Because let's be honest: nobody builds a deck because they want to oil it yearly!
So what will happen to your brand-new Ipe deck if you never oil it?
An Ipe deck constantly exposed to the sun will change its natural color. If proper oil is not applied, your hardwood decking will take on a silvery tone , commonly known as silver patina.

The result of this contact with sun rays is the stunning Silver Ipe (also known as Ipe Silver-Gray Patina or Weathered Ipe). This can be a bonus for some people, as it also looks great with a platinum tone.
Most luxury resorts from the Maldives to the Turks and Caicos Islands take advantage of this color change to create unique, elegant spots, as we'll show you later.
In addition, this silver color is lighter, so it is even less heat-absorbent .
You might think that a hardwood with such remarkable characteristics would require special care, but it is the opposite. Silver Ipe will stay in perfect condition with no maintenance.
Un-Oiled Ipe Turns Silver
Oil indeed increases the Ipe's lifespan. But does letting Ipe turn gray makes it weaker?
Absolutely not! If you skip the maintenance, your Ipe deck will still last up to 50-75 years . So, you can relax knowing Silver Ipe isn't weaker than an oiled wood.
For proof, you need only look at the many large-scale, public projects using Silver Ipe decking. For instance, the Coney Island boardwalk used Ipe for 90 years and was never oiled.

In conclusion, if you don't oil your Ipe deck, it will turn gray, but it can always be sanded and oiled to get back to the original color. A weathered Silver Ipe deck will still give you decades of low-maintenance backyard fun!
(Coney Island Boardwalk made of Silver Ipe)
Here at Brazilian Lumber , we pride ourselves on having the best tropical hardwoods in the world, like Silver Ipe, which tops the list for its characteristics, quality, and beauty.
Why Ipe Is The Best Decking Material
Before pointing out a list of the most beautiful exteriors made of Silver Ipe, let us remind you of those extraordinary qualities that make it such a premium hardwood :

items: Ipe Is Weather & Water-Resistant

blocks.text: Ipe comes from the rainforest of the Americas, where it is exposed to a lot of rain and harsh sun. Thanks to its natural environment, it can withstand bad weather or other threats that surround it.

Its origin has made it the hardest and most durable wood in the world. Its density and natural oils make it impenetrable to almost everything. It also does not splinter or scratch easily and has a high coefficient of friction for safe use.

items: Ipe Does Not Heat Up In The Sun

blocks.text: Ipe's surface will not burn your feet (or paw!) How great is that? With Ipe, you get a material that always retains the cool factor throughout its surface.

items: The Longevity Of Ipe

blocks.text: Silver Ipe can last in perfect condition for more than 70 years! When it comes to longevity, this wood meets the highest and most exquisite expectations for any project you have in mind.

items: Ipe Is Free Of Chemicals

blocks.text: Ipe wood is completely natural and requires no chemical treatment or corrosive sanding process. This means that this hardwood doesn't emit harmful chemicals and doesn't become plastic waste after its useful life.

Its natural oils make it resistant to fungus, mildew, and insect damage. This is the most remarkable grace of Silver Ipe: it turns that beautiful color without effort on your part; it is its purest natural state. How lovely is that?

items: Silver Ipe Equals Luxury And Beauty

blocks.text: Many luxury resorts in the Caribbean take advantage of Ipe when it acquires a Silver Patina color when no oil is applied to preserve its natural color. Any world traveler instantly recognizes Silver Ipe, giving your home an immediate tone of wealth.

items: Ipe Is A Low-Maintenance Material

blocks.text: Sometimes, the worst thing about high-quality products is complicated and costly maintenance. With Silver Ipe, this is not an issue.
One of the best things about it is that it does not require a time-absorbing cleaning routine with expensive products to keep it in top condition. Regular cleaning and primary care are enough.
Best Projects Made Of Silver Ipe
Now that you know about Ipe Silver-Gray Patina (as it's also known), it's time to discover some of the many beautiful ways to apply it.
Silver Ipe will be eye-catching wherever you want to place it, from the stairs to the floor surrounding the pool, and will add a touch of luxury and beauty to your spaces .
Here Are The 5 Most Beautiful Stages Made Of Silver Ipe:

items: Pools

blocks.text: Ipe wood has natural slip resistance , which is why it is perfect for areas that constantly get wet , like pools. No slips or falls around Ipe.
Besides, Ipe decking is naturally beautiful with this beautiful silvery patina. This low-maintenance option works well and looks fantastic.
Can you imagine yourself by your pool having a drink and enjoying a beautiful sunny day or an unforgettable sunset? These examples of Silver Ipe applied to infinity pools might inspire you.

items: Boardwalks

blocks.text: As we mentioned, a great example of stages made from Silver Ipe is the Atlantic City and Coney Island Boardwalk.
Now declared an official landmark, it used Ipe for 90 years and was never oiled . The results? This beautiful and unique silver space.
Another outstanding example of a boardwalk made of Silver Ipe is the Ipe Boardwalk in Disney World:
Disney Boardwalk is a recreation of Coney Island and Atlantic City boardwalks from the start of the twentieth century and emits a sense of timelessness.
It is not strange to imagine why Disney would choose Silver Ipe to build its boardwalk: any Ipe's rigid and slip-resistant characteristics make it perfect for this type of use.

items: Docks and Floats:

blocks.text: The natural slip resistance of Ipe is significant in an area that constantly gets wet, like an Ipe dock, float, marina, or pier.
As an Ipe dock or float weathers, and ages in place, it develops this beautiful silvery patina.
Ipe is one of the few natural building materials that can withstand saltwater corrosion. Therefore, it is the preferred choice for seaside construction and wet environments.

items: Stairs and Multilevel Spaces

blocks.text: Here, you can see how a multilevel space can take on a completely different dimension, brighter and more luxurious, if you install Silver Ipe. If you don't have a big budget, you can start only with the stairs, and you will see how the space changes!

items: Floors For Balcony and Terraces

posts.title: The 4 Types of Fire Pits: What's The Best For You?
posts.h1: The 4 Types of Fire Pits: What's The Best For You?

blocks.text: Who doesn't love being around a warm campfire? It adds comfort and ambiance to any space where family and friends can gather to cook a delicious meal , roast marshmallows, and tell stories. A fire pit is also a great addition to your backyard , whether for decoration or to make it more livable on cold days.

If you are considering buying a fire pit, you have probably found many different options. The secret is doing a little research before purchasing one to ensure you get a design that suits your needs .
There are 4 types of fire pits: wood-burning fire pits, natural gas fire pits, and gel-fuel fire pits , and these are categorized by the type of fuel they use.
In this article, we'll dive into each type of fire pit one by one, discussing their features, pros, and cons. Keep reading!

It's easy to see the benefits of sprucing up your outdoor space with a fire pit. They serve as an endless source of entertainment, illuminate outdoor living spaces after dark, offer warmth, and bring an inviting, cozy ambiance .
(Bonus: you can cook s'mores!)

But before you buy a fire pit, there are a few factors to consider. To make the best decision, consider where you'd like to put your fire pit . Keep in mind that it needs to be placed in an open area and a safe distance from your home (and any combustible materials).

Also, your fire pit size depends on how much space you have ​and​ how prominent a focal point you want it to be . Are you strictly installing a backyard fire pit as a warm central gathering area, or do you plan to use it for cooking? These details will help you decide which type and style would work best for you.
1. Wood Fire Pit

A wood-burning fire pit is like having a campfire at home and is highly popular for backyard setups. They provide warmth, the crackle of wood, and natural smoke, all while keeping the fire fully contained.

They are very easy to install. Besides, the enclosure for these fire pits can be made of any material that won't burn , like metal or stone. Furthermore, it will include a structure to contain the logs.

Wood fire pits can also double as a grill for those who enjoy making BBQs or cooking outdoors . Depending on your needs, the fire size can range from small to large by adding more logs for a larger fire. Cut firewood is inexpensive to buy, and you can't beat the authentic and cozy crackling that occurs when it burns.
Pros of Wood Burning Fire Pits:

items: It comes in various styles and sizes.
They can be placed anywhere due to their versatile sizes that go from compact to large.
They give a natural atmosphere of a traditional campfire.
Unlike others, a wood-burning fire pit allows you to cook over its fire.
They are budget-friendly: they don't cost you anything beyond the price of the structure itself.

blocks.text: Cons of Wood Burning Fire Pits:

items: You can't regulate the fire rapidly. Increasing the flame's size is easy by throwing in more wood. But, it becomes difficult to control the fire promptly.
Unlike gas-burning fire pits, you can't extinguish a wood-burning fire pit.
It produces big amounts of smoke that irritate your eyes, nose, and throat.
It requires more maintenance since the smoke and ash also discolored the pit.

blocks.text: Wood-burning fire pits come in a variety of different types, such as:
This type of wood-burning fire pit acts as a wood-burning grill, and many people use it for cooking and grilling. It comes with a grill gate that attaches above the flaming embers.
They can be portable or built-in designs. Either one will significantly enhance your patio. Outdoor fireplace design can be similar to an indoor fireplace.
This is a relatively easy, cost-effective DIY project. Brick or stone fire pits can be built using cinder blocks, stones, or bricks from almost any local hardware store.
2. Propane Fire Pits
Propane fire pits offer homeowners the ultimate convenience. They allow for a nice flame without needing a refilling gel or wood. Most propane fire pits are large and become the patio's focal point.
This fire pit can become your patio focal point thanks to its impressive design, which also gives a contemporary vibe.
A fire pit powered by liquid propane is more portable than natural gas since you can buy propane in refillable tanks. It also burns clean and bright and gives off considerable heat .
This fire pit is ideal for use under a gazebo, pergola, or outdoor structure.
Propane fire pits are most commonly constructed using glass, faux wood, copper bowls, and rock pebbles. Propane fire pits can also be fitted with wheels for mobility or cooking.
There are three kinds of propane fire pits are:
-Portable Propane Fire Pit:

A portable propane fire pit can be an excellent investment. It provides warmth, ambiance, and cooking capabilities, and it's also conveniently designed to move anywhere in your yard. You can find it in designs with wheels, while others are lightweight and easy to carry.
A propane copper design is one of the fanciest -and most expensive- options for an outdoor fire pit. Since copper has a very high melting point, it is highly durable and will last a long time.

Many propane fire pits have a table-like appearance, with a rim encircling the flames. This large ledge supplies a safe area for children not to get too near the fire. It is also handy for resting your drink or plate around the fire pit.
Pros of Propane Fire Pits:

items: These fire pits are portable and adaptable enough to be placed anywhere.
Unlike a wood-burning fire pit, you won't notice dirty ashes in or near the propane fire pit.
You also can use a fire pit table version during the hot months without using the fire pit.

blocks.text: Cons of Propane Fire Pits:

items: The maintenance and use of these fire pits become expensive due to tank refills.
They provide less warmth than a wood-burning fire pit can.

blocks.text: Propane fire pits can be a great choice if you are looking for contemporary and sophisticated designs for your backyard.
3. Gel Fuel Fire Pits

Gel-fueled fire pits are the perfect way to add ambiance and intrigue to your backyard if you desire a fireplace that does not give off any smoke. They are also highly versatile and can be moved almost anywhere in outdoor and indoor spaces.
Also, gel fuel fire pits don't require electricity, gas connections, or chimneys to operate correctly.

A gel fuel fire pit employs a special alcohol-based gel to torch a fire which renders an exquisite environment. To light this pit, you have to pour the gel fuel into the hole and then set the gel fuel on fire using a gas grill lighter. The fire puts itself out when the fuel is consumed entirely.
Here are a couple of different types of gel-fuel fire pits.

items: Gel Fueled Logs:

blocks.text: You can get gel-fueled logs to place in any fire pit design. They create a fire's natural look and feel while concealing the gel fuel holders inside the logs.

items: Tabletop Fireplace:

blocks.text: A gel-fueled tabletop display firepit is perfect for those who want a small fire in the backyard. These can be easily moved indoors or out and add an excellent display to the patio table.
You can buy beautiful tabletop firepits at The Outdoor Plus.
Pros of Gel Fuel Fire Pits:

items: They are easy to use.
You can use it inside as well as outside your home.
Safe to use inside the house.
It is an inexpensive option.
It doesn't provide any smoke.
The gel helps the fire burn for a few hours without hassle.

blocks.text: Cons of Gel Fuel Fire Pits:

items: The heat output is much less than a wood-burning fire pit.
You cannot regulate the flame levels.
The fuel or construction of this fire pit may cost you little, but refueling can cost you about $3 per hour if you are running a 3-can model with a gel fuel can.
You must refuel it more than once for the fire to keep burning for an entire night.

blocks.text: 4. Natural Gas Fire Pits
Consider a natural gas fire pit if your backyard can install a natural gas line. Similar to propane designs, this fire pit is a permanent fixture in your backyard.
One amazing thing about natural gas fire pits is that they never run out of fuel . In addition, gas is cleaner and safer than wood and doesn't bombard guests with smoke.
Here are a few different ways to design a natural gas fire pit:

items: Sunken Design:

blocks.text: A sunken natural gas fire pit is constructed into the patio or ground. You must be careful around these designs, as the flames are close.

items: Square, Round, or Tabletop Design:

blocks.text: Design your fire pit to be raised above the patio with stone, brick, or copper designs, among others. They make a lovely complement to the space.
Pros of Natural Gas Fire Pits:

items: It is an inexpensive choice.
It will add value to your house.
They are also expected to live for a few decades with little care, given their durability and robustness.
There is no mess to clean up.

posts.title: 12 Winter Deck Ideas to Enjoy Your Deck in The Winter
posts.h1: 12 Winter Deck Ideas to Enjoy Your Deck in The Winter

blocks.text: How do you enjoy your deck during the winter? As the days get shorter and the temperature decreases, you may be tempted to abandon your outdoor living area and switch your activities from outdoors to indoors.
But why waste valuable outdoor space? You can make the most of your outdoor deck in the winter by taking the proper steps.
How Can You Enjoy Your Deck In The Winter?

There are many ways to continue enjoying your deck all year round. With these winter deck ideas, and a little care and maintenance, you'll see how easy it can be to adapt your deck for the cold days and turn it into a cozy winter escape.
We've got plenty of ideas to inspire you, from twinkling lights, crackling fire, and stunning decorations to hot tubs. All are brought together to be enjoyed under fresh winter skies.
Here are 12 winter patio ideas to help you make the most of your outdoor deck in the winter!
12 Great Ways To Enjoy Your Deck In The Winter
1. Add A Heater To Your Outdoor Deck
Do you want to continue enjoying your outdoor space during the cold months? Then, consider installing patio heaters. This is an effective way to prepare your backyard for winter.
A heating element performs two main functions: keeping your space warm and creating an attractive focal point for your deck all year round.

Heaters are safe to use on your deck , but finding the correct type of heater that fits your unique needs is vital. Some heaters produce more heat, run for longer durations, or are more cost-effective than others.
There are several high-quality options available for outdoor heating sources. Take a look at these options and decide which one is right for your house and lifestyle:

-Outdoor Fireplace: An outdoor fireplace can be ideal if you have a large patio and love entertaining. It's a substantial investment, but once done, you and your loved ones will share numerous good times and delicious meals near the open flames. You can find it in several beautiful materials, such as brick, stone, and concrete. Check out the fantastic fire pits at the Heart Stone Outdoor and The Outdoor Plus . Pick your favorite!

-Chimney: If you want the look and feel of an outdoor fireplace, chimneys are a fantastic alternative. They come in various styles, from clay to steel, so you can easily find one that complements your outdoor deck in the winter.
-Heating Lamps: They are portable and bring a modern look to your patio. You can easily adjust the flame, so there is no need to worry about stoking the fire or adding more wood.

-Fire Pits: A fire pit table is an elegant, safe, and weather-resistant solution for getting warmth and enjoyment to your patio. Outdoor fire pits are also easy to clean and maintain, perfect for your busy schedule.
Check out this article to find out what fire pits exist so that you can choose the best for you!

-Stationary patio heaters: Deck heating systems can be powered by electricity, propane, or natural steam. They are installed in such a way that they are safe and practical for winter use and are never an eyesore in summer.
A permanent deck heater will cost less than other heaters and provide more deck comfort.

-Portable deck heaters: If you don't want to heat your backyard, you just need to warm yourself up. Then an infrared heater is perfect. Note that portable deck heaters require the use of infrared heating.
2. Invest in a Hot Tub
How do you use your deck in the winter? Nothing better than a hot tub!
A hot tub is a great patio addition that provides warmth and relaxation all year that can make a winter deck one of your favorite places to be.
They are a lovely way for you and your spouse to hop in and enjoy a romantic evening. It's also an excellent way to decompress when you come back home after a long day.
Even though they're nowhere near as big as a pool, hot tubs still require maintenance and cleaning, and possible permitting, so keep that in mind.
3. Patio Roofs or Enclosures

If you have a detached patio without a roof, consider installing a cover such as an awning . It can entice your family to stay outside when the sun falls and the temperature drops. Considering adding outdoor curtains or screens, if that's the case , you have the perfect recipe to create a beautiful, cozy oasis that provides privacy and protection.

Learning how to enclose a deck for winter is relatively simple because you have many options, including patio covers, vinyl covers, and canopies. With the proper selection, winter deck enclosures create a more protective and welcoming environment , delivering style and utility simultaneously.
In addition, deck enclosures used during winter can help trap the heat generated by heaters, improving their efficiency by keeping your deck cozy.
4. Light It Up

While fire pit tables and heat lamps provide illumination, more is needed to light up ample space. Adding outdoor lighting helps boost your patio's brightness and ambiance instantly, ready for you to stay outside and enjoy a fantastic night.

String lights are an inexpensive, easy-to-hang, and tried-and-true classic. On the other hand, recessed lights offer a sleek, clean look without clutter if you're tight on space. Suppose you want your lights to be the center of attention. In that case, an outdoor chandelier adds luxury and elegance to your patio.
There are several options for lighting . Remember that the right lights depend on factors like budget, style, and installation effort.
If you want to know more lighting choices, we leave you this article about 7 Amazing Ways To Illuminate Your Outdoor Composite Decking.
5. Keep It Cozy

Heat and light help get your family outside, but adding items and accessories that provide coziness and warmth will make them want to stay . You should treat your outdoor space as any indoor room , so include warm blankets and lovely all-weather pillows to keep things homey.
You can even lay down a soft, plush outdoor rug to keep everyone's feet warm and comfy.
6. Decorate Your Deck With Plants

A patio covered with plants is a fantastic way to get outside and provide natural beauty for your outdoor space . Contrary to what many may think, there are plenty of green and flowers that prosper well during the colder months .
But that isn't the only benefit that patio plants have. The right amount of greenery improves air quality, controls moisture, and blocks some winter elements . Not bad, right?

But before dressing your deck with plants, you should clean it up. Start by removing frost-killed plants or picking off damaged leaves and flowers. Cutting back plants will facilitate new development and flowering.
7. A Grill or Outdoor Kitchen

Who says summer is the only time to grill? Once you have excellent heating and lighting ready, why not fire up the grill and cook a nice and delicious meal for your loved ones? There's no winter-friendly meal other than good grilled pork chops or a BBQ, perfect for enjoying a cold-weather family dinner outside.
Consider an outdoor kitchen if you want to elevate your outdoor dining experience. It's a significant investment, but it's a perfect addition to your patio if you love cooking and entertaining.
8. Fun for The Kids

Getting your kids outside during the warmer months can be tricky, so it may be extra challenging to get them to come out during winter. Outdoor games are a good idea to get the little ones excited to be in the exterior.

A giant Jenga, Connect Four set, or even a telescope are beautiful ideas that you and your kids will love playing with. If you get a fire pit table, set up s'mores spread and enjoy roasting marshmallows over an open fire.
9. Outdoor Movie Theater

Family movie nights are always a great way to spend quality time together. But that doesn't mean that you have to limit your home theater experience indoors. You can have fantastic movie nights on your outdoor deck in the winter with the right equipment and setup .

If you're interested in an outdoor home theater, first, you want to decide if your space is better suited for an outdoor TV or a projector screen. TVs are recommended if your patio is smaller, while projector screens are better if you have a bigger space.
10. Decorate Your Deck
Decorations and accessories are not as essential as heat for your deck in the winter. Still, they are perfect for highlighting your unique style and personality.
Whether you prefer modern decor or rustic style, many accessories - such as coffee tables, planters, pillows, and tabletop decorations- can help make your patio lovely and comfortable .
11. High-Quality Outdoor Furniture
Whether it's summer or winter, you want to be as comfortable as possible with your patio. That's why you need high-quality outdoor furniture that resists the elements all year .

But before you pick out your furniture set, decide on your patio's primary purpose. A high-quality dining set will be perfect if you enjoy cooking. On the other hand, a lovely seating set will increase comfort and ease if you're using your patio for entertaining and lounging.

Apart from the style, having seasonally appropriate patio furniture can significantly benefit your deck's comfort. Some types of seating may supply more insulation from the cold or wind protection, which is why wood furniture is so famous for the outdoors. Even something as easy as adding furniture pillows can make a big difference to your deck in the winter.
12. Prepare Your Pergola For Winter

Cold weather is a great excuse to give your composite pergola a winter makeover and turn it into a warm corner this season. You can decorate it with nice lights , like oversized bulbs. Furthermore, you can add a touch of green to your deck in the winter with plants and flowers. You can hang winter baskets from the beams for extra color and place greenery inside the winter hanging baskets.

Occasional small tables can be decorated with potted plants or lanterns. Then, for an eye-catching focal point, add a portable fire pit. This will add visual and psychological comfort and a more intimate setting from which you and your guests will benefit.

posts.title: What Makes Platinum Garapa So Great? 7 Best Features
posts.h1: What Makes Platinum Garapa So Great? 7 Best Features

blocks.text: Are you thinking of starting a new wood project? You may be at a crossroads when choosing the best wood for your needs, being so many options in the market.

If you're debating the merits of the different hardwoods, consider Platinum Garapa . It's an excellent and versatile material, ideal to use for different types of projects , and it's also a budget-friendly alternative to IPE .

Platinum Garapa lumber is one of the best woods for decking , and it has a high level of workability . Besides, thanks to its robustness and resistance to extreme weather conditions , it can be used for any type of outdoor construction .

In addition, this hardwood is resistant to water, rot, and mildew . It is widely used in decking, siding, and floors with heavy foot traffic. Its beautiful golden tones enrich the project with a warm atmosphere and a natural look.
However, there are indeed some good tropical hardwood alternatives to building a deck, such as Ipe , Cumaru , or Jatoba .

Nevertheless, Platinum Garapa has rapidly gained popularity with homeowners in the last few years. Why? Here at Brazilian Lumber, we share with you what we believe are the 7 reasons that make Platinum Garapa so amazing.
Platinum Garapa Hardwood Facts
Garapa, also known as Brazilian Ash , is a tree that grows in Brazil, Venezuela, and other South American countries. The Garapa tree can grow up to 100 feet tall and has a diameter of five feet.

Platinum Garapa wood has a beautiful color ranging from light yellow to deep golden brown. Homeowners love the look of this popular wood, which can be used for siding, decking, fences, furniture, and many other projects.
Platinum Garapa is easy to work with , with its fine-to-medium texture and straight grain. This fantastic wood is also durable and resistant to pests and fungi.

At Brazilian Lumber , we highly recommend that if you work on a luxury project, you use Platinum Garapa. Why? Its incredible hardwood is , among other things, pretty lightweight compared to other woods, resistant, and easier to work with.
If you want to know more, check out this video we made!
But let's not get ahead of ourselves. Let's go into detail, one by one, of the 7 reasons why you should consider Garapa Platinum for your projects.
What Makes Platinum Garapa So Great? Its 7 Best Features
1. Garapa Lumber's Fiber Bending Strength
Platinum Garapa has a flexural strength of 12,900 psi, meaning that this wood spans greater distances with minimal deflection . With less deflection, deck boards are prone to be more stable.
The quality of Platinum Garapa is sometimes compared to more popular ones such as cedar, redwood, or pine.
2. Garapa Lumber's Density
Garapa is a durable hardwood with a 30+ year lifespan suitable for many applications , especially if you want to build a permanent, beautiful, and long-lasting outdoor deck or structure.
It has a Janka Hardness rating of 1,650 pounds. That is softer than other tropical hardwoods, like Ipe and Cumaru, but significantly harder than cedar.
This is also another aspect that proves its high quality.
Garapa Lumber's Density makes it resistant to damage, from splinters, slips, and falls to water, dirt, and insects . And because it's rot-resistant, it t ends to be more durable.
3. Garapa Lumber Is A Low-Maintenance Material

Another benefit of using Garapa hardwood -and probably the favorite of many- is that you don't have to spend much time caring for it . Hardwoods are usually very easy to maintain. Most of the time, they only need soap and water to keep them in perfect condition.
Bonus tip: Garapa decking should be swept up as needed to remove dirt for optimal appearance. As for maintenance, this wood can be left alone to weather naturally or be oiled.

Untreated Garapa will turn an attractive silver-gray color as it ages. Some people even prefer the weathered look! In this article , you can see how Ipe takes on a beautiful silver hue when left natural.
No coating or sealers need to be used if you appreciate this aging process. But you can always apply a UV inhibitor once a year to maintain its honey tone.
4. Garapa Lumber Is Naturally Resistant To Rot, Decay, And Insects

When selecting a material for an outdoor project, you must choose something that can resist the elements. For example, if you are building near a pool or hot tub, you'll also want to consider frequent water exposure.

Garapa lumber's waterproof grain keeps out moisture, prevents rot and decay, and creates a pool-friendly surface. Its density also keeps hungry insects like termites out, which prolongs your deck's life.
5. Garapa Comes in A Variety Of Beautiful Colors

If you're looking to upgrade your home's exterior, Platinum Garapa is a marvelous way to do it. While Ipe is beautiful in its way with its reddish-brown hues, Garapa's golden color has nothing to envy. This fantastic gold shade has gained popularity and is increasingly chosen in modern architecture.
Blonde, yellow, and honey are other words commonly used to describe its shades. But whatever the name, there's no doubt that Garapa's rich, bright color is breathtaking.
As we said before, if left in the open air, Garapa naturally acquires a soft silvery-platinum tone, similar to the appearance of weathered Ipe wood.
6. Garapa Lumber Has A Lower Price Than Ipe
While any hardwood would make a great deck, homeowners love that Garapa is one of the most budget-friendly hardwoods available.

Although Ipe is number 1 in dense and durable woods, Garapa is just a little behind. For starters, it's still much harder than softwoods like cedar and pine. And like Ipe, Garapa offers rot resistance, insect resistance, and a high-end look.
Wrapping Up: How Does Garapa Compare To Ipe?
While Ipe is still the most chosen option for those seeking the ultimate in durability, Platinum Garapa has many benefits:

items: Garapa is lighter than Ipe , so it's easier to manage the wood before construction.
Garapa is easier to work with than Ipe since it's easier.
Garapa is less expensive than Ipe .

blocks.text: So, when you buy Platinum Garapa, you are guaranteed the best product on the market. And you can always find it at the best price here, in Brazilian Lumber!
7. Garapa Lumber Has The Same Fire-Safety Rating As Ipe

While some think of wood as a flammable material, Garapa has a standing for being fire-resistant. With a Class A fire rating equal to Ipe, Garapa is in the same category as inorganic materials like steel, brick, and cement.
This does not mean that Garapa is entirely fireproof. Still, it does mean that fire spreads slowly across the materials' surface. This should give you some safety when grilling on your deck.
Conclusion
To wrap it up, Platinum Garapa decking offers a high-quality, beautiful, resistant, budget-friendly, and long-lasting material.
If you are interested in buying Garapa, come to Brazilian Lumber! Contact us by calling or email, or visit us in our warehouse in Miami or Los Angeles. We will be happy to help you.

posts.title: Hardwood VS Softwood: What's Best For You? 7 Differences
posts.h1: Hardwood VS Softwood: What's Best For You? 7 Differences

blocks.text: So, you have a wood project in mind. Where to start? The best thing to do is learn the differences between hardwood VS softwood so that you can choose the best for you . Here they go!
Different types of construction projects call for different kinds of wood. So choosing the appropriate lumber for the job is crucial to achieving satisfying results.
Determining whether a project demands hardwood or softwood is the first step in deciding what wood is best for the job.

But making the proper selection can be more complex than it sounds. Both types of wood can be used for everything, from structural to decorative. But what is the difference between hardwood and softwood?
This article is a guide that will make the decision process easier by breaking down the main differences between hardwood VS softwood.
Hardwood VS Softwood: The Difference
What Are Hardwoods?
Hardwoods come from trees categorized as Angiosperms , found in temperate and tropical forests worldwide . These trees reproduce with a flowering plant, like oak, walnut, and maple.
Hardwood is considered the ultimate versatile material , with applications ranging from exquisite veneers and furniture to musical instruments, flooring, construction, and boat building.
It is a material of natural beauty, available in countless species, specifications, and color combinations.
The most common types of hardwoods include :
What Are Softwoods?
Softwoods come from trees named Gymnosperm . These trees have needle-like leaves that usually remain green year-round, as opposed to broad leaves that shed annually.

Softwoods became trendy worldwide for their versatility of applications and remarkable aesthetic appeal. Softwood can be used in many projects - from furniture and flooring to decking, landscaping, joinery, and structural applications.

Softwoods are flexible, lighter, and less dense than most hardwoods. They also develop quickly, leading to lower cost levels. These features made them easier to manipulate and more readily available than hardwoods.
The most common types of softwoods include:
Hardwood VS Softwood: 7 Differences
1. Hardwood comes from deciduous trees, while softwood comes from coniferous.

First, let's start with the origin of both kinds of wood. Hardwood comes from Deciduous trees , which leaves change their color in the fall, die, and fall off, and then grow new leaves in the spring. They arise from enclosed seeds covered by a hard shell or fruit.

Instead, softwood comes from Coniferous trees . These trees are evergreens that keep their foliage, which consists of either scaly leaves or needles, all year round. Some famous examples of coniferous trees include pine, cedar, spruce, fir, and juniper.
2. Hardwood is stronger and more durable than softwood.

As you can imagine by the name, hardwoods are stronger and more hard-wearing than softwoods . This is because of their slower growth time and more complex, condensed structure, which results in greater density . Generally, higher density equals higher strength and durability.
Hardwoods better resist dents, divots, and scratches , so they can be ideal for construction projects that must endure significant abuse.
But that does not mean that softwoods are weak at all. In fact, pine is the most commonly used building material, making up most of the framing used in homes.
Because of their more complex structure, hardwoods generally perform better when exposed to the elements.
3. Hardwoods have a harder density than softwoods.

Most hardwoods are notably denser than softwoods , which makes them also heavier. The difference in density is primarily due to the structure of both kinds of wood. Softwood is considerably more porous than hardwood.

Having fewer pores help hardwood be structurally more robust and durable than softwood. It also makes hardwoods more water-resistant , as they have fewer holes in their structure to soak up water and moisture than more porous softwoods.
4. Hardwood is more fire-resistant than softwood.
Because of their lighter density, softwoods have more air pockets inside their wood fibers, allowing them to burn more easily. Hardwoods are denser and therefore burn less easily.

Hardwood's fire resistance, compared to softwoods, usually doesn't overshadow the difference in cost, which is why most homes' wood framing is made of softwood. Still, hardwood's fire resistance makes it ideal for applications with a greater fire risk.
5. Softwood is cheaper than hardwood.

The reason why softwood is cheaper than hardwoods is due mainly to the fact that pine trees are faster growing, easier to source, and as a result, more abundant. (In fact, it's telling that softwoods make up roughly 80 percent of the world's lumber.)

A pine tree can grow 2 feet or more in a year, while an oak tree will only grow about a foot per year. Pine trees can also produce more densely than hardwoods, allowing a timber company to harvest more softwood per acre than hardwood.
However, the cost of any given hardwood or softwood depends entirely on the product and species chosen and, of course, the required volume.
6. Hardwood VS Softwood: environmental impact and sustainability.
Both types of wood remove carbon dioxide and are 100% renewable. Nevertheless, softwood is usually the more environmentally-friendly option.
This is because softwood trees grow faster than hardwood ones, which means they can be replenished more quickly.
However, hardwoods can also be very kind to our planet by sourcing timber from sustainably-managed forests.
7. Hardwood VS Softwood: Different Uses

Wood from the trunk of any hardwood and softwood tree can be used for a large variety of projects. It's safe to say that wood is an incredibly versatile resource, but what are the differences in the uses of hardwood and softwood?
What Is Hardwood Used For?
Solid and durable hardwoods are the most chosen option for any high-impact structure, surface, or construction project intended to last a long time.
Some of the hardwood uses are:
-Construction (such as timber-framed buildings)
Some niche hardwood applications include guitars, smoking pipes, and walking sticks.
What Is Softwood Used For?

It's estimated that 80% of all wood consumed globally comes from softwood trees. Due to their less dense and hard-wearing nature, softwoods are usually employed for temporary, lower-impact construction, where time or budget may be limited.
Some of the softwood uses are:
-Building components, fixtures, and fittings
-Roof and inner wall structures
-Props and trusses in construction
Besides being easier to handle, softwood also takes finishes like paint and stain very well, making it popular for home woodworking.

posts.title: Top 4 Benefits of Installing Artificial Grass in Playgrounds and Children's Play Areas
posts.h1: Top 4 Benefits of Installing Artificial Grass in Playgrounds and Children's Play Areas

blocks.text: As playgrounds and children's play areas continue to gain popularity, more and more people are looking for ways to make them safer and more enjoyable . One way to do this is by installing artificial grass , which can offer many benefits over natural grass. This article will explore the benefits of artificial grass in playgrounds and children's play areas .

If you're a parent, you know just how important playgrounds are for kids. Children one year and up often use play areas for exploration, friend-making, games, and building gross motor skills such as climbing, jumping, and swinging. For these reasons, it's crucial for construction companies, city planners, and neighborhood committees to choose the right materials for the layout and composition of a playground.
As one of the most versatile outdoor materials on the market, turf is an excellent addition to any playground. Below are a few reasons to consider using turf in a playground design. Take a look!
Safety Benefits

When you're designing a space for kids, safety always comes first. Artificial turf looks and feels like natural grass but has outstanding perks, such as being water-resistant and wheelchair-accessible since it does not create muddy conditions. This creates more inclusive environments.

It also provides good traction to prevent unnecessary falls. Unlike dirt, wood chips, or sand, there's also no risk of small children ingesting it accidentally and possibly choking. Bonus? Artificial turf is much cheaper and looks much more natural than rubber!
One of the artificial grass's most important benefits is its added safety in play areas. Here are some ways in which artificial grass can help improve safety :

items: Soft Landing : Artificial grass provides a cushioned landing for children if they fall, which can help prevent injuries. An ideal ground cover reduces the impact of a fall by absorbing the shock. Based on those requirements, natural grass is not an appropriate ground cover for playgrounds. Instead, artificial turf covers all safety regulations without sacrificing the natural beauty of grass.

blocks.text: Likewise, kids can roll about and play on the synthetic turf without getting pieces of grass on their skin or becoming itchy.

items: No Pests : Artificial grass does not attract pests like natural grass does. This helps to reduce the risk of children being bitten or stung while playing.

No Chemicals: Artificial grass doesn't require the use of chemicals such as pesticides or fertilizers, which can be harmful to children. This creates a much safer environment for children to learn and play in.

Better for Allergy Sufferers: The pollen released into the air by grass can be allergic to some adults and children, causing conditions such as hay fever or allergic rhinitis. Artificial turf doesn't require mowing, so there will be less pollen for children to breathe in, reducing the effects on allergy sufferers.

blocks.text: Durability Benefits
Another key benefit of artificial grass is its durability . Here are some ways in which artificial grass can provide long-lasting benefits:

items: Withstands Heavy Use: Artificial grass can withstand heavy use from children without showing signs of wear and tear. This means that it will last longer than natural grass.

Low Maintenance : Artificial grass requires little to no maintenance, which can save time and money compared to natural grass. This can be great for institutions like schools or kindergartens that spend on gardeners, lawnmowers, sprinklers, etc.

blocks.text: Aesthetics Benefits
Artificial grass can also enhance the aesthetic appeal of playgrounds and children's play areas. Here are some ways in which artificial grass can improve the look of a play area:

items: Always Looks Green : Artificial grass always looks green and lush, regardless of the season. This helps create a more inviting and visually appealing play area. You can request a free sample of artificial grass from here .

Uniform Look: Artificial grass creates a uniform look, which can help make the play area more organized and put together. It also has the same color and texture as grass, connecting children to nature.
Customizable : Artificial grass can be cut to fit any space, which means that it can be customized to fit the unique needs of a particular play area.

blocks.text: Environmental Benefits

Finally, artificial grass offers many environmental benefits that can help make it a more sustainable option for playgrounds and children's play areas. Here are some ways in which artificial grass can benefit the environment:

items: Water Conservation : Artificial grass does not require watering, which can help to conserve water resources. Playground artificial grass uses fewer resources because it requires low maintenance. Irrigating the turf doesn't need water and always looks green and healthy!
Reduced Carbon Footprint: Artificial grass doesn't require mowing or other maintenance activities that produce carbon emissions, which makes it a more environmentally friendly option.

Reduces Waste: Artificial grass can be recycled at the end of its life, which helps to reduce waste and minimize environmental impact. It also saves on costs in the long term, which means more funds will be available for other environmental projects.

blocks.text: A Great Alternative To Sand, Dirt, and Grass

Many playgrounds feature a central sandpit or use sand in the surrounding areas. While sand can be fun for kids to play in, it may be challenging for parents: it's tough to clean up and unsafe for small children who may try to eat the sand. Another issue with natural grass playgrounds is the dirty stains on your children's clothes.

While real grass requires many maintenance hours, artificial turf fields require no watering, fertilizing, weeding, or mowing . This saves lots of time and money for playground owners, but also it saves costs for the city or community since they will have to spend less money on new grass and maintenance costs (staff, equipment, etc.)
Conclusion

There are many other popular playground materials (rubber mulch, engineered wood fibers, and pea gravel, to name a few). Still, artificial turf outshines all these options in both cost and practicality. It provides added safety, durability, aesthetic appeal, and environmental sustainability compared to natural grass.

If you are a parent, consider artificial turf installation for your child's next playground!
