posts.title: How to Reduce Wood Waste with Platinum Woods?
posts.h1: How to Reduce Wood Waste with Platinum Woods?

blocks.text: When it comes to construction or woodworking, efficient use of materials is essential for both cost savings and sustainability. Every unnecessary cut, leftover board, or inaccurate measurement leads to higher expenses and more environmental waste. If you want to reduce waste and make the most of your lumber, the first step is to stop guessing how much wood you need.

At Brazilian Lumber Los Angeles , we make it easy to plan smarter. With professional Takeoff Services , expert advice, and sustainable hardwoods from Platinum Woods , you can build efficiently, save money, and minimize waste.
Stop Guessing and Start Planning with Takeoff Services

The number one cause of wasted wood is inaccurate material estimation. Ordering too much lumber leads to piles of unused boards, while ordering too little causes costly delays. Both problems waste time, money, and resources.

Our Takeoff Service helps eliminate this issue entirely. By analyzing your project plans, we calculate the exact amount of material required. Whether you are building a large Ipe deck, a Cumaru pergola, or a Garapa fence, our experts can interpret blueprints and measurements to create a precise list of what you need.

This service ensures that you purchase only the right amount of wood, keeping your project on track and reducing leftover material. Accurate planning is one of the simplest and most effective ways to use wood efficiently.
No Plans? No Problem

Even if your project does not have full architectural drawings, Brazilian Lumber Los Angeles can still help. Our experienced sales team can estimate materials based on your project's dimensions and requirements.

Simply share the measurements of your space, and we will calculate the quantity of wood you need. This service is especially useful for smaller projects such as decks, fences, or siding. With our guidance, you can avoid excess cutting, leftover material, and unnecessary costs.
Whether your project is large or small, our goal is to make sure you have exactly what you need to build efficiently.
Choose the Right Board Lengths for Less Waste
Another overlooked factor in reducing waste is board length selection. Many people believe that longer boards are always better, but this is not always the case.

At Brazilian Lumber Los Angeles , we offer a wide range of board lengths, including shorter pieces known as "shorts." These shorter boards are often the perfect choice for smaller areas or segmented designs. They help you use every inch of your material more effectively and reduce the number of cuts you need to make.

Shorter boards also tend to be more affordable, making them a smart and sustainable option. By selecting the right combination of lengths for your project, you can greatly reduce waste and maximize efficiency.
Choose Quality and Sustainability with Platinum Woods

Efficient material use goes beyond good planning. It also depends on the quality of the wood itself. Low-quality or improperly sourced wood often leads to warping, cracking, or faster deterioration, which increases waste over time.

That is why Brazilian Lumber Los Angeles proudly offers hardwoods from Platinum Woods , a trusted name in quality and sustainability. Platinum Woods hardwoods are FSC-certified , meaning they come from responsibly managed forests with verified chain of custody. This certification ensures that your wood is both premium-grade and environmentally responsible.
When you choose Platinum Woods , you are not only building something strong and beautiful but also supporting sustainable forestry practices that protect natural ecosystems for future generations.
Premium Hardwoods Available at Brazilian Lumber Los Angeles

Brazilian Lumber Los Angeles offers an extensive selection of Platinum Woods hardwoods, each known for its durability, appearance, and resistance to the elements. Here are some of the top options to consider for your next project:
Ipe

Known as the "king of hardwoods," Ipe is one of the most durable and long-lasting woods available. It is naturally resistant to rot, decay, and insects, making it perfect for decking, docks, and outdoor structures. Its deep brown tones and fine grain give projects a sophisticated, timeless look.
Cumaru

Also called Brazilian Teak, Cumaru is dense and strong, with warm hues ranging from golden tan to reddish brown. It is an excellent choice for decks, pergolas, and outdoor furniture that must withstand heavy use and changing weather conditions.
Garapa

Garapa features a golden color that adds brightness and warmth to any project. It is lighter than Ipe or Cumaru but still very durable and weather resistant. Its natural glow makes it ideal for exterior siding or decks with a lighter aesthetic.
Jatoba

Often known as Brazilian Cherry, Jatoba has a rich, reddish color and exceptional hardness. It is a top choice for high-end flooring, furniture, and cabinetry. Its combination of strength and elegance adds a luxurious touch to any project.
Tigerwood

Tigerwood is famous for its bold grain patterns and rich contrast of light and dark tones. It is durable, visually striking, and naturally resistant to decay. It works beautifully for decks, accent walls, and flooring that needs to stand out.
Each of these hardwoods from Platinum Woods is selected for its beauty, longevity, and environmental responsibility, ensuring that every project you complete is both efficient and sustainable.
How to Reduce Waste with Better Planning
Minimizing waste requires the right combination of planning, materials, and professional support. Here are a few practical tips for getting started:

items: Use the Takeoff Service to determine exactly how much material your project requires.
Select the right board lengths to match your design and avoid excess cuts.
Consult with our experts to choose the best hardwood species for your climate and purpose.
Choose FSC-certified Platinum Woods to ensure sustainable and high-quality materials.
Buy everything in one order to reduce delivery trips and maintain material consistency.

blocks.text: These simple steps can save you time, reduce waste, and make your project more environmentally friendly.
Build Smarter with Brazilian Lumber Los Angeles

Building efficiently starts with smart planning and responsible material choices. At Brazilian Lumber Los Angeles , we are committed to helping you reduce waste and use every piece of wood effectively.

With Takeoff Services for accurate planning and Platinum Woods for sustainable, top-quality hardwoods such as Ipe , Cumaru , Garapa , Jatoba , and Tigerwood , we provide everything you need to complete your project successfully.
Visit our showroom or contact our team to learn more about how our Takeoff Service and hardwood selection can make your next project stronger, more efficient, and more sustainable.

Sustainably sourced hardwoods support responsible forestry, protect ecosystems, and provide fair economic opportunities for local communities. By choosing certified lumber, you help preserve forests while supporting ethical supply chains.

It is unfortunate that so much news focuses on illegal deforestation without reporting about legal and ethical practices of forestry management. People are often surprised to learn just how tightly regulated the industry is and how many compliance programs there are.
There are three pillars to responsible forestry management: sustainable harvest, ecosystem health, and community benefits.

items: It is important that the local population have economic opportunities and the forestry industry guarantees fair wages, medical attention, school staffing, and much more.
The flora and fauna in the managed area are all inventoried and evaluated by a forestry engineer.

Only a fraction of the area can be milled in one year, and the engineer picks non-viable, non-seed-bearing trees that are at the end of their life cycle. Removing such trees allows more light into the forest so newer trees can grow.
Once an area is harvested, it cannot be entered again for 25 years.
Each harvested tree has a tag and a ring print (like a thumb print) that is then compared to the log throughout the milling process.
All the milling is also monitored through plane and satellite imaging.

Ipe Lumber Technical Information
Ipe Lumber (pronounced ee-pay) is one of the densest hardwoods available for outdoor construction. It is very dense (in fact, it sinks in water) and is mildew and decay-resistant.

It's denseness and natural oils make it virtually impenetrable to insects (so insect deterioration is not an issue). Ipe does not scratch or splinter easily, does not become hot in the sun, and has a high friction coefficient, making it perfect for outdoor and seaside construction.

Cumaru Lumber Technical Information

Cumaru Lumber (pronounced Ku-mah-rue) also known as Brazilian Teak is one of the densest hardwoods available for outdoor construction, second only to Ipe. Cumaru does not scratch or splinter easily, does not become hot in the sun, and has a high friction coefficient, making it perfect for outdoor and seaside construction.

We have all the products you need if you are around South Carolina looking to build a deck, dock, pergola, boardwalk, or ceiling.

Ipe wood (pronounced e-pay but sometimes spelled Ipè or called Lapacho) is considered by many to be the most resistant wood in the world, more compact and longer-lasting than teak, with an estimated duration of 50 years without being affected by humidity and rain, sunshine, termites, mold or fungus.

We know that our clients from South Carolina are environmentally conscious and want to make informed and sustainable choices . For this reason, we offer certified tropical hardwood. There are several sustainable forestry methods to offer you responsible decking materials. Wood is a toxin-free product that will eventually disintegrate back into the earth, leaving no byproducts behind (although with ipe or Cumaru, that will take over 50 years).

It's denseness and natural oils make it virtually impenetrable to insects (so insect deterioration is not an issue). Ipe does not scratch or splinter easily, does not become hot in the sun, and has a high friction coefficient, making it perfect for outdoor and seaside construction.

Ipe Lumber Technical Information
Ipe Lumber (pronounced ee-pay) is one of the densest hardwoods available for outdoor construction. It is very dense (in fact, it sinks in water) and is mildew and decay-resistant.

It's denseness and natural oils make it virtually impenetrable to insects (so insect deterioration is not an issue). Ipe does not scratch or splinter easily, does not become hot in the sun, and has a high friction coefficient, making it perfect for outdoor and seaside construction.

Cumaru Lumber Technical Information

Cumaru Lumber (pronounced Ku-mah-rue) also known as Brazilian Teak is one of the densest hardwoods available for outdoor construction, second only to Ipe. It is very dense, which is why it is ideal for exterior use, as it is mildew and decay-resistant. It is often used for decking, flooring, railroad ties, as well as other purposes.
Cumaru does not scratch or splinter easily, does not become hot in the sun, and has a high friction coefficient, making it perfect for outdoor and seaside construction.

Ipe Lumber Technical Information
Ipe Lumber (pronounced ee-pay) is one of the densest hardwoods available for outdoor construction. It is very dense (in fact, it sinks in water) and is mildew and decay-resistant.

It's denseness and natural oils make it virtually impenetrable to insects (so insect deterioration is not an issue). Ipe does not scratch or splinter easily, does not become hot in the sun, and has a high friction coefficient, making it perfect for outdoor and seaside construction.

Cumaru Lumber Technical Information

Cumaru Lumber (pronounced Ku-mah-rue) also known as Brazilian Teak is one of the densest hardwoods available for outdoor construction, second only to Ipe. It is very dense, which is why it is ideal for exterior use, as it is mildew and decay-resistant. It is often used for decking, flooring, railroad ties, as well as other purposes.
Cumaru does not scratch or splinter easily, does not become hot in the sun, and has a high friction coefficient, making it perfect for outdoor and seaside construction.

Ipe Lumber Technical Information
Ipe Lumber (pronounced ee-pay) is one of the densest hardwoods available for outdoor construction. It is very dense (in fact, it sinks in water) and is mildew and decay-resistant.

It's denseness and natural oils make it virtually impenetrable to insects (so insect deterioration is not an issue). Ipe does not scratch or splinter easily, does not become hot in the sun, and has a high friction coefficient, making it perfect for outdoor and seaside construction.

Cumaru Lumber Technical Information

Cumaru Lumber (pronounced Ku-mah-rue) also known as Brazilian Teak is one of the densest hardwoods available for outdoor construction, second only to Ipe. It is very dense, which is why it is ideal for exterior use, as it is mildew and decay-resistant. It is often used for decking, flooring, railroad ties, as well as other purposes.
Cumaru does not scratch or splinter easily, does not become hot in the sun, and has a high friction coefficient, making it perfect for outdoor and seaside construction.

Jatoba Lumber is widely used for exterior carpentry thanks to its durability. Commonly referred to as Brazilian Cherry due to its similarity in color to domestic cherry, Jatoba is an incredibly strong wood. Aside from exterior use, Jatoba can also be installed as interior flooring, especially in high-foot traffic areas where a high coefficient of friction is desired.

Sustainable: The Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES) does not list Jatoba in its appendices. The Forest Legality Initiative also states that Jatoba can be exported and traded internationally.

The International Union for Conservation of Nature's Red List of Threatened Species (IUCN) does not list Jatoba as an endangered species. In fact, it is listed as the species of the least concern. Brazilian Lumber, LLC meets high standards for social, economic, and environmental responsibility.

pages.title: TROPICAL HARDWOODS SPECIFICATIONS

blocks.text: 
We Offer The Best Tropical Hardwoods At The Biggest Inventory in the US

Tropical hardwoods have natural oils that make them impenetrable to insects, as well as resistant to rot, mold, water, and weathering. In addition, they are non-toxic, strong, low-maintenance, and durable materials.

Plus, with tropical hardwoods there is always the factor of elegance, warmth, sophistication, and good taste that only wood can provide to your spaces. On top of that, we also offer decorative and functional elements such as artificial turf & ivy for amazing results.
With the experience and knowledge in the wood industry that we have here at Brazilian Lumber , let us share with you this important information about our stunning tropical hardwoods.
Tropical Hardwoods : IPE WOOD

Ipe (spelled ipe and pronounced "ee-pay"), also called Brazilian walnut, is a beautiful exotic wood from South America. These tropical hardwoods are used for decking and as decktiles, as well as for other outdoor applications. Ipe wood structures are hard, strong, and naturally resistant to rot, abrasion, and weathering as well as other tropical hardwoods. It is almost twice as dense as most woods and up to five times harder. It has a dark brown color, like a Mahogany, so it not only lasts a long time, but has the beauty of a fine interior wood. If Ipe lumber is allowed to age, color can be restored to its original tone with a good cleaning and the application of a suitable oil.
STOCK INFORMATION

items: GRADES: FAS/SEL
CUTS: Mixed Grain
DRYING: Kiln-Dried (KD)

blocks.text: SPECIES INFORMATION

items: OTHER NAMES: Brazilian Walnut, Lapacho, Pau Lope.
SCIENTIFIC NAME: Handroanthus spp. (formerly placed in the Tabebuia genus).
ORIGIN: Brazil, tropical South-America.
DENSITY: Janka scale hardness is 3684, making it extremely hard and durable.
WEIGHT: 71 lbs. / cu. ft., or approximately 5.9 lbs. per board foot.
DRYING: Ipe dries very well, with few cracks, twists or bows.
DURABILITY: Ipe can be used without preservatives or additional treatments. Ipe is expected to last 25+ years with little to no degradation from rot, decay, or termite infestation.

PRESERVATION: Ipe hardwood is extremely resistant to attack by decay, fungi and termites, but is not as resistant to marine borers. Due to its density, it is very resistant to preservative treatments.

FINISHING: If left unfinished, like any other natural wood, Ipe will turn gray. Due to Ipe's density, it is difficult for any finish treatment to penetrate the wood. Our recommendation is to use Ipe oil to maintain its natural color.

APPEARANCE: Hardwood ranges from olive brown to amber to near black, often with lighter and darker streaks, sharply demarcated from the whitish or yellowish sapwood. Texture is fine to medium, low luster, with a straight to irregular wide grain pattern.

blocks.text: Tropical Hardwoods: CUMARU WOOD

Cumaru wood is a dense hardwood from South America, mainly used for exterior decking and interior tropical hardwoods flooring. In some places it is known as Brazilian teak, golden teak or southern chestnut. Cumaru wood is often used as a less expensive hardwood alternative decking. These tropical hardwoods also come in dimensional lumber stock for use in heavy construction, railroad ties, and turnery. It is also extremely stiff, strong, and hard, making it suitable for a wide variety of applications.
STOCK INFORMATION

items: GRADES: FAS/SEL
CUTS: Mixed Grain
SIZES: 4/4, 4/4 RED, 5/4
DRYING: Kiln-Dried (KD)

blocks.text: SPECIES INFORMATION

items: OTHER NAMES: Brazilian Teak, Golden Teak, Southern Chestnut.
ORIGIN: Brazil, Equatorial South America.
DENSITY: Janka scale hardness is 3,540 for dry material.
WEIGHT: 62 - 81 lbs. / cu. ft., or approximately 5.2 - 6.75 lbs. per board foot.
DRYING: The wood is graded as easy to aerate, with a slight tendency to deformation and moderate warping. Drying is uniformly fast.
DURABILITY: This hardwood has excellent durability and is resistant to termite attack.
PRESERVATION: It is rated as resistant to preservative treatments, sapwood is permeable.
FINISHING: Finishes well.

WORKABILITY: The wood is difficult to saw and drill; where severely interlocked grain is not present, the wood is planed to a smooth surface. Due to its high density and oily nature, the wood sticks poorly.

APPEARANCE: It has a reddish brown or purplish brown color with light yellowish-brown or purplish streaks. Upon exposure, it gradually becomes uniform light-brown or yellowish brown. Sapwood distinct, narrow, yellowish brown. Rather low to medium luster; fine texture with interlocked grain.

blocks.text: Tropical Hardwoods: JATOBA WOOD

Jatoba lumber is better known as "Brazilian Cherry" in the hardwood flooring industry. These tropical hardwoods are also used for other applications where good impact resistance is needed, steam-bent parts, flooring, turnery, furniture, and cabinet work, railroad cross-ties tree-nails, gear cogs, wheel rims, and other specialty items. Jatoba wood is exceptionally stiff, strong, and hard, which is a great value for woodworkers looking for high-strength, low-cost wood tropical hardwoods.
STOCK INFORMATION

items: GRADES: FAS/SEL
CUTS: Mixed Grain
DRYING: Kiln-Dried (KD)

blocks.text: SPECIES INFORMATION

items: OTHER NAMES: Brazilian Cherry.
ORIGIN: Brazil, Peru.
DENSITY: Janka scale hardness ranges from 2,350 to 3,290, for dry material.
WEIGHT: 52 - 61 lbs. / cu. ft., or approximately 4.3 - 5.1 lbs. per board foot.
DRYING: The wood has a slight difficulty drying in the open air. It ages at a fast to moderate rate, with only slight cracking and warping.
DURABILITY: Very resistant to brown and white rot fungi. It is also classified as very resistant to dry-wood termites, yet little resistance to marine borers.
PRESERVATION: It cannot be treated with open tank or pressurized vacuum systems. The sapwood, however, responds.
FINISHING: Finishes well.

WORKABILITY: Jatoba wood is moderately difficult to saw and machine, largely due to its high density, but except in planing it can be machined to a smooth surface. The wood is somewhat difficult to plane because of the interlocked grain. It is easy to glue and has a satisfactory finish; its steam bending properties are comparable to those of White Oak.

APPEARANCE: It is salmon red to orange brown when fresh, becoming russet to reddish brown when cured. It is often marked with dark streaks. Sapwood is usually broad, white, gray, or pinkish. The texture is medium to rather coarse; the grain is mostly interlocked with a golden luster.

blocks.text: Tropical Hardwoods: GARAPA WOOD

Garapa is a South American wood with a yellow to brown color. These tropical hardwoods have a medium luster, an interlocked grain, and a fine texture that accentuates the rich golden and brown tones of the wood. The tropical hardwoods are also rated with a solid Janka hardness rating of 1,700, about 25% harder than Red Oak. Graded as durable and resistant to fungus and insects, Garapa exterior decking is an attractive and versatile option that is as resilient as it is beautiful.
TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS

items: Rot resistant.
Annual sealing is not necessary to obtain a natural patina.
No chemical treatments.

blocks.text: Tropical Hardwoods: TIGER WOOD

Tigerwood is unlike any other Brazilian tropical hardwoods, with its reddish brown color and dark stripes that resemble those of a tiger. It inspires and transforms any outdoor living space while adding a unique touch to decks and other products. When you build a deck with Tigerwood, you get a low maintenance surface that does not require chemical treatments like other decking materials. In fact, with sun exposure over time, the rich, deep colors of the wood become even more enhanced. We do recommend using a deck oil twice a year for the first few years, and every two years thereafter to keep your deck looking new. This durable, exotic wood is the third hardest of the Brazilian tropical hardwoods and naturally resistant to rot and decay, with a lifespan of more than 50 years.

pages.title: Calculator

blocks.text: Work out how much decking you need before you ask for a price. The number that matters is coverage, not board count, because board width and gap change the answer more than anything else.
How to calculate decking

items: Measure the deck area in square feet: length times width, plus any bump-outs.
Add 10% for a straight, perpendicular layout. Add 15% for a diagonal layout, and 20% for herringbone or a picture frame border.
Divide by the coverage of the board you chose. A 5/4x6 covers about 0.48 square feet per linear foot once you allow a 3/16 inch gap; a 1x4 covers about 0.31.
Order the substructure separately: joists at 16 inches on center, plus blocking at every board joint.

blocks.text: Wednesday, October 5th 2022, 2:23 PM EDT
Brazilian Lumber offers a vast tropical hardwood collection for decking and outdoor projects.

Following the tagline "Premium decking built the right way," Brazilian Lumber is paving the way for efficient, sustainable, and high-quality hardwood decking for homes across the US. It boasts the most extensive inventory of tropical hardwood and decking materials in the country, bridging the market gap for limited options currently available in the market.

Brazilian Lumber's specialty product is Ipe or ironwood, the toughest tropical hardwood in the world. Compared to commercial wood used in decking, Ipe is dense, weather-resistant, and offers fire-retardant characteristics comparable to steel and concrete. Ipe has naturally occurring oils that protect it from corrosion, splintering, mold, mildew, and even insect infestation. This hardwood can last up to 30 to 50 years without chemical treatment - a far cry from the 5-year lifespan of commercial wood decking.

Besides Ipe, Brazilian Lumber also offers a collection of premium tropical hardwoods, called the Platinum Woods, that provide the same hardiness and benefits as Ipe. What is Composite Decking?

Composite decking is a modern and highly durable alternative to traditional wood decking. It's an innovative blend of 95% recycled wood and plastic film that provides a wide range of benefits not available with traditional wood. This impressive material doesn't only give your deck an appealing aesthetic but also offers longevity, sturdiness, and minimal maintenance.

Deckotech

Deckotech delivers bold, high-performance solutions in decking, cladding, and fencing, offering both composite and aluminum lines designed for today's most visionary spaces. Whether you're designing a sleek façade, a low-maintenance fence, or an enduring deck, Deckotech empowers you to create with confidence and clarity - uniting innovation, sustainability, and signature design in every detail.
Timbertech Composite Decking

Renowned for its high-quality composite decking, Timbertech provides a low-maintenance, high-performance alternative to traditional wood decking. Timbertech decking is engineered for maximum toughness, offering superior resistance to fading, staining, scratching, and mold. With a range of colors and finishes that mimic the natural beauty of wood, Timbertech decking brings your outdoor living space to life.
Trex Composite Decking

As a pioneer in the composite decking industry, Trex offers some of the most innovative and sustainable outdoor living solutions available. Made from an eco-friendly blend of 95% reclaimed wood and plastic film, Trex composite decking offers a wood-like look without the need for regular maintenance.
Fiberon Composite Decking

Fiberon is a popular choice for homeowners seeking both style and durability. Known for its high-definition grain patterns and rich, multi-chromatic colors, Fiberon composite decking offers the warmth and charm of natural hardwoods without the ongoing maintenance.
Composite Decking vs Wood
When contemplating composite decking vs. wood, the former undoubtedly has numerous advantages. While traditional wood
decks can warp, crack, and host mold or mildew, composite decking boards are designed to withstand these common issues.

Composite wood decking is resistant to fading, staining, scratching, and mold - it's an excellent choice for homeowners seeking durability and low-maintenance options. Unlike wood, it doesn't need to be stained or sealed annually, making it a time and cost-efficient choice.

Frequently Asked Questions

items: What are wood wall panels?

blocks.text: Wood wall panels are decorative elements made from various types of wood that are used to cover walls and generate a sophisticated touch of elegance in the space/ They offer both aesthetic appeal and functional benefits, such as insulation and soundproofing. These wall panels can be made from hardwoods or softwoods such as Ipe, Garapa, Cumaru, Tigerwood, Jatoba, Sapele, Oak, Walnut, thermally modified ayous, thermally modified ash, thermally modified pine and many more.

items: What types of wood wall panels do you offer?

blocks.text: We offer a wide range of wood wall panels, including hardwood panels, thermally modified wood panels, softwood panels. These wall panels can be made from hardwoods or softwoods such as Ipe, Garapa, Cumaru, Tigerwood, Jatoba, Sapele, Oak, Walnut, thermally modified ayous, thermally modified ash, thermally modified pine and many more.

items: How do I install wood wall panels?

blocks.text: Installing wood wall panels typically involves securing them to the wall using nails or screws, depending on the panel type and application method. Our experts are always available to recommend which type of installation method is the most appropriate for each panel.

items: Are wood wall panels suitable for all rooms?

blocks.text: Yes, wood wall panels can improve the aesthetic appeal of any room, including living rooms, bedrooms, kitchens, offices, and commercial spaces. However, it's essential to consider factors such as humidity levels and exposure to moisture when selecting panels for specific areas like bathrooms or kitchens.

items: Can wood wall panels be customized?

blocks.text: Yes, we offer customization options to meet your specific design preferences and project requirements. Whether you need custom sizes, finishes, or patterns, our team can work with you to create personalized wood wall panels that complement your space perfectly. At Brazilian Lumber we have our own milling machine which means that we can mill any profile or pattern that you or your architect need!

items: How do I maintain wood wall panels?

blocks.text: Maintaining wood wall panels is relatively simple. Regular dusting with a soft cloth or vacuum cleaner attachment helps keep the panels clean. Additionally, if your wall panel is exposed to the sun or rain maybe once or twice a year maintenance will be necessary.

items: Are wood wall panels eco-friendly?

blocks.text: Yes, we are direct importers of sustainably sourced, premium grade tropical hardwoods which means that our wood wall panels are sourced from sustainable forestry practices and adhere to environmental standards. We prioritize eco-friendly manufacturing processes and materials to minimize our carbon footprint and promote sustainability.

items: Can wood wall panels help improve insulation and acoustics?

blocks.text: Yes, wood wall panels provide additional insulation to rooms by creating a barrier between the interior and exterior walls. Additionally, the natural density of wood helps absorb sound, making wood wall panels an excellent choice for improving acoustics in residential and commercial spaces. The denser the type of wood you choose, the better sound insulation you will get.

items: Do you offer samples of wood wall panels?

blocks.text: Yes, we provide samples of our wood wall panels to help you visualize how they will look and feel in your space before making a purchase. Simply contact us to request samples, and we'll be happy to assist you. How do I clean composite wall panels?
Regular cleaning with a mild detergent and water solution is usually sufficient to remove dirt and grime.For tougher stains, you can use a soft brush or sponge.
Avoid using abrasive cleaners or pressure washers, as they can damage the surface of the panels

items: Can composite wall panels be used outdoors?

blocks.text: Yes, many composite wall panels are suitable for outdoor use. However, it's essential to choose panels specifically designed for exterior applications and follow the manufacturer's recommendations for installation and maintenance.

items: Can composite wall panels be recycled?

blocks.text: Many composite wall panels are made from recycled materials and can be recycled themselves at the end of their lifespan, contributing to sustainability efforts. However, recycling options may vary depending on local facilities and regulations.

items: What are the colors of Deckotech wall panels?

blocks.text: Our Serenity and Harmony collections offer a delightful array of colors and dimensions,providing a wide spectrum of options to satisfy
different preferences and architectural needs. We have available these colors: teak, ashwood, walnut and dark grey.

items: How do composite wall panels compare to traditional materials like wood or metal?

blocks.text: Composite wall panels often outperform traditional materials in terms of durability, longevity, and resistance to environmental factors such as moisture, insects, and rot. They may also offer greater design flexibility and ease of installation.

items: Are composite wall panels eco-friendly?

blocks.text: DeckoTech composite wall panels are manufactured using recycled materials, making them environmentally sustainable choices for construction projects. Additionally, their durability and low maintenance requirements contribute to long-term sustainability by reducing the need for frequent replacements and repairs.

items: Can DeckoTech composite wall panels be customized to fit specific project requirements?

blocks.text: Yes, composite wall panels are highly customizable and can be tailored to meet various design specifications, including size, shape, color, and texture. This flexibility allows architects and designers to achieve their desired aesthetic and functional goals.

items: How do you install composite wall panels?

blocks.text: DeckoTech wall panels are easy to install; all boards come tongue and grooved, making them very easy to assemble. The installation method involves screws. They can be secured directly to a plywood wall. If the wall is not plywood or drywall, then some PT frames or aluminum frames may be added to the wall first, and then the panels can be screwed directly to the frames.

items: Are composite wall panels suitable for exterior applications?

blocks.text: Yes, DeckoTech composite wall panels are designed for exterior use and offer excellent resistance to weathering, UV exposure, and temperature fluctuations. They can be used for cladding, facades, and other exterior architectural elements, providing both aesthetic appeal and structural integrity.

items: How do you maintain composite wall panels?

blocks.text: Composite wall panels typically require minimal maintenance compared to traditional materials. Regular cleaning with mild soap and water is usually sufficient to remove dirt and debris. Avoid harsh chemicals or abrasive cleaners that could damage the panel's surface.

items: What is PVC grid cladding?

blocks.text: PVC grid cladding is a type of wall covering made from polyvinyl chloride (PVC) material. It consists of interlocking grid panels that are installed on walls to enhance aesthetics and provide protection.

items: What are the benefits of using PVC grid cladding?
Durability: PVC is a durable material that is resistant to moisture, mold, and mildew, making it suitable for use in damp environments.
Easy Installation: PVC grid cladding typically comes in interlocking panels, making it easy to install without the need for specialized tools or skills.
Low Maintenance: PVC cladding is easy to clean and requires minimal or no maintenance over time.
Versatility: PVC grid cladding is available in a beautiful Ipe color same as the real Ipe hardwood.
Cost-Effectiveness: PVC cladding is often more affordable than other materials such as wood or metal, making it a cost-effective option for wall covering.

Characteristics Of Cypress Wood

Cypress wood is renowned for its striking beauty and impressive durability, making it a favorite among woodworkers and homeowners alike. Known for its natural preservative oil, Cypress wood offers exceptional resistance to moisture, decay, and insect damage. Its fine grain and uniform texture not only enhance its aesthetic appeal but also contribute to its smooth finish and stability. With its warm, light honey tones, Cypress wood weathers gracefully to a soft gray when left untreated, adding a rustic charm to any setting. This wood's density and strength make it a versatile choice for both interior and exterior applications.
Uses Of Cypress Wood

Cypress wood's versatility and resilience make it ideal for a wide range of applications. Popularly used in building construction, it is a top choice for structural timbers, siding, and roofing. Its resistance to moisture and rot also makes it perfect for outdoor uses such as decking, landscaping, and garden structures like pergolas and arbors. In interior design, Cypress is often seen in flooring, paneling, and cabinetry, where its distinct color and grain add elegance and warmth. Beyond its structural uses, Cypress is also favored for crafting durable and beautiful outdoor furniture, doors, and even boats.
Installation Guide (DIY Vs Professional)
DIY Installation
For those who prefer a hands-on approach, DIY installation of Cypress wood can be a rewarding project. Here are key steps to ensure a successful installation:
Preparation: Ensure that Cypress wood is properly acclimated to your local environment to minimize expansion or contraction post-installation.
Tools: You will need basic woodworking tools, including a saw, drill, and sandpaper.
Cutting and Assembly: Measure twice and cut once to ensure precision. Use galvanized or stainless steel screws and nails to prevent corrosion.
Finishing: Although Cypress weathers beautifully, a finish can enhance its color and protect it from the elements. Use a high-quality wood sealant suited for Cypress.
Hiring a Professional
For large projects or installations requiring precise craftsmanship, hiring a professional is advisable. Professionals bring:
Expertise: Extensive knowledge of Cypress wood properties.
Precision: High-quality tools and techniques to maximize the wood's beauty and lifespan.
Efficiency: Faster completion with attention to detail.
Peace of Mind: Assurance that your installation adheres to local building codes and standards.

Our Cypress wood is of premium quality, carefully selected to ensure consistent texture and color. It undergoes rigorous quality checks to meet the high standards our customers expect from Brazilian Lumber. Cypress is a type of softwood, but it is known for its durability and resistance, which makes it comparable to many hardwoods in terms of longevity and robustness. What is

Accoya Wood?

Accoya modified wood has become the timber industry benchmark for performance and sustainability. No other timber offers the same combination of durability, stability, and versatility. Sustainably sourced , and with a low total lifetime carbon cost, Accoya actively contributes to a circular, bio-based economy and is one of the few truly sustainable building materials.

Accoya wood is produced in both Kingsport, USA, and Arnhem, The Netherlands. This video includes an exclusive look behind the scenes at our Arnhem production site. This guided video tour shows how we turn fast-growing, sustainable woods into an ultra-high-performance building material.
Wood Siding
Brilliance for generations to come

Your exterior wood siding needs to weather any storm, in style. We know that aesthetics, low maintenance and durability are crucial. What you may not know is that Accoya out-performs even the most durable tropical hardwood siding.

By combining superior stability and durability with the beauty of natural wood, you can achieve the look and the performance you want from your timber siding. Not to mention Accoya's world-leading sustainability credentials.
To specify Accoya siding in your next project, head to our Architect Zone to learn more.
Accoya wood has an industry-leading warranty, giving you peace of mind and complete confidence for your beautiful Accoya siding.

Stay true to your vision with a range of finishes, including Shou Sugi Ban and custom board sizes and fixings. Left untreated, your exterior wood siding will weather naturally. But if you'd prefer to coat it, Accoya siding makes the ultimate surface.
Resistant to rotting, Accoya siding is likely to stay free of any visible distortion over its lifetime. A cost-effective choice for lasting performance.

Now you can meet the most demanding of planning requirements. Accoya wood siding is 100% non toxic and contains no biocides or harmful chemicals. Each siding panel is made from ® certified timber that's fully sustainable.
Color Grey Decking
Enhanced wood. Advanced Performance.
Durable decking that delivers
A stylish grey deck can enhance any home, bringing the outdoors inside. But being outdoors, your deck needs to withstand the elements and stay looking as fresh as the day it was built.

There's a lot of choice when it comes to choosing a decking material and sadly most materials do not live up to the high standards you might expect. Accoya Color Grey is an ultra-high performance decking product that combines the beauty and benefits of 100% real wood, but without the drawbacks. Colored through completely from surface to core, the gorgeous Color Grey delivers a premium look and a deck that lasts.
Accoya Color is colored through to the core, requiring less maintenance. Save time and money by choosing Accoya for your deck.
Your Color Grey deck will last for years to come due to the minimal movement of the Accoya wood, keeping your deck boards in place like the day they were installed.
25 year* residential warranty, giving you peace of mind that your decking is a worthwhile investment. 10 year warranty for Commercial Applications and residential use in the state of Florida.

Tropical Hardwood , Ipe Wood

Ipe (pronounced ee-pay) is one of the densest hardwoods available for outdoor construction. Ipe 1x4 is very dense (in fact it sinks in water), it has the same fire rating as concrete and steel, and it is mildew and decay resistant. Its denseness and natural oils make it virtually impenetrable to insects (so insect deterioration is not an issue). Ipe 1x4 does not scratch or splinter easily, it does not become hot in the sun, and has a high friction coefficient, making it perfect for outdoor and seaside construction.

This promotion is available exclusively to Brazilian Lumber Exterior Wood Solutions customers who have received this offer through official company channels.
The promotion consists of a $500 (five hundred dollars) credit to be applied toward a future purchase made with Brazilian Lumber.
The $500 credit is valid only on purchases with a minimum order value of $1,500 (one thousand five hundred dollars).
The credit may be redeemed once per customer.
The promotional credit is non-transferable, non-refundable, and may not be redeemed for cash.
The promotional credit is valid through May 31, 2026. After this date, the credit will automatically expire and cannot be extended.
This promotion cannot be combined with other discounts, offers, or promotions.
The credit is not valid for purchases made prior to receipt of this offer.
Brazilian Lumber reserves the right to verify order eligibility before applying the promotional credit.

Brazilian Lumber Exterior Wood Solutions reserves the right to modify, suspend, or terminate this promotion at any time, with or without prior notice, while honoring credits already applied in accordance with these Terms & Conditions.
Participation in this promotion constitutes full and unconditional acceptance of these Terms & Conditions.

items: Overview

blocks.text: The Early Black Friday Campaign ("Promotion") is organized by Brazilian Lumber, LLC ("the Company"). items: Promotional Period

blocks.text: This Promotion is valid from November 10, 2025, through November 30, 2025 ("Promotion Period").

items: All orders must be placed, confirmed, and invoiced within the promotional period.
No extensions, retroactive discounts, or adjustments will be granted after the promotion expires.
Cannot be combined with any other promotional offer.
Eligibility

The Promotion is available to all customers purchasing directly from Brazilian Lumber during the Promotion Period, either in person at any physical location or by phone order. Orders can be shipped anywhere within the United States and the Caribbean, but purchases cannot be completed online.
The 10% contractor discount and price-beating offer are for trade professionals, including builders, contractors, architects, designers, and installers.
The Promotion is valid across all Brazilian Lumber locations in the U.S.
Offer Details

blocks.text: A 10% discount will be applied to the total eligible materials purchased by qualifying trade professionals at the time of purchase or invoicing. This discount applies only to the product subtotal before taxes and shipping and does not apply to milling.
Brazilian Lumber will beat any competitor's pricing on equivalent qualifying items when a current written quote from an authorized U.S. retailer or distributor is provided.

items: The competitor quote must be dated within the promotional period.
The quoted product must be identical in species, grade, dimensions, and finish.
The quote must include the competitor's company details, product information, and contact information for verification.

blocks.text: Technical information provided by The Wood Database :
Durability: Durable - class 2 Strength class: Unknown
Applications: Angelim Pedra wood is used for various applications: Interior: carpentry, window framing doors and stairs Exterior: window framing, doors, cladding, parkbenches and decking.
Mass volume: 950-1200 kg/m3. at 12% moisture level 650-850 kg/m3.
Colour: The colour of the Angelim Pedra heartwood is fresh sawn orange yellow brown, darkening to (dark) brown.
Details: The timber has fresh sawn a typical smell which disappears with time. The lighter sapwood is easy to distinguish.
Grain: The grain is straight to irregular and sometimes interlocked.
Texture: The wood has a remarkable stripy pattern. Irregular darker spots can be seen (mineral spots). The texture is coarse.
Drying: Angelim pedra wood dries slowly, with little deformation. When drying too fast or carelessly there is a risk of deformation and cracks.
Screwing/nailing: Pre-drilling recommended with Angelim Pedra wood
Finishing surface: With gluing and finishing are many positive experiences
Botanical name: Hymenolobium excelsum Ducke
Origin area: Brazil, Surinam, Guyana

Other names: Angelin, angelim, sapupira amarela, sapupira amarella, angelim do para, angelim da mata, angelim pedra, angelim da terra, caramate, murarena (Brazil), Saint Martin gris (French Guyana), makkakabbes (Surinam).

Remarks: FSC Angelim Pedra wood is available in large quantities in the Amazon region of Brazil. The large trees reach up to about 45 m, with diameters up to 120 cm. The straight and cylindric clear trunk is about 20 m long. Recent research proves that the differences between wood from the different sources are very small, with no impact on the relevant wood properties.
Family: Leguminosae (Mimosaceae)
Machining: Take care that with painting the pores are filled.

blocks.text: Ipe Lumber Technical Information
Ipe Lumber (pronounced ee-pay) is one of the densest hardwoods available for outdoor construction. It is very dense (in fact, it sinks in water) and is mildew and decay-resistant.

It's denseness and natural oils make it virtually impenetrable to insects (so insect deterioration is not an issue). Ipe does not scratch or splinter easily, does not become hot in the sun, and has a high friction coefficient, making it perfect for outdoor and seaside construction.

Cumaru Lumber (pronounced Ku-mah-rue) also known as Brazilian Teak is one of the densest hardwoods available for outdoor construction, second only to Ipe. It is very dense, which is why it is ideal for exterior use, as it is mildew and decay-resistant. It is often used for decking, flooring, railroad ties, as well as other purposes. pages.title: Frecuently Ask Questions

blocks.text: What type of wood do you carry?

We carry a full range of premium outdoor building materials, including tropical hardwoods, thermally modified woods, and low-maintenance alternatives such as composite, PVC, and aluminum systems. Our New Jersey warehouse services the Northeast and also ships nationwide across the U.S.
What type of hardwoods do you carry?
We offer Ipe, Cumaru, Garapa, Jatoba, Tigerwood and Massaranduba, dense, durable hardwoods known for their exceptional strength, rich color, and long-term performance outdoors.
What brands of composite decking do you carry?

We proudly supply leading composite and PVC decking brands including TimberTech, Azek, Trex, Deckotech, MoistureShield, Fiberon, Deckorators, Zuri, and Versatex. These low-maintenance materials offer long-lasting durability and modern design flexibility.
Do you carry non-wood alternatives?
Yes. In addition to hardwoods, we stock composite decking, PVC decking, thermally modified woods, and aluminum systems designed for exterior projects.
What makes Ipe special?

Ipe, also known as Brazilian Walnut, is one of the hardest and densest woods in the world. It naturally resists rot, insects, and extreme weather. It carries a Class A fire rating (the same as concrete and steel), resists surface scratches, and stays cooler due to its heat-repelling properties.
What makes Cumaru special?
Cumaru, or Brazilian Teak, is a strong, durable hardwood with warm golden-brown tones. It offers excellent outdoor performance and is a more affordable alternative to Ipe.
What is tropical hardwood?

Tropical hardwoods are dense species sourced from South America, Africa, and Asia. They offer natural resistance to pests, decay, and heavy wear, making them ideal for decking, fencing, and exterior structures.
What are the benefits of using tropical hardwood?
Tropical hardwoods last significantly longer than softwood or synthetic alternatives, require minimal maintenance, and provide natural beauty with rich variations in grain and color.
Can tropical hardwood be refinished?
Yes. These woods can be sanded and refinished to restore their original tone, making them long-lasting, premium options for outdoor builds.
How much hardwood will I need?
Your needs depend on project size and board width. Hardwood decking is sold by the linear foot. Use this formula:

items:
Calculate square footage (L x W).
2. Select board width and gap (¼" or T&G).
3. Multiply by the correct factor (see below).
4" boards → 3.43
6" boards → 2.20
4" boards → 3.84
6" boards → 2.34

blocks.text: Always add 5-10% extra for waste. Our New Jersey sales team can calculate exact quantities for you.
Do you offer cutting or milling services?
Yes. We provide select custom milling and profiling upon request. Contact the New Jersey warehouse for availability.
Do you accept returns?
Yes, within 15 days of the invoice date.

items: A 25% restocking fee applies to processed orders.
Special orders cannot be returned or refunded.
Adhesive products (glue, oils, adhesives) are not returnable.

blocks.text: Contact our NJ team for assistance with any return.
Do you ship from New Jersey to other states?
Yes. Although we serve New Jersey, New York, and Pennsylvania locally, we also ship from our New Jersey warehouse to customers anywhere in the United States.
Do you offer same-day pickup?
Yes. Many materials are stocked at the New Jersey warehouse and available for same-day pickup when ordered in advance.
How much does shipping cost?
Shipping costs depend on order size, weight, and destination. We work with multiple carriers to secure competitive rates and provide quotes upfront.
Can the carrier deliver directly to my jobsite?
Yes. Most freight companies can deliver to homes, warehouses, or jobsites as long as the area is accessible for a delivery truck.
How do I track my order?
